daas-irab:56-59.t: ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an. ﴿نَفْسٌ﴾ fāʿil (agent); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from an and the verb is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿يا﴾ the vocative particle. ﴿حَسْرَتى﴾ a munādā (the one addressed) annexed to the yāʾ of the first person, which has turned into an alif. ﴿عَلى﴾ a preposition. ﴿ما﴾ maṣdariyya; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of genitive by ʿalā, and the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to حسرتا. ﴿فَرَّطْتُ﴾ a past verb and its agent. ﴿فِي جَنْبِ﴾ the two are attached to فرطت. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ the wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and in is lightened (mukhaffafa) and inoperative (muhmala). ﴿كُنْتُ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿لَمِنَ السَّاخِرِينَ﴾ the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa), and a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَقُولَ﴾ an imperfect verb conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional. ﴿أَنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ anna, and the Name of Majesty is its noun. ﴿هَدانِي﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿لَكُنْتُ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to law, and kāna and its noun; the clause هداني is the khabar of anna, and anna with what follows it is interpreted as a maṣdar that is the agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being "ثبت" (it were established); the implied clause has no grammatical position. ﴿مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of كنت; the clause كنت is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَقُولَ﴾ an imperfect verb, its agent latent (mustatir). ﴿حِينَ﴾ an adverb of time; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَرَى﴾ an imperfect verb, its agent latent. ﴿الْعَذابَ﴾ its object; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لَوْ﴾ conditional, non-jussive. ﴿أَنَّ﴾ a particle resembling the verb. ﴿لِي﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿كَرَّةً﴾ its postponed noun; anna and what follows it are interpreted as a maṣdar in the position of nominative as the agent of an omitted verb. ﴿فَأَكُونَ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied an, and its noun is a latent pronoun. ﴿مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of أكون; the interpreted maṣdar is conjoined to كرة. ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer. ﴿قَدْ﴾ a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿جاءَتْكَ﴾ a past verb and its object. ﴿آياتِي﴾ its agent; the clause is initial. ﴿فَكَذَّبْتَ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its agent. ﴿بِها﴾ the two are attached to كذبت. ﴿وَاسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾ conjoined to كذبت. ﴿وَكُنْتَ﴾ kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar of كنت; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:60-64.t:
﴿وَيَوْمَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and يوم is an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿تَرَى﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive. ﴿كَذَبُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to كذبوا. ﴿وُجُوهُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ its i'rab preceded in ayah 32.
﴿وَيُنَجِّي﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its agent. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its object. ﴿اتَّقَوْا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ the two are attached to ينجي. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَمَسُّهُمُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object. ﴿السُّوءُ﴾ agent. ﴿وَلا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction and lā is negative. ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحْزَنُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its agent; the clause is the khabar of هم, the nominal clause is conjoined to what precedes it, and the clause لا يمسهم is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهُ خالِقُ﴾ the Name of Majesty is mubtadaʾ and خالق is khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿كُلِّ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ a second muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and هو is mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ the two are attached to وكيل. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكِيلٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, a fronted khabar. ﴿مَقالِيدُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and agent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِآياتِ﴾ the two are attached to كفروا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْخاسِرُونَ﴾ khabar, nominative.

daas-irab:65-67.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ﴾ a particle of oath and a preposition; the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and qad is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿أُوحِيَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿إِلَيْكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun standing in place of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ conjoined to إليك. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِكَ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ the lām prepares for the oath (al-lām al-muwaṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and in is conditional. ﴿أَشْرَكْتَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿لَيَحْبَطَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis. ﴿عَمَلُكَ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿وَلَتَكُونَنَّ﴾ a conjunction; the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, its noun latent (mustatir). ﴿مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, the khabar (predicate) of تكونن; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the response to the oath indicates it. ﴿بَلِ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb. ﴿فَاعْبُدْ﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of the implied condition), and an imperative verb, its agent latent. ﴿وَكُنْ﴾ an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperative verb, its noun latent. ﴿مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, its khabar; the clause اعبد is the apodosis of an implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle and mā is negative. ﴿قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ a past verb and its agent, and the Name of Majesty is its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿حَقَّ﴾ a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) (nāʾib mafʿūl muṭlaq). ﴿قَدْرِهِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالْأَرْضُ﴾ the wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl. ﴿قَبْضَتُهُ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالسَّماواتُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَطْوِيَّاتٌ﴾ khabar. ﴿بِيَمِينِهِ﴾ the two are attached to مطويات; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿سُبْحانَهُ﴾ a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb. ﴿وَتَعالى﴾ a past verb, its agent latent, and the wāw is a conjunction. ﴿عَمَّا﴾ the two are attached to تعالى. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its agent; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause تعالى is conjoined to what precedes it, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:68-70.t: ﴿وَنُفِخَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and a passive past verb with a latent nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb. ﴿فَصَعِقَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿مَنْ﴾ a relative noun, fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception. ﴿مَنْ﴾ excepted. ﴿شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its agent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿نُفِخَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿فِيهِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿أُخْرى﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿فَإِذا﴾ a conjunction, and إذا of surprise (fujāʾiyya). ﴿هُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿قِيامٌ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿يَنْظُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its agent; the clause is a second khabar. ﴿وَأَشْرَقَتِ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿الْأَرْضُ﴾ its agent. ﴿بِنُورِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿رَبِّها﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَوُضِعَ الْكِتابُ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb and nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَجِيءَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿بِالنَّبِيِّينَ﴾ the two are attached to the verb; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَالشُّهَداءِ﴾ conjoined to النبيين. ﴿وَقُضِيَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb of place attached to قضي. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾ the wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and a mubtadaʾ. ﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يُظْلَمُونَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَوُفِّيَتْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿كُلُّ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿نَفْسٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿عَمِلَتْ﴾ a past verb, its agent latent; the clause is the ṣila of ما. ﴿وَهُوَ﴾ the wāw is of the ḥāl, and the pronoun is mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَعْلَمُ﴾ its khabar; the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿بِما﴾ the two are attached to أعلم. ﴿يَفْعَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its agent; the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:71-72.t: ﴿وَسِيقَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿إِلى جَهَنَّمَ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to سيق. ﴿زُمَراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿حَتَّى﴾ inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial, non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿جاؤُها﴾ a past verb, its agent and its object; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿فُتِحَتْ﴾ a passive past verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَبْوابُها﴾ nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿خَزَنَتُها﴾ fāʿil. ﴿أَلَمْ﴾ a particle of affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī), and lam is a jussive particle. ﴿يَأْتِكُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the kāf is its object. ﴿رُسُلٌ﴾ fāʿil; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying). ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted naʿt (adjective) of رسل. ﴿يَتْلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its agent; the clause is a second adjective. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿آياتِ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبِّكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause قال is conjoined, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb, nominative; the wāw is its agent and the kāf its first object. ﴿لِقاءَ﴾ second object. ﴿يَوْمِكُمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هذا﴾ an adjective of يومكم; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its agent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَلى﴾ a particle of answer. ﴿وَلكِنْ﴾ a conjunction, and lākin is an inoperative particle of rectification (istidrāk). ﴿حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ﴾ a past verb and its agent. ﴿الْعَذابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ the two are attached to حقت; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿قِيلَ﴾ a passive past verb. ﴿ادْخُلُوا﴾ an imperative verb and its agent; the clause is in the position of nominative as nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿أَبْوابَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ. ﴿فِيها﴾ the two are attached to خالدين. ﴿فَبِئْسَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and an inflexible (jāmid) past verb for expressing blame. ﴿مَثْوَى﴾ its agent. ﴿الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause قيل is resumptive.

daas-irab:73-75.t: ﴿وَسِيقَ﴾ a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿اتَّقَوْا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿رَبَّهُمْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ﴾ the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to سيق. ﴿زُمَراً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause سيق is conjoined to what precedes it, and the clause اتقوا is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿حَتَّى﴾ inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverbial, non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿جاؤُها﴾ a past verb, its agent and its object; the clause is in the position of genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَفُتِحَتْ﴾ the wāw is the wāw of the ḥāl, and a passive past verb. ﴿أَبْوابُها﴾ nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. ﴿وَقالَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿خَزَنَتُها﴾ fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿سَلامٌ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ the two are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿طِبْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and agent; the two clauses, nominal and verbal, are the maqūl al-qawl (object of the verb of saying). ﴿فَادْخُلُوها﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ of the implied condition), and an imperative verb, its agent and its object. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾ ḥāl, accusative (manṣūb) by the yāʾ; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَقالُوا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its agent; the clause is conjoined to the apodosis. ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ its khabar; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a naʿt (adjective) of the Name of Majesty. ﴿صَدَقَنا﴾ a past verb and its first object, the agent latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَعْدَهُ﴾ its second object. ﴿وَأَوْرَثَنَا﴾ a conjunction, and a past verb and its first object. ﴿الْأَرْضَ﴾ its second object. ﴿نَتَبَوَّأُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its agent latent; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ the two are attached to the verb. ﴿حَيْثُ﴾ an adverb of place, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, in the position of accusative. ﴿نَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its agent latent. ﴿فَنِعْمَ﴾ a past verb for expressing praise. ﴿أَجْرُ﴾ fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ). ﴿الْعامِلِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَتَرَى الْمَلائِكَةَ حَافِّينَ﴾ a resumptive particle, and an imperfect verb and its object, the agent latent, and حافين is ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ حَوْلِ﴾ the two are attached to حافين. ﴿يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its agent; بحمد is attached to an omitted ḥāl and ربهم is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَقُضِيَ﴾ a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb attached to the verb. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾ the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَقِيلَ﴾ a conjunction, and a passive past verb. ﴿الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ﴾ a mubtadaʾ, and the Name of Majesty is genitive by the lām, the two attached to an omitted khabar; the clause is nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ﴾ badal (substitute), and العالمين is muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the yāʾ because it is treated as a sound masculine plural (mulḥaq bi-jamʿ al-mudhakkar al-sālim); the clause is the object of saying.

farraa:1-1.t: His words: ﴿تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ﴾: You make ﴿تنزيل﴾ nominative by implying "this is a revelation", as He said: ﴿سُورَةٌ أَنْزلْنَاهَا﴾, whose meaning is: "this is a sūra which We have sent down". And if you wish, you may make it nominative by min, the meaning being: "from Allah is the revelation of the Book". Had you made it accusative, while commanding [people] to follow it and hold to it, it would have been correct; as Allah said ﴿كِتَابَ اللهِ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, i.e. hold to the Book of Allah.

farraa:2-2.t: His words: ﴿فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ﴾: [al-dīn] is accusative because "making sincere" (ikhlāṣ) falls upon it. Likewise whatever resembles it in the Quran, such as ﴿مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدينَ﴾, takes the accusative as here. And if you made (الدين) nominative by lahu, making "sincere" self-sufficient and not transitive «[Translator's note: the apodosis is missing in the source; the sense is presumably "it would be correct"]» — as if you said: "Worship Allah, obedient — for to Him belongs the religion."

farraa:3-3.t: His words: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾: (الذين) is in the position of a nominative, with an implied "saying". The meaning is: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ﴾ say to their patrons — which are the idols —: "We worship you only so that you bring us near to Allah." So it is in the (ḥarf, i.e. reading) of Ubayy, and the reading of ʿAbdallāh is (قالُوا ما نعبدهم) ("they said: we worship them only…"). In reported speech, when it is with "saying", implied or explicit, it is permissible to treat the absent as the addressed, or to leave it as absent; as in His words: ﴿قُلْ لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَيُغْلَبُونَ﴾ and ﴿سَتُغْلَبُونَ﴾, with yāʾ and tāʾ, according to what I have described to you.

farraa:6-6.t:
His words: ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾: someone may say: How did He say ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ﴾, to the children of Adam, then say ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾, when the spouse was created before the offspring? There are two explanations of this in Arabic. One: when the Arabs report two acts of a man, they bring the second with thumma when it is the later in meaning; but sometimes they use (thumma) for what is earlier in meaning, making (thumma) part of the speaker's report. Of that is your saying: "I have heard what you did today; then what you did yesterday is more amazing." This is a sequence within the speaker's report. And you say: "I have given you something today; then what I gave you yesterday is more." This is of that kind.
The other explanation: that you make His creating the spouse refer back to (وَاحدة), as if He said: "He created you from a soul on its own, then made from it its spouse." So in (وَاحدةٍ) there is the sense of His creating it alone.
He said: one of the Arabs recited to me:
أعددتَه للخَصْم ذى التعدّى * كوّحتَه منك بُدون الجَهْد
(You prepared him for the transgressing adversary; you overcame him without [even] exertion.)
Its meaning is: the one who, when he transgresses, you overcome him; and kawwaḥtahu means: you overcame him.

farraa:7-7.t: His words: ﴿وَإِن تَشْكُرُواْ يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ﴾: He says: He is pleased with the thanks for you. This is like His words: ﴿فأخْشَوْهُمْ فَزَادَهُمْ إيماناً﴾, i.e. the people's saying increased them. If someone says: How did He say ﴿وَلاَ يَرْضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ ٱلْكُفْرَ﴾ when they have disbelieved? I say: He is not pleased that they should disbelieve. So the meaning of "disbelief" is "that they disbelieve", and its meaning is not disbelief itself. A similar case that will make it clear to you is that you say: "I do not love evildoing, yet I would love for so-and-so to do evil so that he may be punished." This is something that makes its meaning clear to you.

farraa:8-8.t:
His words: ﴿نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوۤ إِلَيْهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: He says: he abandoned the One whom he used to call upon when harm touched him — He means Allah the Exalted. If you say: Why then was it not said: "he forgot whom (man) he used to call upon"? I say: (mā) may stand in the place of (man). Allah said ﴿قُلْ يأيُّهَا الكافِرُونَ لا أَعْبُدُ مَا تَعْبُدُونَ، وَلاَ أَنْتُم عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾, meaning Allah. And He said ﴿فانكِحُوا مَا طابَ لَكُمْ مِنَ النِّسَاء﴾. This is one explanation, and the commentary came with it. Similar is ﴿أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَىّ﴾. And ﴿نسىَ ما كان يدعُو إليْه﴾ may mean: he forgot his calling upon Allah before. If you wish, you may make the hāʾ in (إليه) refer to mā, and if you wish, to Allah; all is sound.
His words ﴿قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلاً﴾ 166 ا: this is a threat, not a pure command. Likewise His words ﴿فتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ and the like.

farraa:9-9.t:
His words: ﴿أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read it without doubling [a-man]; that is also mentioned of Nāfiʿ and Ḥamza, and they explained it as meaning: "O you who are devoutly obedient". It is a good option: the Arabs call with the alif just as they call with yā; they say: yā Zaydu aqbil and a-Zaydu aqbil ("O Zayd, come"). The poet said:
أبنى لبُيََنْىَ لستم بيـدٍ * إلاّ يدٍ ليسَت لها عَضُد
(O sons of Lubaynā, you are not a hand — except a hand that has no upper arm.)
Another said:
أضمر بن ضمـرةَ ماذا ذكَرْ * تَ مِن صِرْمة أُخذت بالمُرارِ
(O Ḍamra son of Ḍamra, what have you mentioned of a herd of camels taken at al-Murār?)
This is frequent in poetry. The meaning is then connected by the vocative, like something conjoined: because He mentioned the forgetful disbeliever, then related the story of the righteous one with a vocative; as you say in speech: "So-and-so neither prays nor fasts — so O you who pray and fast, rejoice!" This is its meaning, and Allah knows best.
The alif may also be interrogative, interpreted as am, because the Arabs sometimes put (am) in place of the alif when speech precedes it — I have described enough of that. The meaning would be: "Is one who is devoutly obedient — (without doubling) — like the first, who was mentioned with forgetfulness and disbelief?"
Whoever reads it with doubling [am-man] intends the meaning of the alif. And this is the [proper] way: that you say am when it refers back to a meaning that has preceded. Al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it so, meaning: am man. The Arabs say: "This was when I said: Is it your brother or the wolf?" — this phrase is said after sunset when you see a figure and do not know what it is. Of it is your saying: "Is that [my she-camel] or a wild one?", and your saying: "Is that [my camel] or a wild ass chasing she-asses?"
If someone says: Where then is the answer to (أمّن هُوَ)? It is clear from the speech that it is implied, and its meaning has run in the beginning of the passage, since He mentioned the one gone astray, then mentioned the rightly guided with the interrogative; that is evidence that He means: "Is this one like that one?" or "Is this one better, or that one?" Whoever does not know the ways of the Arabs, and to whom the meaning in this and its like is not clear, will not be satisfied or contented. Do you not see the poet's saying:
فأقسم لو شَىْءٌ أتانا رَسُـوله * سواكَ ولكن لم نجد لك مَدْفعَا
(I swear, if anything other than you had sent its messenger to us — but we found no way of repelling you.)
Its meaning is: had a messenger of someone other than you come to us, we would have repelled him; the meaning was known and not made explicit. His words ﴿أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللهُ صَدْرَهُ للإِسْلاَمِ﴾ run on the same pattern.
His words ﴿آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ سَاجِداً وَقَآئِماً﴾: accusative on the sense of: he is obedient, prostrating at one time and standing at another, i.e. obedient in both states [ḥāl (circumstantial)]. Had it been made nominative as "obedient" (qānit) is nominative, it would have been correct. al-qunūt is obedience.

farraa:19-19.t:
His words: ﴿أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ ٱلْعَذَابِ أَفَأَنتَ تُنقِذُ مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
It may be asked: How did two interrogatives come together in one meaning? It is answered: This is one of the cases where a single question is intended; the interrogative comes early, out of its place, and is then brought back to the place that belongs to it. The meaning is — and Allah knows best —: "Will you save one upon whom the word of punishment has become due?" Similar to it, outside interrogatives, are His words: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إذا مِتُّمْ وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَاباً وَعِظَاماً أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُون﴾, where He repeated ﴿أنكم﴾ twice; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Does he promise you that you will be brought out when you have died and become dust?" Similar are His words: ﴿لاَ تَحْسَبَنّ الذِينَ يَفْرَحُونَ بِمَا أَتَوْا وَيُحِبُّونَ أن يُحْمَدُوا بِمَا لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا فَلاَ تَحْسَبَنّهُمْ﴾, where He repeated (taḥsabanna) twice; their meaning — and Allah knows best — is: "Do not think that those who rejoice in what they have done are in a place of safety from the punishment." There is much like this in the Revelation and in other speech of the Arabs.

farraa:22-22.t: His words: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ and ﴿عن ذكر الله﴾ — all is correct. You say: "I got indigestion from (min) food I ate" and "from (ʿan) food I ate", the same in meaning. It is as if His saying "they hardened from (min) His remembrance" means that they made it a lie, so it hardened their hearts, i.e. increased them in hardness. And it is as if one who said "they hardened away from (ʿan) it" means: they turned away from it.

farraa:23-23.t:
His words: ﴿كِتَاباً مُّتَشَابِهاً﴾, i.e. not discordant; no part of it contradicts another.
His words ﴿مَّثَانِيَ﴾, i.e. repeated: the mention of reward and punishment is repeated in it.
His words: ﴿تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾: they shiver in fear at a verse of punishment when it is revealed, ﴿ثُمَّ تَلِينُ﴾ ("then they soften") when a verse of mercy is revealed.

farraa:24-24.t:
His words: ﴿أَفَمَن يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوۤءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
It is said: the keepers [of Hell] take the disbeliever off to the Fire, shackled, and he is hurled into the Fire, and he cannot shield himself from it except with his face. Its answer is of the implied kind that I mentioned to you.

farraa:29-29.t:
His words: ﴿فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ مُتَشَاكِسُونَ﴾: at variance. This is a parable Allah struck for the disbeliever and the believer. He made the one in whom there are partners the one who worships the various gods.
His words ﴿وَرَجُلاً سَلَماً لِّرَجُلٍ﴾: he is the believer who affirms Allah's oneness. The common people read (سَلَماً). salam and sālim are close in meaning; it is as if (salaman) were the maṣdar (verbal noun) of your saying: salima lahu salaman. The Arabs say: rabiḥa ribḥan and rabaḥan, and salima silman, salaman and salāmatan. So sālim is a description of the man, and salam is its maṣdar. And Allah knows best.
Abū al-ʿAbbās related to us: Muḥammad related to us: al-Farrāʾ related to us; he said: Abū Isḥāq al-Taymī — not the companion of Hushaym — related to me from Abū Rawq, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read (ورَجُلاً سَالماً). Al-Farrāʾ said: And Ibn ʿUyayna related to me from ʿAbd al-Karīm al-Jazarī, from Mujāhid, that he read (سالماً).
His words: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلاً﴾, and He did not say "two likenesses", because both together were struck as a single parable, so "likeness" ran for them in the singular. Similar is ﴿وجَعَلْنَا ابنَ مَرْيَمَ وَأُمّهُ آيَةً﴾, and He did not say "two signs", because their case is one. Had it been said "two likenesses" or "two signs", it would have been correct, because they are two in wording.

farraa:33-33.t: His words: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾: (الذى) is not specific (ghayr muwaqqat), so it is as if it is plural in meaning. In the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (والذين جاءوا بالصّدق وصَدّقوا به); this is evidence that (الذى) is to be interpreted as plural.

farraa:36-36.t: His words: ﴿أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ﴾: Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb and Abū Jaʿfar al-Madanī read it (أليس الله بكافٍ عباده), in the plural. The people read it ﴿عَبْدَهُ﴾. That is because Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Do you not fear that our gods will derange you because of your faulting them?" So Allah revealed ﴿أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ﴾ — Muḥammad ﷺ — so how can they frighten you with those besides Him? And those who said ﴿عِبَادَهُ﴾ said: the nations of the prophets had intended [harm] against them and threatened them with the like of this; they said to Shuʿayb ﴿إنْ نقُولُ إلاّ اعْتَراكَ بَعْضُ آلِهَتِنَا بسُوءٍ﴾ [Translator's note: in the Quran (11:54) these words were said to Hūd, not Shuʿayb], so Allah said ﴿أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عبادَهُ﴾, i.e. Muḥammad, peace be upon him, and the prophets before him. And all is correct.

farraa:38-38.t: His words: ﴿هَلْ هُنَّ كَاشِفَاتُ ضُرِّهِ﴾ ﴿مُمْسِكَاتُ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾: ʿĀṣim, al-Ḥasan and Shayba al-Madanī read both with tanwīn, and Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb read them with iḍāfa. All is correct. Similar are ﴿إنَّ اللهَ بَالِغُ أَمْرِهِ﴾ and ﴿بالِغٌ أمْرَهُ﴾, and ﴿مُوهِنُ كَيْدِ الكافِرِينَ﴾ and ﴿مُوهِنٌ كَيْدَ الكافِرِين﴾. The iḍāfa carries the sense of the action being past. So when you see that the action has passed in meaning, prefer the iḍāfa in it: you say "your brother took his due", and so here you say: akhūka ākhidhu ḥaqqihi; and it is ugly to say: ākhidhun ḥaqqahu. But when it is future and has not yet happened, you say: akhūka ākhidhun ḥaqqahu ʿan qalīl and ākhidhu ḥaqqihi ʿan qalīl ("your brother will shortly take his due"). Do you not see that you do not say: hādhā qātilun Ḥamzata mubaghghaḍan ("this is the slayer of Ḥamza, hated"), because its meaning is past, so the tanwīn is ugly, because it is a noun.

farraa:42-42.t:
His words: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلأَنفُسَ حِينَ مِوْتِـهَا وَٱلَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِـهَا﴾: the meaning in it is: He takes the souls at the time of their death, and takes the one that has not died in its sleep at the end of its term. And it is said that its being taken is its sleep. That is the dearer of the two explanations to me, because of His words ﴿فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ﴾,
and because of His words: ﴿وَهُوَ الذِى يَتَوَفَّاكُمْ بالليلِ﴾. And it is read ﴿قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ﴾ and ﴿وقُضِى عَليها الموتُ﴾.

farraa:49-49.t: His words: ﴿بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾: (hiya) came out feminine because "trial" (fitna) is feminine. Had it been said: bal huwa fitnatun, it would have been correct; as He said ﴿هَذَا رَحْمَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّى﴾, and there is much like it in the Quran. Likewise His words: ﴿قَدْ قَالَهَا الذينَ منْ قَبْلِهِم﴾: it was made feminine meaning "the word" (al-kalima); had it been said qad qālahu alladhīna min qablihim, it would have been correct. Similar in speech is your saying: qad faʿaltahā and faʿalta dhāk ("you did it"). And similar is His saying: ﴿وَفَعَلْتَ فَعْلتك التى فعَلْتَ﴾; in its place would be permissible, had it come: wa-faʿalta fiʿlaka.

farraa:53-53.t: His words: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً﴾: in the reading of ʿAbdallāh it is (الذنوب جميعاً لمن يشاء) ("all sins, for whom He wills"). Al-Farrāʾ said: And Abū Isḥāq al-Taymī related to me from Abū Rawq, from Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read it as it is in the codex of ʿAbdallāh (يغفر الذنوب جيمعاً لمن يشاء). It was revealed concerning Waḥshī, the killer of Ḥamza, and those like him.

farraa:56-56.t:
His words: ﴿أَن تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يٰحَسْرَتَا﴾, i.e. act, turn back [to Allah], and act ﴿أَن تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ﴾: so that none of you will say tomorrow ﴿يٰحَسْرَتَا﴾. Similar are His words: ﴿وَأَلْقَى فِى الأَرْضِ رَوَاسِىَ أَنْ تَمِيدَ بِكُمْ﴾, i.e. so that it does not sway.
His words: ﴿يٰحَسْرَتَا﴾: [like] yā waylatā, in iḍāfa to the speaker. The Arabs change the yāʾ into an alif in every expression whose meaning is a cry for help, which comes out in the form of a vocative. Sometimes yā ḥasrati is said, just as they said: yā lahfi ʿalā fulān and yā lahfā ʿalayhi ("O my grief for so-and-so"). He said: Abū Tharwān al-ʿUklī recited to me:
تزورونها أَو لا أزور نِسَاءكم * ألهَفِ لأولاد الإماء الحواطب
(Will you visit her while I may not visit your women? O my grief at the sons of the firewood-gathering slave-girls!)
He put it in the genitive (kasra) as the one addressed is put in the genitive when the speaker attaches it to himself.
Sometimes the Arabs add a hāʾ after the alif that is in ﴿حسرتَا﴾, and give it kasra at times and ḍamma at others. He said: Abū Faqʿas, one of the Banū Asad, recited to me:
يا ربِّ ياربّاهِ إيّاك أسَلْ * عَفراء يا ربّاهِ من قبل الأَجل
(O Lord, O my Lord, it is You I ask for ʿAfrāʾ, O my Lord, before the appointed term.)
so he used the kasra. He said: and Abū Faqʿas recited to me:
يا مرحباهِ بحمار ناهِيْـه * إِذَا أتى قرّبته للسَّانية
(Welcome to Nāhiya's donkey! When it comes I bring it near to the water-wheel.)
The kasra is more frequent in the speech of the Arabs, except in their saying yā hanāh and yā hantāh, where the ḍamma is more frequent than the kasra, because it is frequent in speech, so it is as if it were a single called word.

farraa:58-58.t:
His words: ﴿لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَـرَّةً فَأَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُحْسِنِينَ﴾: the accusative in His words ﴿فَأَكُونَ﴾ is as the answer to law. And if you wish, you may make it refer back to an interpreted an, implied in "the return" (al-karra), as you say: law anna lī an akurra fa-akūna ("if only I could return and be…"). Similar, among what is accusative by an implied an, are His words: ﴿وَمَا كَانَ لِبَشَرٍ أنْ يُكَلِّمهُ اللهُ إلاّ وَحيْاً أوْ مِنْ وَرَاء حِجَابٍ أَوْ يُرْسِلَ﴾; the meaning — and Allah knows best — is: it is not for a human that Allah should speak to him except that He reveal to him or send. Had ﴿فيُوحى﴾ been made nominative, since an does not appear before it or with it, it would have been correct; some readers read it so. He said: and someone of the Banū Asad recited to me:
يَحُلّ أُحَيْدَه ويقال بَعْـلٌ * ومثلُ تموُّلٍ منه افتقارُ
فما يُخطئكِ لا يخطئكِ منه * طَبَانِيَةٌ فيَحْظُلُ أو يَغارُ
(He settles alone and is called a husband, and the like of his getting wealth is poverty; and whatever else misses you, there will not miss you from him a jealous watchfulness, so that he restrains you or grows jealous.)
He made it nominative. Another recited to me:
فمالك منها غير ذِكرى وحِسْبة * وتسأل عن ركبانها أينَ يمَّموا
(You have nothing of her but a memory and a reckoning, and you ask about her riders, where they have headed.)
Al-Kisāʾī said: I heard from the Arabs: "It is nothing but one blow from the lion, and it breaks (fa-yaḥṭimu) his back", (and) fa-yaḥṭima ẓahrahu. He said: and al-Asadī recited to me:
عَلى أحْوذِيَّيْن استقلت عَشِيَّة * فما هى إلاَّ لمحة فتغيب
(On two swift wings she rose one evening, and it was but a glance, and she vanished.)

farraa:59-59.t: His words: ﴿بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَآءَتْكَ آيَاتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا﴾: the readers agree on fatḥa on the kāf, the one addressed being masculine. Al-Farrāʾ said: And an elder related to me from Wiqāʾ ibn Iyās, with his chain, that he read (بَلَى قد جَاءَتْكِ آياتى فكذَّبتِ بهَا واستكبرتِ), with kasra on the kāf and the tāʾ, as if addressing the soul (nafs, feminine). It is a good option, because He mentioned the soul and addressed it first, so He ran the second speech on the soul in addressing it.

farraa:60-60.t:
His words: ﴿وَيَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ تَرَى ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَبُواْ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُم مُّسْوَدَّةٌ﴾: You make ﴿وجوههم﴾ and ﴿مسودّة﴾ nominative because the verb has fallen upon (الذين), then after (الذين) came a noun with its own predicate, so you make it nominative by its predicate, while there is in it the sense of an accusative. Likewise with every noun on which you have made "thinking", "seeing" and the like fall: make the nouns that come after it nominative when their predicates are with them after them; as you say: raʾaytu ʿAbdallāhi amruhu mustaqīmun ("I saw ʿAbdallāh — his affair is upright"). If you put the uprightness first, you make it accusative and the noun nominative, saying: raʾaytu ʿAbdallāhi mustaqīman amruhu. And had you made all three accusative in the first case, by repetition (takrīr, i.e. as a badal), it would be permissible; so you say: raʾaytu ʿAbdallāhi amrahu mustaqīman. ʿAdī ibn Zayd said:
ذرِينى إن أمركِ لن يطاعَا * وما ألفيتِنى حِلْمى مُضَاعَا
(Leave me — your command will not be obeyed; and you have not found my forbearance squandered.)
He made "forbearance" and "squandered" accusative by repetition. Similar is:
* ما للجمال مشيِها وئيـدا *
(What is the matter with the camels, their walking slowly?)
He put "the camels" and "walking" in the genitive by repetition. Had a reader read ﴿وُجُوهَهُم مُّسْوَدَّةٌ﴾ on this pattern, it would have been correct [Translator's note: on the stated pattern one would expect the second word to be accusative as well, «مسودّةً»; the source prints it with ḍamma].

farraa:61-61.t: His words: ﴿بِمَفَازَاتِهِمْ﴾ is plural, while the people of Medina read ﴿بِمَفَازَتِهِمْ﴾ in the singular. All is correct. You say in speech: "the affair of the people has become clear" and "the affairs of the people", and "the voice was raised" and "the voices", (and the meaning) is one. Allah said ﴿إنَّ أنْكَرَ الأصواتِ لَصَوْتُ الحَمِيرِ﴾ and did not say "voices"; and all is correct.

farraa:66-66.t:
His words: ﴿بَلِ ٱللَّهَ فَٱعْبُدْ﴾: You make (Allāh) accusative — meaning in the i'rab — by this overt verb, because it is a reply to speech. And if you wish, you may make it accusative by a verb you imply before it, because nothing but a verb precedes a command or prohibition.
But the Arabs say: Zaydun fa-l-yaqum and Zaydan fa-l-yaqum ("Zayd — let him stand"). Whoever makes it nominative says: I make it nominative by the verb after it, since what is before it does not appear. It may also be made nominative by implying for it the like of what is after it, as if you said: "Let Zayd see to it — let him stand." And whoever makes it accusative, it is as if he said: "Look to Zayd — let him stand."

farraa:67-67.t:
His words: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضُ جَمِيعـاً قَبْضَـتُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾: you make "the grip" (al-qabḍa) nominative. And if someone made it accusative [it would be possible] «[Translator's note: the apodosis is missing in the source]», as you say: shahru Ramaḍāna insilākha Shaʿbāna, i.e. this is for me at the passing away of that.
His words: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾: you make "the heavens" nominative by "folded" (maṭwiyyāt) when you make maṭwiyyāt nominative. And whoever says ﴿مَطْوِيَّاتٍ﴾ makes "the heavens" nominative by the bāʾ in "His right hand", as if He said: "and the heavens are in His right hand", and makes maṭwiyyāt accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or by qaṭʿ (detachment). The ḥāl is better.

farraa:68-68.t: His words: ﴿فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾: He said: al-Kalbī used to say: I do not know what al-ṣūr is. It has been mentioned that it is the horn; and it is mentioned of al-Ḥasan or of Qatāda that he said: al-ṣūr is the plural of ṣūra ("form").

farraa:73-73.t: His words: ﴿طِبْتُمْ﴾, i.e. you have become pure, ﴿فَٱدْخُلُوهَا﴾.

farraa:74-74.t: His words: ﴿وَأَوْرَثَنَا ٱلأَرْضَ﴾: He means Paradise.

harrat-mujtaba:28-28.t: «قرآنًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «غير» is a second naʿt (adjective); and the clause «لعلهم يتقون» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:29-29.t: «رجلا» is a badal (substitute) from «مثلا»; the clause «فيه شركاء» is a naʿt (adjective) of «رجلا»; the preposition phrase «لرجل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سلمًا»; the interrogative clause is resumptive, and likewise the clause «الحمد لله», and the clause «أكثرهم لا يعلمون».

harrat-mujtaba:31-31.t: The clause «ثم إنكم ...» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إنهم ميتون», and the two adverbs are attached to (mutaʿalliq) «تختصمون».

harrat-mujtaba:32-32.t: The clause «فمن أظلم» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «ممن» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أظلم»; «إذ» is an adverb of time attached to «كَذَب»; the clause «أليس في جهنم مثوى» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «للكافرين» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «مثوى».

harrat-mujtaba:33-33.t: The wāw in «والذي» is resumptive; «هم» is for separation (faṣl); and the clause «أولئك ... المتقون» is the khabar (predicate) of «الذي».

harrat-mujtaba:34-34.t: The clause «لهم ما يشاءون» is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «أولئك»; «عند» is an adverb of place attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:35-35.t: The interpreted maṣdar in the genitive «ليُكَفِّر» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «بالمحسنين»; «أجرهم» is a second object.

harrat-mujtaba:36-36.t: (أليس الله بكاف عبده) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The bāʾ in the khabar of laysa is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «ويخوفونك» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, i.e.: is He not sufficient for you at the time of their frightening you with such-and-such; the preposition phrase «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); «من» is a conditional noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first; and «هاد» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant.

harrat-mujtaba:37-37.t: «من» is conditional, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first, and the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «يضلل الله»; «مضل» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); «ذي» is a naʿt (adjective).

harrat-mujtaba:38-38.t: The wāw in «ولئن» is resumptive; the clause «مَنْ خلق» is the second mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the asking, suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative; the lām is the preparatory lām (mūṭṭiʾa) [of the oath]; and the clause «ليقولُنَّ الله» is the answer to the oath. «الله» is the fāʿil (agent) of an omitted verb, i.e.: Allah created them. «يقولُنَّ» is an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, which was dropped because of the succession of identical letters, and the wāw, dropped because of the meeting of two vowelless letters, is the fāʿil. The fāʾ in «أفرأيتم» links to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of an implied (muqaddar) condition, i.e.: if there is a god other than Him, then tell me. The implied conditional clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). «أرأيتم» takes two objects: the first is «ما», and the second is the interrogative clause «هل هن كاشفات»; the preposition phrase «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; the clause «إن أرادني الله» is parenthetical, and the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes it; the clause «أرادني برحمة» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «أرادني.. بضر»; and the clause «هل هُنَّ ممسكات» is conjoined to the clause «هل هن كاشفات», as in: أرأيت زيدًا: إن جاءك هل تكرمه؟ أو غاب هل تعاقبه؟ ("Have you considered Zayd: if he comes to you, will you honour him? Or if he is absent, will you punish him?"). His saying «حسبي الله» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the preposition phrase «عليه» is attached to «يتوكل».

harrat-mujtaba:39-39.t: His saying «يا قوم»: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, with the yāʾ implied (muqaddar); the preposition phrase «على مكانتكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of [the agent of] «اعملوا»; the clause «إني عامل» is resumptive; and the clause «فسوف تعلمون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إني عامل».

harrat-mujtaba:40-40.t: «مَنْ» is a relative noun, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause «يخزيه» is a naʿt (adjective) of «عذاب».

harrat-mujtaba:41-41.t: The preposition phrase «للناس» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أنزلنا»; the preposition phrase «بالحق» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «أنزلنا»; the conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «إنا أنزلنا»; «من» is a conditional noun, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition phrase «فلنفسه» is attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e.: his being guided is for himself; the preposition phrase «عليها» is attached to a ḥāl of the fāʿil of «يضل»; the clause «وما أنت عليهم بوكيل» is conjoined to the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of «ما»; and the preposition phrase «عليهم» is attached to «وكيل».

harrat-mujtaba:42-42.t: «حين» is an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يَتَوَفَّى». His saying «والتي»: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأنفس»; the preposition phrase «في منامها» is attached to «يتوفَّى». The clause «فيمسك» is conjoined to the clause «يتوفَّى»; the preposition phrase «إلى أجل» is attached to «يرسل»; the preposition phrase «لقوم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «لآيات»; and the clause «يتفكرون» is a naʿt.

harrat-mujtaba:43-43.t: «أم» is the disjunctive (munqaṭiʿa) one; the preposition phrase «من دون» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted second object; the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) is omitted, i.e.: will they intercede?; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), conjoining this ḥāl (circumstantial) to an implied (muqaddar) ḥāl for comprehensiveness, the implied form being: will they intercede in every state, even if they possess nothing? The clause «ولو كانوا» is a ḥāl of the fāʿil (agent) of the implied verb, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:44-44.t: «جميعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الشفاعة»; the clause «له ملك» is resumptive; and the clause «ثم إليه ترجعون» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «له الملك».

harrat-mujtaba:45-45.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; «وحده» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) interpreted as an indefinite; the second conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first; the preposition phrase «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied (muqaddar) ṣila (relative clause); the clause «إذا هم يستبشرون» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); and «إذا» is of surprise (fujāʾiyya).

harrat-mujtaba:46-46.t: «اللهم»: the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma in the position of the accusative, and the mīm is a substitute for the omitted (يا); «فاطر» is a badal (substitute); «عالم» is a second badal; the clause «أنت تحكم» is the answer to the vocative, resumptive; the preposition phrase «فيه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «يختلفون».

harrat-mujtaba:47-47.t: The conditional clause is resumptive; the interpreted maṣdar is the fāʿil (agent) of [an implied] «ثبت»; «ما» is the noun of «أن»; the preposition phrase «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); «جميعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «ما»; «مثله» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «ما»; «معه» is an adverb attached to a ḥāl of «مثله»; and the clause «بدا» is conjoined to the clause «افتدوا».

harrat-mujtaba:48-48.t: The clause «وبدا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the earlier clause «بدا»; «ما» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the second «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «حاق».

harrat-mujtaba:49-49.t: The conditional clause is resumptive, and the second conditional clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the first; the preposition phrase «منا» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «نعمة»; the preposition phrase «على عِلْم» is attached to a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) in «أوتيته»; the clause «ولكن أكثرهم لا يعلمون» is conjoined to the resumptive clause «بل هي فتنة».

harrat-mujtaba:50-50.t: The clause «فما أغنى ... ما» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «قد قالها»; «ما» is a relative noun, the fāʿil (agent) of «أغنى».

harrat-mujtaba:51-51.t: The clause «فأصابهم سيئات» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «فما أغنى»; «ما» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «الذين ظلموا» is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the preposition phrase «من هؤلاء» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the wāw; the clause «وما هم بمعجزين» is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «سيصيبهم»; and the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida) in the khabar of «ما».

harrat-mujtaba:52-52.t: The clause «أولم يعلموا» is resumptive, and the interpreted maṣdar is the object of «يعلموا».

harrat-mujtaba:53-53.t: «الذين» is a naʿt (adjective); «جميعًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الذنوب»; «هو» is a tawkīd (emphasis) of the hāʾ in «إنه»; and the clause «إنه هو الغفور» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:54-54.t: The clause «وأنيبوا» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «لا تقنطوا»; the interpreted maṣdar «أن يأتيكم» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); «ثم» is a particle of resumption, [followed by] an imperfect verb and its nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), and the clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:55-55.t: «ما» is a relative noun, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the two preposition phrases are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «أنزل»; «بغتة» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl (circumstantial); and the clause «وأنتم لا تشعرون» is a ḥāl clause.

harrat-mujtaba:56-56.t: The interpreted maṣdar «أن تقول» is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e.: out of dislike [that a soul should say]. «يا حسرتا»: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb) with the fatḥa implied (muqaddar) on the letter before the yāʾ that was changed into alif, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the preposition phrase «على ما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the regret; «ما» is maṣdariyya, the implied form being: O my regret, being over my neglect. The wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); «إنْ» is lightened from the heavy one and inoperative; the lām is the differentiating lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); and the clause «وإن كنت» is a ḥāl clause.

harrat-mujtaba:57-57.t: The interpreted maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it is the fāʿil (agent) of an implied (muqaddar) «ثبت».

harrat-mujtaba:58-58.t: The clause «ترى» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the fāʾ is causal (sababiyya); the interpreted maṣdar from «أنَّ» and what follows it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to a maṣdar extracted from the preceding speech, the implied form being: would that there were a return for me, so that my being among the doers of good [would follow]; and the clause «أكون» is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (al-mawṣūl al-ḥarfī).

harrat-mujtaba:59-59.t: The clause «قد جاءتك آياتي» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied (muqaddar) saying, and the clause «فكذَّبْتَ» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «جاءتك آياتي».

harrat-mujtaba:60-60.t: The wāw is resumptive; «يوم» is an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ترى»; the clause «وجوههم مسودة» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الذين»; and the clause «أليس في جهنم مثوى» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:61-61.t: The clause «وينجِّي» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ترى»; the preposition phrase «بمفازتهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «ينجي»; the clause «لا يمسهم السوء» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the relative noun; and the clause «ولا هم يحزنون» is conjoined to the clause «لا يمسهم السوء».

harrat-mujtaba:62-62.t: The clause «وهو على كل شيء وكيل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the resumptive clause, and the preposition phrase «على كل» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «وكيل».

harrat-mujtaba:63-63.t: The clause «له مقاليد» is a second khabar (predicate) of «هو»; the relative clause is resumptive; «هم» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl); and «الخاسرون» is the khabar of «أولئك».

harrat-mujtaba:64-64.t: The fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida); «غير» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «أعبد» placed first, and «تأمرونِّي» does not govern it; the meaning is: أفغير الله أعبد تأمروني؟ ("Is it other than Allah that I should worship, you bid me?"). The clause «تأمرونِّي» is resumptive, because it is placed after in the implied order; the omission of «أن» with «أعبد» in the other view is not regular (lā yanqās). The nūn of the nominative was assimilated into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya). «أيها» is the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, and «ها» is for drawing attention; «الجاهلون» is ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the vocative clause is resumptive; and the clause «أعبد» is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

harrat-mujtaba:65-65.t: The clause «ولقد أوحي» is resumptive, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is the preposition phrase «إليك»; the clause «لئن أشركت ليحبطن عملك» explains what was revealed; the clause «ليحبطن» is the answer to the oath; and the clause «ولتكونَنَّ» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the answer to the oath.

harrat-mujtaba:66-66.t: «بل» is for digression (iḍrāb); the name of Majesty is accusative by the verb «أعبد»; and the fāʾ is redundant (zāʾida).

harrat-mujtaba:67-67.t: The clause «وما قدروا» is resumptive; «حق» is a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause «والأرض.. قبضته» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause, i.e.: they did not magnify Him as He truly deserves to be magnified, while He is described with this dazzling power. «جميعًا» is a ḥāl of «الأرض»; the clause «والسماوات مطويات» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ḥāl clause; the preposition phrase «بيمينه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مطويات»; the clause «سبحانه» is resumptive. The preposition phrase «عمَّا» is attached to «تعالى».

harrat-mujtaba:68-68.t: The clause «ونفخ» is resumptive; the preposition phrase «في الصور» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition phrase «في السماوات» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ṣila (relative clause); «مَنْ» is excepted; the fāʾ in «فإذا» is conjunctive; the clause «فإذا هم قيام» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «نفخ فيه»; and the clause «ينظرون» is a second khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «هم».

harrat-mujtaba:69-69.t: The clause «وأشرقت» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause {هُمْ قِيَامٌ}; the preposition phrase «بالنبيين» is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the preposition phrase «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the nāʾib fāʿil, which is the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e.: and the judgement was passed, being bound up with the truth; and the clause «وهم لا يظلمون» is a ḥāl clause.

harrat-mujtaba:70-70.t: «ما» is a second object; the clause «وهو أعلم» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; «ما» in «ما يفعلون» is maṣdariyya, and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أعلم».

harrat-mujtaba:71-71.t: The preposition phrase «إلى جهنم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سِيق»; «زمرًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya), and the conditional clause is resumptive; the preposition phrase «منكم» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «رسل»; the clause «يتلون» is a second naʿt of «رسل»; «لقاء» is a second object; «هذا» is a naʿt of «يومكم», and it is interpreted as a derived word, i.e.: the one pointed to. The object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl) of «قالوا» is omitted, i.e.: yes, the messengers came to us; the clause «حَقَّتْ كلمة» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «جاءتنا», and the link between the conjoined and what it is conjoined to is the overt noun.

harrat-mujtaba:72-72.t: The nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) of «قيل» is the pronoun of the maṣdar, i.e.: the saying was said; the preposition phrase «فيها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the ḥāl (circumstantial) «خالدين»; the clause «فبئس مثوى» is resumptive, and the specified noun (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, i.e.: Hell.

harrat-mujtaba:73-73.t: The preposition phrase «إلى الجنة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «سِيق»; «زمرًا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); «حتى» is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya); the conditional clause is resumptive and its apodosis is omitted, i.e.: they were happy; «سلام» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the preposition phrase «عليكم» is attached to the khabar (predicate); the clause «طبتم» is resumptive within the scope of the saying; the clause «فادخلوها» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «طبتم»; «خالدين» is a ḥāl of the pronoun «ها».

harrat-mujtaba:74-74.t: «الذي» is a naʿt (adjective); «وعده» is a second object; the clause «نتبوأ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of «أورثنا»; the clause «نشاء» is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause «فنِعْم أجر» is resumptive, and the specified noun (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, i.e.: Paradise.

harrat-mujtaba:75-75.t: The clause «وترى» is resumptive; «حافِّين» is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the preposition phrase «من حول» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «حافِّين»; the clause «يسبحون» is a ḥāl of the pronoun in «حافِّين»; the clause «قضي» is a ḥāl of the wāw in «يسبحون»; the preposition phrase «بالحق» is attached to a ḥāl of the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent), the implied form being: the judgement was passed, being bound up with the truth; and the clause «وقيل» is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the clause «ترى».

harrat-mujtaba:1-1.t: The preposition «من الله» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «تنزيل».

harrat-mujtaba:2-2.t: The preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أنزلنا». The clause «فاعبد» is conjoined to the clause «أنزلنا». «مخلصًا»: ḥāl from the fāʿil of «اعبد»; the preposition «له» is attached to «مخلصًا»; «الدين» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the active participle «مخلصا».

harrat-mujtaba:3-3.t: «ألا» is for drawing attention (tanbīh). The clause «والذين اتخذوا» is resumptive; «الذين» is a mubtadaʾ (subject). The preposition «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the second object. The clause «ما نعبدهم» is the content of what is said (maqūl al-qawl) of an implied speech, i.e.: they say: we do not worship them; and the clause of saying is the khabar (predicate) of «الذين». «إلا» is for restriction. The maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليقرِّبونا» is genitive, attached to «نعبدهم». «زلفى»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), being synonymous with its governing word. The preposition «فيما» is attached to «يحكم», and the preposition «فيه» is attached to «يختلفون». «كفار»: a second khabar.

harrat-mujtaba:4-4.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) is the fāʿil (agent) [Translator's note: so written; it is the object] of «أراد». The preposition «مما» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun «ما يشاء». The two clauses «نسبح سبحانه» and «هو الله» are resumptive, and «الواحد القهار» are two predicates (khabars).

harrat-mujtaba:5-5.t: The preposition «بالحق» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «خلق». The clause «يكور» is resumptive. The clause «كل يجري» is a ḥāl from «الشمس» and «القمر». «ألا» is for drawing attention (tanbīh).

harrat-mujtaba:6-6.t: The clause «خلقكم» is resumptive. «جعل» means "created", and the preposition «منها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «جعل». The clause «يخلقكم» is resumptive. «خلقًا»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the preposition «من بعد» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «خلقًا». The preposition «في ظلمات» is a badal (substitute) of «في بطون» and is attached to what that is attached to. «ربكم»: a second khabar (predicate); the clause «له الملك» is a third khabar of «ذلكم», and the clause of declaring [Allah] transcendent (tanzīh) is a fourth khabar. The khabar of «لا» is omitted, its implied form being "deserving of worship"; «هو» is a badal of the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar. The clause «فأنى تصرفون» is resumptive, and «أنى» is an interrogative noun, ḥāl (circumstantial).

harrat-mujtaba:7-7.t: The preposition «عنكم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «غني». The clause «ولا يرضى» is conjoined to the khabar (predicate), of the type of conjoining a clause to a single word. The second conditional clause is conjoined to the first conditional clause. The hāʾ in «يرضى» [Translator's note: so written; the hāʾ is in «يرضه»] is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ refers to the gratitude. The clause «ولا تزر» is resumptive. The clause «ثم إلى ربكم مرجعكم» is conjoined to the clause «لا تزر وازرة», and the clause «فينبئكم» is conjoined to the clause «إلى ربكم مرجعكم». The preposition «بذات» is attached to «عليم».

harrat-mujtaba:8-8.t: The conditional clause is resumptive. «منيبًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الإنسان»; the preposition «إليه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «منيبًا». The second conditional clause is conjoined to the first. The preposition «منه» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «نعمة», and the preposition «لله» is attached to the second object. The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) «ليضلَّ» is genitive, attached to «جعل». «قليلا»: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), its adjective having taken its place.

harrat-mujtaba:9-9.t: «أم» is the disjoined (munqaṭiʿa) one. «من»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: like one who is disobedient. «آناء»: an adverb of time attached to (mutaʿalliq) «قانت». «ساجدًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «قانت», and the clause «يحذر» is a second ḥāl. The clause «قل» is resumptive, and likewise the clause «إنما يتذكر».

harrat-mujtaba:10-10.t: His words «يا عباد»: the one addressed, in a construct (munādā muḍāf), accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ. «الذين»: naʿt (adjective) of «عباد». The clause «للذين أحسنوا» is resumptive; «حسنة» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) placed later. The clause «وأرض الله واسعة» is conjoined to the resumptive [clause]. «أجرهم»: second object. The clause «إنما يوفى» is resumptive within the scope of the speech. The preposition «بغير» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «أجرهم».

harrat-mujtaba:11-11.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from «أن» and what follows it is accusative by removal of the preposition (the bāʾ). «مخلصًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the fāʿil (agent) of «أعبد»; the preposition «له» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «مخلصًا»; «الدين» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «مخلصًا».

harrat-mujtaba:12-12.t: The lām is for giving the reason (taʿlīl); the implied form is: and I have been commanded what I have been commanded «لأن أكون» (in order that I be).

harrat-mujtaba:13-13.t: (قل إني أخاف إن عصيت ربي عذاب يوم عظيم) [Translator's note: phrase discussed] The conditional clause is parenthetical, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, indicated by what precedes it.

harrat-mujtaba:14-14.t: The Divine Name is the object of «أعبد», placed first, and «ديني» is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:15-15.t: The clause «فاعبدوا» is conjoined to the clause {أَعْبُدُ}. The preposition «من دونه» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ما». «ألا» is a particle of drawing attention (tanbīh), and «هو» is a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl).

harrat-mujtaba:16-16.t: The clause «لهم ظلل» is resumptive. The preposition «من فوقهم» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ظلل». The fāʾ in «فاتقون» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «اتقون» is resumptive, and likewise the vocative clause.

harrat-mujtaba:17-17.t: The clause «والذين اجتنبوا ...» is resumptive, and the clause «لهم البشرى» is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) «الذين». The maṣdar (verbal noun) «أن يعبدوها» is a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from «الطاغوت». The clause «فبشِّر عباد» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:18-18.t: «الذين»: naʿt (adjective) of «عباد». «هم»: a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position.

harrat-mujtaba:19-19.t: The hamza is interrogative and the fāʾ is resumptive. «مَنْ»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e.: like one who is saved. The second hamza is interrogative and the fāʾ is a conjunction; the clause «أفأنت تنقذ» is conjoined to «أفمَنْ حَقَّ». The preposition «في النار» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the implied ṣila (relative clause).

harrat-mujtaba:20-20.t: «لكن»: a particle of rectification (istidrāk). The preposition «من فوقها» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) an implied khabar (predicate) of «غرف», and the clause «من فوقها غرف» is a naʿt (adjective) of «غُرف». «مبنية»: naʿt of «غرف», and the clause «تجري» is a second naʿt. «وَعْدَ»: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an implied verb, and the clause of the implied verb is resumptive. The clause «لا يخلف» is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:21-21.t: The interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) formed from «أنَّ» and what follows it is the object of «تر». «ينابيع»: second object, by making «سلكه» carry the sense of «جعله» ("made it"). The preposition «في الأرض» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of «ينابيع». «مختلفًا»: naʿt of «زرعًا», and «ألوانه» is the fāʿil (agent) of «مختلفًا». «مصفرًا»: ḥāl (circumstantial) from the hāʾ, and «حطامًا» is a second object. The preposition «لأولي» is attached to a naʿt of «لذكرى».

harrat-mujtaba:22-22.t: The hamza is interrogative, and «مَنْ» is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject); the khabar (predicate) is implied, i.e.: like one whose heart has hardened. The preposition «للإسلام» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) «شرح». The clause «فهو على نور» is conjoined to the clause «شرح». The preposition «من ربه» is attached to a naʿt (adjective) of «نور». The clause «فويل للقاسية» is resumptive; «ويل» is a mubtadaʾ, and beginning with an indefinite noun is allowed because it denotes a supplication; the preposition «للقاسية» is attached to the khabar of «ويل». «قلوبهم» is the fāʿil (agent) of «القاسية». The preposition «من ذكر» is attached to «القاسية».

harrat-mujtaba:23-23.t: «كتابًا»: badal (substitute) of «أحسن». «مثاني»: a second naʿt (adjective) of «كتاب»; the clause «تقشعر» is a third naʿt, and the clause «ثم تلين» is conjoined to the clause «تقشعر». The clause «يهدي» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «هدى». «مَنْ» is conditional, a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) placed first. «هادٍ» is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «من» is redundant (zāʾida); the clause «فما له من هاد» is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

harrat-mujtaba:24-24.t: The fāʾ is resumptive. «من»: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being: like one who does not guard himself. The clause «وقيل» is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the wāw is circumstantial. «ما»: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object).

harrat-mujtaba:25-25.t: «حيث»: an adverbial noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of the genitive, attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أتاهم», and the clause «لا يشعرون» is muḍāf ilayhi (in genitive construct).

harrat-mujtaba:26-26.t: «الخزي»: second object. The preposition «في الحياة» is attached to (mutaʿalliq) a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الخزي». The clause «ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر» is resumptive. The apodosis of «لو» is omitted, its implied form being: they would not have denied; and the conditional clause is resumptive.

harrat-mujtaba:27-27.t: The wāw is resumptive. The three prepositions are attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb «ضربنا». The clause «لعلهم يتذكرون» is resumptive.

mekki-muskil:1-1.t: His saying, the Exalted, {تَنْزِيل الْكتاب}: a mubtadaʾ (subject), and the khabar (predicate) is من الله. It has also been said that it is nominative by an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being "this is the sending down of the Book". Al-Kisāʾī allowed the accusative on the implied form "recite the sending down" or "follow the sending down". Al-Farrāʾ said the accusative is by incitement (ighrāʾ).

mekki-muskil:3-3.t:
His saying {وَالَّذين اتَّخذُوا}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, its implied form being "they said: we do not worship them…". It has also been said that الذين is nominative by an implied verb, its implied form being "and those who took… said".

His saying زلفى is in the accusative position as a maṣdar (verbal noun).

His saying {أم من هُوَ قَانِت}: whoever read أَمَنْ without doubling made it a vocative, with nothing omitted in the speech. According to Sībawayh it is not permissible to drop the vocative particle from an indeterminate noun (mubham); the Kufans allowed it. It has also been said that it is an interrogative in the sense of drawing attention, with a counterpart to the alif implied, its implied form being "Is the one who is devoutly obedient, doing such and such, like one who is otherwise?". What shows the omission is His saying {قل هَل يَسْتَوِي الَّذين يعلمُونَ وَالَّذين لَا يعلمُونَ}; and this is stronger.

Whoever read أمّن with doubling has made أم enter upon من, and he too implies a counterpart for it before it, the implied form being "Are those who disobey their Lord better, or the one who is devoutly obedient?". من is then in the sense of الذي (relative noun), not an interrogative, because أم does not enter upon what is an interrogative, since it is itself for interrogation. What shows this omission is أم's need for a counterpart, and His saying {هَل يَسْتَوِي الَّذين يعلمُونَ وَالَّذين لَا يعلمُونَ} also shows it.

[Translator's note: أمّن هو قانت is in āya 9, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:10-10.t: His saying {للَّذين أَحْسنُوا فِي هَذِه الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَة}: (حسنة) is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and what precedes it — the prepositional phrase — is the khabar (predicate). في is attached (mutaʿalliq) to أحسنوا on the view that حسنة is Paradise and the recompense in the Hereafter; or it is attached to حسنة on the view that the "good" is what the servant is given in this world of what is desirable in it. It has also been said that it is what he is given of Allah's friendship toward him and His love for him, and recompense in this world. The first is better, because this world is not the abode of recompense.

mekki-muskil:28-28.t: His saying {قُرْآنًا عَرَبيا}: قرآنا is a preparatory element (tawṭiʾa) for the ḥāl (circumstantial), and عربيا is the ḥāl. It has also been said that قرآنا is a tawkīd (emphasis) of what precedes it and عربيا is a ḥāl from القرآن.

mekki-muskil:44-44.t:
His saying {الشَّفَاعَة جَمِيعًا}: (جميعا) is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). جميع came though there is only a singular word before it, because الشفاعة is a maṣdar (verbal noun) indicating little and much, so جميع was construed according to the sense.

His saying وحده is accusative as a maṣdar according to Sībawayh and al-Khalīl, and a ḥāl according to Yūnus.

His saying أن تقول نفس: أن is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose).

His saying {أفغير الله تأمروني أعبد}: غير is accusative, governed by أعبد, its implied form being "Say: is it other than Allah that I should worship, in what you command me?". It has also been said that it is accusative, governed by تأمروني, by omission of the preposition, its implied form being "Say: do you command me to the worship of other than Allah?", in what you command me; because أعبد is originally أن أعبد, but أن was dropped and (the verb) became nominative. It (أن) is thus implied in the speech, and it is a badal (substitute) for غير, so it must take its place in the implied form; and it together with the verb is a maṣdar. That is why the implied form was "Say: do you command me to the worship of other than Allah?". Had أن been overt, it would not be permissible to put غير in the accusative by أعبد, because it would then be within the ṣila (relative clause), and you would have placed it before the relative element. Putting it in the accusative by أعبد is clearer than putting it in the accusative by تأمروني.

[Translator's note: وحده is in āya 45, أن تقول نفس in āya 56 (the source has «نفسا») and أفغير الله in āya 64, though all are printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:66-66.t: His saying {بل الله فاعبد}: (الله) is accusative, governed by اعبد. Al-Kisāʾī and al-Farrāʾ said it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "rather worship Allah; so worship (Him)". The fāʾ is for requital (mujāzāt) according to Abū Isḥāq, and redundant (zāʾida) according to al-Akhfash.

mekki-muskil:67-67.t:
His saying {وَالْأَرْض جَمِيعًا قَبضته}: a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate), and جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial). Al-Farrāʾ allowed قبضتَه in the accusative in (ordinary) speech, on the assumption that the preposition was omitted, i.e. "in His grasp". That is not permissible according to the Basrans: if you said زيد قبضتَك, meaning "in your grasp", it would not be permissible.

His saying {وَالسَّمَاوَات مَطْوِيَّات بِيَمِينِهِ}: a mubtadaʾ and khabar. In (ordinary) speech مطويّاتٍ in the accusative is permissible as a ḥāl, with بيمينه then being the khabar.

mekki-muskil:71-71.t:
His saying {إِلَى جَهَنَّم زمرا}: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

His saying {جاؤوها فتحت}: it has been said that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida) and فتحت is the answer of إذا. It has also been said that the wāw indicates the opening of the gates of Paradise before those who feared Allah come to it, and the answer is omitted, i.e. "until, when they come to it, they are safe". It has also been said that the answer is وقال لهم خزنتها, with the wāw redundant.

[Translator's note: the wāw discussion (وفتحت) concerns āya 73, about Paradise, though it is printed under this entry.]

mekki-muskil:75-75.t: His saying حافّين is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), because ترى is from seeing with the eye. The singular of حافّين is حافّ. Al-Farrāʾ said it has no singular, because this noun applies to them only when they are gathered together.

muyesser-irab:53-53.t:
﴿قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله﴾: قل: an imperative verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on sukūn, and the fāʿil (agent) is "أنت" (you); يا: a vocative particle; عبادي: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative (manṣūb) with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause ﴿يا عبادي﴾ is in the position of accusative as the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); الذين: a relative noun, mabnī on fatḥa, in the position of accusative as a naʿt (adjective) of عبادي; أسرفوا: a past verb, mabnī on ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿أسرفوا..﴾ is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun, a clause with no grammatical position. على أنفسهم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أسرفوا﴾; لا: prohibitive (nāhiya); تقنطوا: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لا, the sign of its jussive being the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; من رحمة: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿تقنطوا﴾, and the Divine Name is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause ﴿لا تقنطوا﴾ is resumptive (mustaʾnafa), with no grammatical position, and it is the answer to the vocative; and the clause ﴿قل يا عبادي...﴾ is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم﴾: إن: an abrogating particle (ḥarf nāsikh); الله: the Divine Name, the ism (noun) of إن, accusative with fatḥa; يغفر: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) with ḍamma; الذنوب: mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جميعًا: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, from الذنوب; the clause ﴿يغفر..﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of إن; the clause ﴿إن الله يغفر﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is causal (taʿlīliyya); إنه: إن: an abrogating particle, and the hāʾ is the ism of إن; هو: a pronoun, mabnī on fatḥa, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), or of accusative as a tawkīd (emphasis) of the ism of إن; الغفور: the khabar of إن, or of هو, nominative with ḍamma; الرحيم: a second khabar, nominative with ḍamma; the clause ﴿إنه هو الغفور﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is causal.

muyesser-irab:54-54.t:
﴿وأنيبوا﴾: the wāw: conjunctive; أنيبوا: an imperative verb, mabnī on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent).
﴿إلى ربكم﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنيبوا﴾; the clause ﴿أنيبوا﴾ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause ﴿لا تقنطوا﴾.
﴿وأسلموا﴾: the wāw: conjunctive; أسلموا: an imperative verb, mabnī on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil.
﴿له﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿أسلموا﴾.
﴿من قبل﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿أن يأتيكم﴾: a maṣdar-forming, subjunctive-governing particle; يأتيكم: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن; كم: in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يأتيكم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿العذاب﴾: a postponed fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) with ḍamma.
﴿ثم﴾: a conjunction for sequence with delay.
﴿لا﴾ negating.
﴿تنصرون﴾: an imperfect verb, passive, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause ﴿لا تنصرون﴾ is conjoined to an implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), i.e.: "if it comes upon you, you will be punished".

muyesser-irab:55-55.t:
﴿واتبعوا أحسن ما أنزل إليكم من ربكم﴾: the wāw: conjunctive; اتبعوا: an imperative verb, mabnī (indeclinable) on the dropping of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); أحسن: mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of ﴿اتبعوا﴾, accusative (manṣūb) with fatḥa; ما: a relative noun, mabnī, in the position of genitive as muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); أنزل: a past verb, passive, mabnī on fatḥa, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is "هو"; إليكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿أنزل﴾; the clause ﴿أنزل إليكم﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun; من ربكم: a preposition and its genitive noun, also attached to أنزل; the clause ﴿اتبعوا..﴾ is maʿṭūf (conjoined) to the clause ﴿أسلموا..﴾.
﴿من قبل أن يأتيكم العذاب بغتة وأنتم لا تشعرون﴾: من قبل: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); أن: a maṣdar-forming, subjunctive-governing particle; يأتيكم: an imperfect verb, accusative by أن; كم: a pronoun, mabnī, in the position of accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن يأتيكم﴾ is muḍāf ilayhi; العذاب: fāʿil, nominative (marfūʿ) with ḍamma; بغتة: a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of a ḥāl, i.e. "taking you suddenly"; the wāw: circumstantial (ḥāliyya); أنتم: a pronoun, mabnī, in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject); لا: negating; تشعرون: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause ﴿لا تشعرون﴾ is in the position of nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أنتم; and the clause ﴿أنتم لا تشعرون﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.

muyesser-irab:56-56.t:
﴿أن تقول نفس يا حسرتا على ما فرطت في جنب الله﴾: أن: a maṣdar-forming, subjunctive-governing particle; تقول: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, the sign of its accusative being the fatḥa; نفس: fāʿil (agent), nominative (marfūʿ) with ḍamma; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿أن تقول﴾ is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose) with a muḍāf omitted, i.e. "for fear (كراهةَ) that [a soul] should say"; the clause ﴿تقول...﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila of ﴿أن﴾; يا: a vocative particle; حسرتا: the one addressed (munādā), a muḍāf, accusative with an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the letter before the yāʾ that has turned into an alif, and the yāʾ turned into an alif is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). على: a preposition; ما: maṣdar-forming or relative, mabnī (indeclinable) on sukūn, in the position of genitive, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) ﴿حسرتا﴾; the interpreted maṣdar from ﴿ما فرطت﴾ is genitive by على, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to ﴿حسرتا﴾. في جنب: a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to ﴿فرطت﴾; الله: the Divine Name, muḍāf ilayhi, genitive; the clause ﴿فرطت..﴾ has no grammatical position, because it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun.
﴿وإن كنت لمن الساخرين﴾: the wāw: circumstantial; إن: lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), inoperative (muhmala); كنت: كان is an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is its ism (noun); the lām is the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); من: a preposition; الساخرين: a noun, genitive with the yāʾ, because it is a sound masculine plural; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of ﴿كنت﴾; the clause ﴿وإن كنت لمن الساخرين﴾ is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).
