فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضى عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ: the reading of Yaḥyā ibn Waththāb, al-Aʿmash, Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī is فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضى عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ ] «[Translator's note: i.e. قُضِيَ عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتُ; the source prints the standard vowelling, followed by a stray bracket.]» as [a verb] whose agent is not named (passive). The meaning is the same, except that the first reading is clearer and more consistent with the arrangement of the speech, because they agreed on «ويرسل» and did not read ويُرسَل [in the passive]. The reason for the fatḥa of the wāw in His saying, Majestic and Mighty:
أَوَلَوْ كانُوا لا يَمْلِكُونَ شَيْئاً وَلا يَعْقِلُونَ has already been given in the book before this.

nahhas-irab:44-44.t: [جميعا] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial). If it is said: جميع applies only to two or more, while intercession is one — the answer is that الشفاعة is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and a maṣdar stands for two and for a plural.

nahhas-irab:45-45.t: وَإِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ: [وحده] is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh, and as a ḥāl (circumstantial) according to Yūnus. Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: اشْمَأَزَّتْ, that is, shrank [in aversion].

nahhas-irab:46-46.t: قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ: accusative because it is a vocative in construct; likewise عالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ. According to Sībawayh it is not permissible for it to be a naʿt (adjective) [of اللهمّ].

nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
Among that is His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ﴾.
The meaning may be: the sending down of the Book is from Allah [Translator's note: i.e. "from Allah" is its khabar (predicate)].
Or the meaning may be: this is the sending down of the Book.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ ٱلْكِتَابَ بِٱلْحَقِّ فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ﴾.
That is: in accordance with what was made true in the [earlier] scriptures about its being sent down to you.
And the meaning may be: He made it binding upon you, by His right over you and over His creation.
And it is said that the meaning is: it commands justice and truth.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَٱعْبُدِ ٱللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَّهُ ٱلدِّينَ﴾.
That is: do not worship anything else along with Him.
And al-Farrāʾ related ﴿لَهُ الدِّينُ﴾ with al-dīn in the nominative.
And it is wrong from three angles:
The first: that after it comes ﴿ألاَ لِلَّهِ الدينُ الخَالِصُ﴾, which makes this unnecessary.
Also: it has not been read so.
Also: it makes ﴿مُخْلِصاً﴾ the full stop (al-tamām), whereas the full stop at the end of the verse is more fitting.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلاَ لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْخَالِصُ﴾.
That is: He alone is to be worshipped, because among people there are those who have a religion but do not make it purely for Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda: ﴿أَلاَ لِلَّهِ ٱلدِّينُ ٱلْخَالِصُ﴾: he said: "There is no god but Allah."
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَآءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلاَّ لِيُقَرِّبُونَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ زُلْفَىۤ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, a rank.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: that is, only so that they intercede for us.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and in the reading of Ibn Masʿūd, Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid: ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ قَالُوا مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إلاَّ لِيُقَرّبُونَا إلى اللهِ زُلْفَى﴾.
And in the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy: ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أوْليَاءَ مَا نَعْبُدُكُمْ إلاَّ ليقرِّبُونَا إلَى اللهِ زُلْفَى﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the reported speech (ḥikāya) in this is clear [Translator's note: i.e. an implied "saying" introduces their words].

nahhas-meani:4-4.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّوْ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً لاَّصْطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُ﴾.
The connection of this with the preceding indicates that these are among those who took protectors besides Allah.
And ﴿لاَّصْطَفَىٰ﴾: He would have chosen.

nahhas-meani:5-5.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يُكَوِّرُ ٱللَّيْـلَ عَلَى ٱلنَّهَـارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ ٱلنَّـهَارَ عَلَى ٱللَّيْلِ﴾.
Qatāda said: that is, He casts this over that, and that over this.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the root meaning of al-takwīr in the language is wrapping and gathering together; from it is kawr al-ʿimāma (the winding of the turban), and from it is ﴿إذا الشَّمْسُ كُوِّرَتْ﴾.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾.
﴿ثُمَّ﴾ here indicates that the second statement comes after the first.
And Qatāda said: ﴿ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا﴾ is Ḥawwāʾ; He created her from one of his ribs.
And it is said: His creating the mate is referred back to "one", i.e. to a soul on its own [Translator's note: i.e. "who created you from a single soul, alone, then made from it its mate"], then He made from it its mate.
That is, kinds [Translator's note: this gloss evidently belongs to the omitted continuation of the verse, ﴿وَأَنزَلَ لَكُم مِّنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾].
Mujāhid said: of camels two, of cattle two, of sheep two and of goats two.
Qatāda said: it is like the one in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُـمْ خَلْقاً مِّن بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ﴾.
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: a drop, then a clinging clot, then a lump of flesh, until the creation is complete.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ ثَلاَثٍ﴾.
Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: in the darkness of the womb, in the darkness of the placenta, and in the darkness of the belly.
And it is said: in the loins, then in the womb, then in the belly; this is the view of Abū ʿUbayda, and the first is sounder.

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِن تَكْفُرُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنكُمْ، وَلاَ يَرْضَىٰ لِعِبَادِهِ ٱلْكُفْرَ، وَإِن يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ﴾.
That is: He is pleased with gratitude for you; and ﴿تَشْكُرُواْ﴾ indicated the [noun] gratitude [to which the pronoun refers] [Translator's note: the verse is quoted in the text as «وَإِن يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ»; the Qurʾānic wording is ﴿وَإِن تَشْكُرُواْ يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ﴾].

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَا رَبَّهُ مُنِيباً إِلَيْهِ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: sincere.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says anāba when he returned and repented.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلَهُ نِعْمَةً مِّنْهُ نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوۤ إِلَيْهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
That is: He gave it to him and made it freely his; and Abū ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAlāʾ used to recite:
هُنَالِكَ إنْ يُسْتَخْوَلُوا المَالَ - يُخْوِلُوا * وإن يُسْأَلُوا يُعْطُوا، وإن يَيْسِرُوا يُغْلُوا
(There, if they are asked to bestow wealth, they bestow; if asked, they give; and if they cast lots at the gaming, they pay high.)
Then He said: ﴿نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُوۤ إِلَيْهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
That is: he forgot that for which he used to call on Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, before.
And the meaning may be: he forgot Allah whom he used to call on, as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ أَنْتُمْ عَابِدُونَ مَا أَعْبُدُ﴾.
And in His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلاً﴾ there is the meaning of threat.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَندَاداً لِّيُضِلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِ﴾.
Al-Suddī said: the rivals are men whom he obeys in acts of disobedience.
And it is said: he worshipped idols.
And this is nearer to what is correct, because that is in the context of Allah's, Mighty and Majestic is He, reproaching them for worshipping them.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ سَاجِداً وَقَآئِماً﴾.
That is: praying; and al-qunūt is obedience.
Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda said: ﴿آنَآءَ ٱللَّيْلِ﴾ means its hours: its beginning, its middle and its end.
Abū Jaʿfar said: al-Akhfash said: the reading of whoever read ﴿أَمَّنْ هُوَ﴾? without doubling [i.e. «أَمَنْ»] is weak in Arabic, because the alif of interrogation does not lean on what precedes it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: what al-Akhfash said is good; indicating it is that the one in Sūrat al-Naml was only read with doubling. And the meaning of his statement is that the speech leans on what precedes it; it has no khabar (predicate), but what precedes it indicates it, because He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَنْدَاداً لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾.
So He omitted the khabar, because the meaning is: Is one who is obedient like this one?
Or: Is one who is obedient better, or this one?
And this is the place of the ﴿أَمْ﴾ that means "bal", as the poet said:
أَفَتِلْكَ أَمْ وَحْشِيَّةٌ مَسْبُوْعَةٌ * خَذَلَتْ وَهَادِيَةُ الصِّوَارِ قِوَامُهَا
(Is it that one, or a wild cow whose calf the beasts of prey have taken, who lagged behind, while the herd's leader is her mainstay?)
And his saying:
أذلك أم جَأْبٌ يُطَارِدُ آتُناً * حَمَلْنَ فَأَدْنَى حَمْلِهِنَّ دُرُوْصُ
(Is it that, or a thick-set wild ass chasing she-asses that have conceived, the nearest of whose pregnancies is about to give birth?)
And for whoever reads without doubling, the khabar is also omitted; and this is something subtle in Arabic, with which only one practised in it is at ease, as the poet said:
فَأُقْسِمُ لَوْشَيْءٌ أتانَا رَسُوْلُهُ * سِوَاكَ، وَلَكِنْ لَمْ نَجِدْ لَكَ مَدْفَعاً
(I swear, had anything other than you sent its messenger to us — but we found no way to repel you.)
That is: "we would have repelled it"; the omission occurs in this way.
And it is said: it is a vocative (nidāʾ), i.e. "O you who stand [in prayer] in the hours of the night."
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يَحْذَرُ ٱلآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُواْ رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr read ﴿يَحْذَرُ عَذَابَ الآخِرَةِ﴾, and the meaning is the same.
That is [Translator's note: this explains the following phrase of the verse, ﴿قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾]: just as the knowing and the ignorant are not equal, so the obedient and the disobedient are not equal.
And it is said: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ what is theirs in obedience and what is against them in disobedience.
Then He said ﴿إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾, i.e. [those of] intellects.
And the lubb of everything is its pure essence.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُواْ فِي هَـٰذِهِ ٱلدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَاسِعَةٌ﴾.
It is said: the good is the Garden.
And it is said the meaning is: they have good in this world, i.e. good praise, and tranquillity in what they have.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَرْضُ ٱللَّهِ وَاسِعَةٌ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, so emigrate, and keep away from the idols.

nahhas-meani:15-15.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَٱعْبُدُواْ مَا شِئْتُمْ مِّن دُونِهِ﴾.
[It is] by way of threat, and this was before the command to fight.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ ٱلْخَاسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوۤاْ أَنفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
That is: they lost themselves by being consigned forever to the Fire, and their families by not entering the Garden, where they would have had families.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: there is no one but Allah has prepared for him a family in the Garden, if he obeys Him.

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ ٱللَّهُ بِهِ عِبَادَهُ يٰعِبَادِ فَٱتَّقُونِ﴾.
That is: that punishment which has been described.

nahhas-meani:17-17.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱجْتَنَبُواْ ٱلطَّاغُوتَ أَن يَعْبُدُوهَا﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: al-ṭāghūt is the devils.
Abū Jaʿfar said: we have explained this in Sūrat al-Baqara.

nahhas-meani:18-18.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَبَشِّرْ عِبَادِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ فَيَـتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُ﴾.
There are two views on the meaning of this:
The first view: al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿يَسْتَمِعُونَ ٱلْقَوْلَ﴾ is the Qurʾān, and ﴿أَحْسَنَهُ﴾ is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, commanded the prophets of obedience to Him, so they follow it.
And the other view: that they listen to the Qurʾān and to other things, and follow the Qurʾān.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the first view is good, and the meaning is: when they hear of punishment and pardon, they pardon, and consider pardon to be better, even if the punishment is their right.

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ ٱلْعَذَابِ أَفَأَنتَ تُنقِذُ مَن فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾? [verse 19].
It is asked: how can two interrogatives be brought, when the grammarians are agreed that two interrogatives are not permissible in a noun and its khabar (predicate)?
There are two answers to this:
One of them: that when the speech grows long, the Arabs repeat [it] for emphasis (tawkīd); and Sībawayh said the same about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَيَعِدُكُمْ أَنَّكُمْ إِذَا مِتُّمْ، وَكُنْتُمْ تُرَابَاً وَعِظَاماً، أَنَّكُمْ مُخْرَجُونَ﴾?
The meaning on this [view] is: Is the one against whom the word of punishment has become due — will you then rescue him?
And the speech is a condition and its apodosis (jawāb), and the interrogative was brought to indicate making [the addressee] stop and acknowledge (al-tawqīf wa-l-taqrīr).
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is: Will you rescue one against whom the word of punishment has become due?
Abū Jaʿfar said: this and the first are one.
And the other answer: that there is an omission in the speech.
And the meaning is: Will the one against whom the word of punishment has become due get free, or be saved?
Then He omitted the answer, and what comes after it is resumptive.
And the meaning is: Will the one of whom it is preceded in the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, that he will enter the Fire be saved or get free?

nahhas-meani:21-21.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنَابِيعَ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It is narrated that all water in the earth has its origin in the sky.
And it may be that His sending it down is His creating it and bringing it into being by His command.
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَسَلَكَهُ﴾ means He made it enter and made it ﴿يَنَابِيعَ﴾, the plural of yanbūʿ, on the pattern "yafʿūl" from nabaʿa, yanbaʿu (to spring forth).
﴿ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعاً مُّخْتَلِفاً أَلْوَانُهُ﴾, i.e. green, black, yellow and white.
﴿ثُمَّ يَهِـيجُ فَـتَرَاهُ مُصْفَـرّاً﴾, i.e. it dries up.
Al-Aṣmaʿī said: it is said of a plant when its drying is complete: qad hāja, yahīju, hayjan.
﴿ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطَاماً﴾, i.e. crumbled debris.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَىٰ لأُوْلِي ٱلأَلْبَابِ﴾.
That is: they reflect, and so they remember that this points to the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and His power.

nahhas-meani:22-22.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن شَرَحَ ٱللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ فَهُوَ عَلَىٰ نُورٍ مِّن رَّبِّهِ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech.
And the meaning is: Is one whose breast Allah has opened, so that he is guided, like one upon whose heart He has set a seal, so that he is not guided?!
And in the ḥadīth, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Does the heart then expand? He said: Yes; when Allah brings light into it, it expands and becomes spacious. They said: Is there a sign of that? He said: Yes:
* withdrawing from the abode of delusion,
* turning to the abode of eternity,
* and preparing for death before [meeting] death."
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِّن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ، أُوْلَـٰئِكَ فِي ضَلاَلٍ مُّبِينٍ﴾.
It is said: the meaning of ﴿مِن﴾ and "ʿan" here is the same.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is nothing; the meaning of ﴿مِّن﴾ is: when His verses are recited to them they grow hard [i.e. because of them], as He the Exalted said: ﴿وَأَمَّا الَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزَادَتْهُمْ رِجْساً إِلى رِجْسِهِمْ﴾.
And if one says "ʿan", its meaning is: their hearts grew hard and turned away from accepting the remembrance of Allah.

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ كِتَاباً مُّتَشَابِهاً﴾.
Al-Shaʿbī narrated from ʿAwn ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: they said: O Messenger of Allah, tell us something. So there was revealed ﴿ٱللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ ٱلْحَدِيثِ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿مُّتَشَابِهاً﴾ means it is not inconsistent.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning is that its parts resemble one another in wisdom and truth, as He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَلَوْ كَانَ مِنْ عِندِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ لَوَجَدُواْ فِيهِ اخْتِلاَفاً كَثِيراً﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿مَّثَانِيَ﴾.
Qatāda said: ﴿مَثَانِي﴾: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, repeated it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning is: that in which the stories, the reward and the punishment are repeated.
And it is said: al-mathānī is every sūra containing fewer than a hundred verses, i.e. they are repeated in prayer.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ، ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
That is: they shiver at the verses in which punishment is mentioned, then they soften at the verses in which mercy is mentioned.

nahhas-meani:24-24.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَفَمَن يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوۤءَ ٱلْعَذَابِ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾.
There is an omission in the speech.
And the meaning is: Is one who shields himself with his face from the evil of the punishment like one who enters the Garden?
Mujāhid said: he falls on his face into the punishment on the Day of Resurrection.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and it is narrated that he is thrown into the Fire shackled, so he cannot shield himself from the Fire except with his face.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ، لَّعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: that is, without ambiguity.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is that it is straight, its parts not contradicting one another, because a crooked thing is inconsistent.
And it has been narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ﴾: not created.

nahhas-meani:29-29.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلاً رَّجُلاً فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾.
Qatāda said: he is the disbeliever, and the partners are the devils.
He said: ﴿وَرَجُلاً سَلَماً﴾ is the believer, who works for Allah alone.
Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: this is a parable for truth and falsehood, and the partners are the idols.
Al-Farrāʾ said: ﴿مُتَشَاكِسُونَ﴾: at odds with one another.
Abū Jaʿfar said: whoever read ﴿رَجُلاً سَالِماً﴾ took it according to the verb [i.e. as an active participle], and whoever read ﴿سَلَماً﴾ made it a maṣdar (verbal noun), so its meaning is: one of complete belonging (dhā salam).

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ عِندَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾.
That is: the wronged will dispute with the wrongdoer, and the believer with the disbeliever.
Ibn ʿUmar said: we did not know what we would dispute about, until the civil strife (al-fitna) occurred, and we said: this is it.
And in the ḥadīth: al-Zubayr said: O Messenger of Allah, "shall we dispute on the Day of Resurrection after what was between us? He said: Yes, until to everyone who has a right his right is rendered. He said: then the matter is indeed severe."

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾.
Bakr ibn Sahl narrated to us: Abū Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ﴾, he says: he came with "There is no god but Allah"; ﴿وَصَدَّق بِهِ﴾ means [he believed] in the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ﴿أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْمُتَّقُونَ﴾, he says: they guarded themselves against associating partners [with Allah].
And Ibn ʿUyayna narrated from Manṣūr, who said: I said to Mujāhid: O Abū al-Ḥajjāj, what is the meaning of His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾? [verse 33].
He said: the one who came with the Qurʾān and believed in it.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this resembles the first view, and it is the view of most linguists.
And what indicates its correctness is that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read ﴿والَّذينَ جاءوا بالصِّدقِ وصَدَّقُوا به، أولئك هم المتَّقُونَ﴾.
So ﴿الَّذِي﴾ here and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ are one.
And al-Ḥasan said: he is the believer, who comes with the truth on the Day of Resurrection, and believed in it in this world.
And some linguists say: the nūn was dropped from ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ because of the length of the noun [with its ṣila (relative clause)].
And some of them say: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is in the sense of "alladhīna" (those who).
And some of them say: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is a singular that conveys the meaning of a group.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and this view is the soundest of them: ﴿الَّذِي﴾ is like "man" (whoever), because no particular individual is intended by it; and its true sense is that the meaning is: "and the party that came with the truth and believed in it."
And other than this has been said about the verse.
Qatāda and Abū al-ʿĀliya said: the one who came with the truth is the Prophet ﷺ, and Abū Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, [is the one who believed in it].
And it is said: the Prophet ﷺ and ʿAlī, peace be upon him.
ʿAlī ibn Saʿīd narrated to us: al-Ḥusayn ibn Naṣr narrated to us: my father narrated to me: ʿUmar ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujāhid: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي جَآءَ بِٱلصِّدْقِ﴾ is Muḥammad ﷺ, ﴿وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾ is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him.
And a parallel to "alladhī jāʾa bi-l-ṣidq", in its being a singular conveying [the meaning of] a group, is the poet's saying:
وإنَّ الَّذِي حَانَتْ بِفَلْجٍ دِمَاؤُهُمْ * هُمُ القَوْمُ كُلُّ القَوْمِ يَا أُمَّ خَالِد
(Those whose blood was spilt at Falj are the people, the people indeed, O Umm Khālid.)
And he dropped the nūn [Translator's note: i.e. in the dual relative «اللذا» for «اللذان»] in his saying:
أَبَنِي كُلَيْبٍ إنَّ عَمَيَّ اللَّذَا * قَتَلا المُلُوكَ وفَكَّكا الأَغْلاَلاَ
(O sons of Kulayb, my two uncles are the ones who killed kings and broke the fetters.)

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَلَيْسَ ٱللَّهُ بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِ﴾.
This indicates [promised] help; and most of the Kufans read ﴿بكافٍ عِبَادَهُ﴾.
And the singular is better, because it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ is meant by it, and indicating this is ﴿وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: [those besides Him are] the idols.
Qatāda said: Khālid ibn al-Walīd took an axe to it [Translator's note: the text reads «أخذها خالد… فأساً»] and came to "al-ʿUzzā" to break it, and its custodian said to him: its force cannot be withstood, so beware of it. But he went on until he broke its nose.
And it is narrated that they said to the Prophet ﷺ: if you do not stop reviling them, we will command them to drive you mad.
Mujāhid said: this verse was revealed when the Prophet ﷺ recited Sūrat al-Najm at the door of the Kaʿba.

nahhas-meani:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ يٰقَوْمِ ٱعْمَلُواْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُـمْ إِنِّي عَامِلٌ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُـمْ﴾ means according to your way.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is a correct view.
And the meaning is: according to your way which you have chosen and which has become firmly established with you.
﴿إِنِّي عَامِلٌ﴾: the meaning is: I am working according to my way; then [this] was omitted.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ٱللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى ٱلأَنفُسَ حِينَ مِوْتِـهَا وَٱلَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِـهَا﴾.
Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra narrated from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: the souls of the living and the souls of the dead are gathered, and they become acquainted with one another as long as Allah wills; then He withholds the one for which He has decreed death, and sends the other back to its body.
Al-Farrāʾ said: the meaning is ﴿وَٱلَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِـهَا﴾ [He takes] at the end of its term; and he said: "tawaffāhā" may mean He put it to sleep.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and it is said that the meaning is: Allah takes the souls at the time of their death by removing their breath and their discernment; then a verb was implied for the second, because it differs from the first.
So the meaning is: and He takes the one that has not died, in its sleep, by removing its discernment only, because the sleeper breathes.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the best that has been said on this is that ﴿يَتَوَفَّى﴾ and "yastawfī" have one meaning, [said] when a thing is taken in full, just as one says tabayyantu and istabantu, and tayaqqana and istayqana; so the dead person and the sleeper are one in this respect; and what indicates it is His saying ﴿فَيُمْسِكُ ٱلَّتِي قَضَىٰ عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ، وَيُرْسِلُ ٱلأُخْرَىٰ إِلَىٰ أَجَلٍ مُّسَمًّى﴾.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَمِ ٱتَّخَذُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ شُفَعَآءَ قُلْ أَوَلَوْ كَـانُواْ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ شَيْئاً وَلاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: they said: we worshipped them only so that they would intercede for us.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَوَلَوْ كَـانُواْ لاَ يَمْلِكُونَ شَيْئاً وَلاَ يَعْقِلُونَ﴾.
Sībawayh said: this is the chapter of the wāw when the alif of interrogation enters upon it; that is your saying: "Is So-and-so with So-and-so?", and he says: "Is he one who would be with So-and-so?"
Abū al-ʿAbbās [al-Mubarrad] said: this is by way of seeking guidance, or by way of disapproval; and what occurs of it in the Qurʾān means disapproval, affirmation (taqrīr), and the [actual] occurrence of the thing.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُل لِلَّهِ ٱلشَّفَاعَةُ جَمِيعاً﴾.
As He the Exalted said: ﴿مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلاَّ بِإِذْنِهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ ٱللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ ٱشْمَأَزَّتْ قُلُوبُ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿ٱشْمَأَزَّتْ﴾: they were arrogant and disbelieved.
And Ibn Abī Najīḥ narrated from Mujāhid, who said: they shrank.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says ishmaʾazza min kadhā when he recoiled from it.
And it is narrated that when they heard someone say "There is no god but Allah alone", they recoiled and said: our gods have not been mentioned.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَبَدَا لَهُمْ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ مَا لَمْ يَكُونُواْ يَحْتَسِبُونَ﴾.
It is narrated that they did deeds which they imagined would benefit them, but they did not benefit them, because they were associators.

nahhas-meani:49-49.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا مَسَّ ٱلإِنسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَانَا، ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلْنَاهُ نِعْمَةً مِّنَّا﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿خَوَّلْنَاهُ﴾: We gave him.
Abū Jaʿfar said: one says khawwaltuhu kadhā, i.e. I gave it to him as a favour, not as a recompense.
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَالَ إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: ﴿إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَىٰ عِلْمٍ﴾ means on account of honour.
And Qatāda said: that is, on account of good that is in me.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: I have knowledge of earning, whether by trade or otherwise, so I knew that I would be given this.
And among the best that has been said on it: that the meaning is: I knew, when I was given this in this world, that I have a rank with Allah; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, rejected this from him and said: ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أنَّ اللهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ مِهَ القُرُونِ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the text; the wording is that of Q 28:78, ﴿أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ قَدْ أَهْلَكَ مِن قَبْلِهِ مِنَ ٱلْقُرُونِ﴾, with «مِهَ» presumably a misprint for «مِنَ»] — the verse.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He does not give wealth to everyone who has a rank.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ﴾.
That is: rather, the gift is a trial by which the servant is tested, so that it becomes manifest from him whether he is grateful or ungrateful.

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ يٰعِبَادِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُواْ عَلَىٰ أَنفُسِهِمْ لاَ تَقْنَطُواْ مِن رَّحْمَةِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Mujāhid narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: it was revealed concerning "Waḥshī", the killer of Ḥamza — peace be upon Ḥamza — up to the completion of three verses. The Prophet ﷺ could not bear to look at him, so he thought that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, had not accepted his Islam from him; so these three verses were revealed.
And Ibrāhīm al-Taymī narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās that he used to read: ﴿قُلْ يَا عِبَادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لاَ تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللهِ، إِنَّ اللهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبِ جَمِيعاً لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ﴾.
And he said: it was revealed concerning the killer of Ḥamza and his kind; so he said.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and likewise it is narrated that it is [so] in the codex of Ibn Masʿūd.
And the meaning of ﴿لا تَقْنَطُواْ﴾ is: do not despair.
Qatāda said: ﴿وأنِيبُوا إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ﴾ means turn [to Him] and work for Him.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱتَّبِعُـوۤاْ أَحْسَنَ مَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُم مِّن رَّبِّكُـمْ مِّن قَبْلِ أَن يَأْتِيَكُـمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ بَغْتَةً﴾.
And all of it is good, so there are several views on this:
a- Among them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has permitted retaliation — after wrong has been done — and pardon, and pardon is better.
b- Among them: that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has informed about a people that they obeyed and about a people that they disobeyed, and commanded that we follow obedience.
c- Among them: that it is the abrogating [text].
d- Among them: that the meaning is: the good among what was sent down to you.
And ﴿بَغْتَةً﴾ means suddenly.

nahhas-meani:56-56.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أَن تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يٰحَسْرَتَا عَلَىٰ مَا فَرَّطَتُ فِي جَنبِ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
The meaning is: do this for fear that a soul should say, and in dislike that a soul should say, "Alas, my regret!"
And al-ḥasra is remorse, i.e. there befalls a person that with which he becomes ḥasīr, i.e. worn out [Translator's note: the text has «معيباً»; perhaps «مُعْيِياً», exhausted]; and the vocative particle indicates that it is something inseparable, i.e. "O regret, this is your time"; this is the position of Sībawayh.
Mujāhid said: ﴿فِي جَنبِ ٱللَّهِ﴾ means in the matter of Allah.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning is: in the side of Allah's command, by way of figurative representation (tamthīl).
That is: on the path that leads to the truth, which is faith.

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلَىٰ قَدْ جَآءَتْكَ آيَاتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا وَٱسْتَكْبَرْتَ وَكُنتَ مِنَ ٱلْكَافِرِينَ﴾.
﴿بَلَىٰ﴾ in the speech of the Arabs occurs only after a negation, and there is no negation in the speech, but its meaning is there, because the meaning of ﴿لَوْ أنَّ اللهَ هَدَانِي﴾ is: Allah did not guide me.
And al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas narrated from Umm Salama that the Prophet ﷺ read: ﴿بَلَى قَدْ جَاءَتْكِ آياتِي، فَكَذَّبْتِ بِهَا وَاسْتَكْبَرْتِ، وَكُنْتِ مِنَ الكَافِرِينَ﴾ [i.e. with the feminine kasra on the tāʾ].
And the reading of al-Aʿmash is ﴿بَلَى قَدْ جَاءَتْهُ آيَاتِي﴾, and this indicates the masculine.
And al-Rabīʿ ibn Anas did not meet Umm Salama; nevertheless the reading is permissible, because "nafs" (soul) applies to the masculine and the feminine.
And some of them rejected this reading, saying: if he puts kasra on the tāʾ, he must say "wa-kunti min al-kawāfir" or "min al-kāfirāt".
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not binding; do you not see that before it is ﴿أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ﴾, then He said ﴿وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنْ السَّاخِرِينَ﴾, and did not say "min al-sawākhir", nor "min al-sākhirāt"?
And the implied construction (taqdīr) in Arabic with kasra on the tāʾ is: "and you (f.) were arrogant, and were among the whole [company] of mockers", or "among the people who mock", or "among the folk (qawm) who mock"; and "qawm" applies to men and women when they are together, and to men alone, as [the poet] said:
وَمَا أَدْرِي وَسَوفَ إِخَالُ أَدْرِي * أَقَومٌ آلُ حِصْنٍ أَمْ نِسَاءُ
(I do not know — and I think I shall come to know — whether the family of Ḥiṣn are men or women.)

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيُنَجِّي ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْاْ بِمَفَازَتِهِمْ﴾.
That is: by their deliverance from the Fire.
And it is read ﴿بِمَفَازَاتِهِمْ﴾; and the singular is better, because mafāza is in the sense of fawz (success).

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لَّهُ مَقَالِيدُ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَاسِرُونَ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda, who said: ﴿مَقَالِيدُ﴾ means keys.
Abū Jaʿfar said: and the meaning of "His are the keys of the heavens and the earth" is: He is the Creator of what is in them, and the key to its door is in His hand, Mighty and Majestic is He. Then He said: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِـآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ أُوْلَـٰئِكَ هُمُ ٱلْخَاسِرُونَ﴾, i.e. whoever claims that another than He created anything of this has lost and disbelieved.

nahhas-meani:64-64.t:
Then He informed that He alone ought to be worshipped, and said after the proofs:
﴿قُلْ أَفَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ تَأْمُرُونِّيۤ أَعْبُدُ أَيُّهَا ٱلْجَاهِلُونَ﴾.
That is: Is it other than Allah that I should worship, at your command?
This is the view of Sībawayh.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū ʿUbayda holds that the meaning is: they did not know Allah as He truly should be known.
And there is another view on its meaning, namely that the implied construction is: "they did not value the blessings of Allah", then [the muḍāf] was omitted, as He, Glorified is He, said: ﴿وَاسْأَلِ القَرْيَةَ﴾.
* Then He said, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلأَرْضُ جَمِيعـاً قَبْضَـتُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ وَٱلسَّمَاوَاتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: all of this is in His right hand.
Abū Jaʿfar said: the meaning of ﴿وَٱلأَرْضُ جَمِيعـاً قَبْضَـتُهُ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ﴾ is: He owns it, as you say: "this is in my grasp."
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the meaning of ﴿بِيَمِينِهِ﴾ is: by His power, and he recited:
إِذَا مَا رَايَةٌ رُفِعَتْ لِمَجْدٍ * تَلَقَّاهَا عَرَابَةُ باليَمِينِ
(Whenever a banner is raised for glory, ʿArāba receives it with the right hand.)
That is, with strength.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾.
There are two views on its meaning:
One of them: that it is narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked about al-ṣūr, and he said: it is a horn that is blown into.
And Maʿmar narrated from Qatāda concerning His saying ﴿وَنُفِخَ فِي ٱلصُّورِ﴾: he said: into the forms (ṣuwar) of all people.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this is not well known; what is used as the plural of ṣūra is ṣuwar, and no one has read "wa-nufikha fī al-ṣuwar".
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Saʿīd narrated from Qatāda: ﴿فَصَعِقَ﴾: so he died.
And ʿĀṣim narrated from ʿĪsā al-Madanī, who said: I heard ʿAlī ibn Ḥusayn asking Kaʿb al-Aḥbār about His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾, and Kaʿb said: "Jibrāʾīl", "Mīkāʾīl" and "Isrāfīl", the angel of death, and the bearers of the Throne; then Allah causes them to die afterwards.
And Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq narrated from Yazīd al-Raqāshī, from Anas ibn Mālik, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿فَصَعِقَ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَن فِي ٱلأَرْضِ إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾: he said: "Jibrāʾīl, Mīkāʾīl, the bearers of the Throne, the angel of death, and Isrāfīl."
And in this ḥadīth: the last of them to die is Jibrāʾīl ﷺ.
And Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾: they are the martyrs, girded with swords around the Throne.
Abū Jaʿfar said: this does not contradict the first.
And Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ: (The trumpet will be blown, and I shall be the first to rise, and there will be Mūsā ﷺ; and I do not know whether he rose before me, or whether he is among those whom Allah excepted).
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخْرَىٰ فَإِذَا هُمْ قِيَامٌ يَنظُرُونَ﴾.
Abū Hurayra narrated from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Between the two blasts there are forty."
Al-Ḥasan said: I do not know whether it is forty years, or forty months, or forty nights, or forty hours.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَأَشْرَقَتِ ٱلأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّهَا﴾.
This is made clear by the ḥadīth traced back (marfūʿ) to the Prophet ﷺ through many sound chains: (You will look at Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; you will not be wronged in seeing Him).
And it is narrated in four ways: "lā tuḍāmūna", "lā tuḍārūna", "lā tuḍārrūna" and "lā tuḍāmmūna".
So the meaning of (tuḍāmūna) is: no injustice (ḍaym) will befall you, as befalls [people] in this world in looking at kings.
And (lā tuḍārūna): no harm (ḍayr) will befall you.
And (lā tuḍāmmūna): you will not crowd up to one another so that one asks another to show him.
And (lā tuḍārrūna): you will not disagree with one another; one says ḍārartuhu muḍārratan wa-ḍirāran, i.e. I disagreed with him.

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوْاْ رَبَّهُمْ إِلَى ٱلّجَنَّةِ زُمَراً، حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا﴾.
The Kufans hold that the wāw is redundant (zāʾida).
And this is wrong according to the Basrans, because the wāw conveys the meaning of conjunction, and it is not permissible for it to be redundant.
Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said: the meaning is: until, when they came to it and its gates were opened, they were happy [Translator's note: i.e. the apodosis is omitted].
* And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُـمْ طِبْتُمْ فَٱدْخُلُوهَا خَالِدِينَ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: the meaning is: "you have been good, so enter it, abiding forever" — they entered; and this was omitted because the hearer knows it.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿طِبْتُمْ﴾ is: you were good in the world.
And it is narrated from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, peace be upon him, that he said: "They wash in a river in the Garden and drink from it, and no impurity or rancour remains in their insides but it comes out."

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَـالُواْ ٱلْحَـمْدُ للَّهِ ٱلَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعْدَهُ وَأَوْرَثَنَا ٱلأَرْضَ﴾.
Qatāda said: meaning the land of the Garden.

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَقِيلَ ٱلْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
So He concluded with praise, as He began with it.

safi-cedvel:54-59.t:
* I'rab:
(و) a conjunction (إلى ربّكم) attached to (أنيبوا); (له) attached to (أسلموا); (من قبل) attached to the two verbs (أنيبوا وأسلموا); (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative; (ثمّ) a conjunction; and (الواو) in (تنصرون) is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يأتيكم ... ) is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أنيبوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا تقنطوا «[Note: in the previous verse (53).]».
The clause «أسلموا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause لا تقنطوا.
The clause «يأتيكم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «لا تنصرون» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to an implied apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), that is: "so when it comes to you you will be punished, then you will not be helped."
(55) (و) a conjunction; (ما) a relative noun in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi; the nāʾib fāʿil of the verb (أنزل) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, "he", which is the ʿāʾid (the returning pronoun); (إليكم) attached to (أنزل); (من ربّكم) attached to (أنزل); (من قبل ... العذاب) as the first one, and the preposition is attached to (اتّبعوا); (بغتة) a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) standing in for the maṣdar, since it meets it in meaning «[Note: or it is a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "taking by surprise".]»; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (لا) negative.
The clause «اتّبعوا ... » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause أسلموا.
The clause «أنزل ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «يأتيكم العذاب ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «أنتم لا تشعرون» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
The clause «لا تشعرون» is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of the mubtadaʾ (أنتم).
(56) (أن) a maṣdar particle that governs the accusative; (يا) a particle of vocative and lamentation; (حسرتا) the one addressed, one for whom lamentation is made, a muḍāf, accusative, its accusative marker being the implied fatḥa on the letter before the alif, which is converted from the (ياء), and that (ياء) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (ما) a maṣdar particle «[Note: or a relative noun in the position of a genitive, attached to (حسرتا), its ʿāʾid being omitted.]».
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تقول) is in the position of an accusative, a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), with an omitted muḍāf; its governing word is أنيبوا.. «[Note: or its governing word is implied, i.e. "we warned you ..."]», that is: "for fear that a soul should say ..."
The interpreted maṣdar (ما فرّطت ... ) is in the position of a genitive after (على), attached to (حسرتا).
(في جنب) attached to (فرّطت); (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya); (إن) the lightened form of the heavy (inna), and it is necessarily inoperative (muhmala); (اللام) the distinguishing lām (al-fāriqa); (من الساخرين) attached to the khabar of كنت.
The clause «تقول نفس ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the particle-type relative (أن).
The clause «يا حسرتا ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech (maqūl al-qawl).
The clause «فرّطت ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «كنت لمن الساخرين» is in the position of an accusative, a ḥāl.
(57) (أو) a conjunction; (تقول) an imperfect verb in the accusative, conjoined to the preceding (تقول); (لو) a non-jussive conditional particle; (اللام) occurring in the apodosis of (لو) .. (من المتّقين) attached to an omitted khabar of كنت.
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ الله هداني) is in the position of a nominative, the fāʿil of an omitted verb whose implied form is ثبت, that is: (لو) "my guidance had been established, I would have been ..."
The clause «تقول.... (الثانية) » has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تقول نفس (the first).
The clause «لو (ثبتت) هدايتي....» is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
The clause «هداني ... » is in the position of a nominative, the khabar of أنّ.
The clause «كنت من المتّقين» has no grammatical position; it is the apodosis of a non-jussive conditional.
(58) (أو تقول) like the preceding; (حين) an adverb of time in the accusative, attached to (تقول); (لو) a particle of wishing; (لي) attached to an omitted khabar of (أنّ); (كرّة) the ism of أنّ, accusative; (الفاء) the fāʾ of causation; (أكون) an incomplete imperfect verb, put in the accusative by an implied أن after the (الفاء), and its ism is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I"; (من المحسنين) attached to the khabar of أكون.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن أكون..) is conjoined to a maṣdar taken from the wish that came before, that is: "would that there were a return for me, so that my being one of those who do good ..." «[Note: It is permissible for the interpreted maṣdar to be conjoined to (كرّة) without regard to causation in the fāʾ. The difference between the two cases is that the conjunction above makes the "being" consequent upon the wish, whereas, without regard to causation, the "being" is itself wished for, as is the case with the word كرّة.]».
The clause «تقول....» has no grammatical position; it is conjoined to the clause تقول (the second).
The clause «ترى....» is in the position of a genitive, a muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «أكون ... » has no grammatical position; it is the ṣila of the implied particle-type relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّ لي كرة) is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech.
(59) (بلى) a particle of response, affirming the negated question; (قد) a particle of certainty (taḥqīq); (الفاء) a conjunction; (بها) attached to (كذّبت); (الواو) a conjunction in both places; (من الكافرين) attached to the khabar of كنت.
The clause «قد جاءتك آياتي ... » is in the position of an accusative, the quoted speech of an implied saying.
The clause «كذّبت ... » is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause جاءتك آياتي.
The clause «استكبرت» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause كذّبت.
The clause «كنت من الكافرين» is in the position of an accusative, conjoined to the clause كذّبت..

* Morphology:
(الساخرين), plural of الساخر, an active participle from the triliteral verb سخر, of the pattern فرح, on the wazn فاعل.

* Rhetoric:
1- Clarification (al-īḍāḥ): in His saying, the Exalted, «وَأَنِيبُوا إِلى رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ» .
It is conjoined to لا تقنطوا, to complete the clarification, as if it were said: "Do not despair of the mercy of Allah the Exalted, thinking that He will not accept your repentance, but turn to Him, the Exalted, and be sincere to Him, the Mighty and Majestic."
2- Indefiniteness (al-tankīr): in His saying, the Exalted, «أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ» .
The word «نفس» is made indefinite because what is meant by it is some of the souls, namely the soul of the disbeliever; it is also possible that a soul distinguished from the other souls is meant, either by stubbornness in disbelief that is severe or by a great punishment; and it is possible that multiplicity is meant, as al-Aʿshā said:
وربّ بقيع لو هتفت بجوّه ... أتاني كريم ينفض الرّأس مغضبا
(Many a level plain: had I called out in its midst, a noble man would have come to me, shaking his head in anger.)
He means droves of noble men who would help him, not one noble man. Its like is: "many a land I have crossed, many a hero I have faced", meaning many lands and heroes.
3- Metonymy (al-kināya): in His saying, the Exalted, «عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ» .
The original sense of الجنب is the bodily limb, then it is borrowed for the side and direction adjoining it, following their habit of borrowing the other limbs for that, such as "right" and "left"; and what is meant here is the direction, figuratively.
Neglect with regard to the direction of obedience is a metonymy for neglect of obedience itself, because whoever has lost a direction has all the more lost what is in it, the most eloquent way since it proceeds by demonstrative proof. Similar to that is the saying of Ziyād al-Aʿjam:
إن السماحة والمروءة والندى ... في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج
(Generosity, manliness and bounty are in a dome pitched over Ibn al-Ḥashraj.)
He means that he is singled out for these qualities, which are not found in anyone else; there is no tent there, and nothing was pitched at all.

semin-durr:36-36.t:
His saying: {بِكَافٍ عَبْدَهُ}: The majority read «عبدَه» in the singular. The Two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «عباده» in the plural, meaning the prophets and their followers. It was also read «بكافي عبادِه» with the genitive construct (iḍāfa). And «يُكافى» is the imperfect of «كافى»; «عباده» is accusative as the direct object (mafʿūl bihi). Then the form fāʿala (mufāʿala) here may be in the sense of the simple form faʿala, like «نُجازي» in the sense of «نَجْزي», and it was built on the form mufāʿala because of what has preceded, namely that the pattern mufāʿala signals intensification, since it implies contending (mughālaba). It may also be that its original is «يُكافِئ» with a hamza, from «المكافأة» in the sense of «يَجْزِيْهم» (He requites them), and then the hamza was lightened. [Translator's note: the source text reads "فخفَّف الهمزةِ" with the hamza in the genitive; translated as written.]
His saying: «ويُخَوِّفُونَك»: It may be a ḥāl (circumstantial), since the meaning is: "Is He not sufficient for you at the time of their frightening you with such-and-such, and He knows it?" As though the meaning were: He is sufficient for him in every state, even in this state. It may also be resumptive (mustaʾnafa).

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {أَفَرَأَيْتُم مَّا تَدْعُونَ}: This is the «رأى» that takes two objects. The first is «ما تَدْعوْن» and the second is the interrogative clause. The pronoun returning to the object from it is his saying «هُنَّ». He made it feminine only in contempt of what they call upon besides Him, and because they used to name them with feminine names: al-Lāt, Manāt and al-ʿUzzā. The full treatment of this has already preceded in several places.
His saying: {هَلْ هُنَّ كَاشِفَاتُ ضُرِّهِ}: Abū ʿAmr read «كاشفاتٌ» and «مُمْسِكاتٌ» with tanwīn (nunation) and put «ضُرَّه» and «رحمتَه» in the accusative, which is the original rule for the active participle. The others read them with the genitive construct, which is a lightening.

semin-durr:42-42.t: His saying: {والتي لَمْ تَمُتْ}: It is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to «الأنفس», that is: "He takes the souls when they die, and He also takes the souls that have not died, in their sleep." So «في منامِها» is an adverbial (ẓarf) attached to «يَتَوفَّى». The Two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) read «قُضِيَ» in the passive, with «الموتُ» in the nominative because it stands in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil).

semin-durr:43-43.t: And his saying: {أَمِ اتخذوا}: «أم» is the disconnected (munqaṭiʿa) one, so it is taken as «بل» plus the interrogative hamza. The discussion of expressions like «أَوَلَوْ» and how this construction works has already preceded.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {وَإِذَا ذُكِرَ الذين}: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the operator (ʿāmil) in «إذا ذُكِرَ»? I say: the operator in «إذا» is the sudden «إذا» (al-fujāʾiyya); the implied form is: 'at the time of the mention of those besides Him, they were taken by surprise at the time of rejoicing.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "As for al-Zamakhsharī's statement, I do not know it as the statement of anyone who is affiliated with grammar, namely that the two adverbials are both governed by «فاجؤوا», so that the first «إذا» is accusative as an adverbial and the second as a direct object." And al-Ḥawfī said: "«إذا هم يَسْتَبشرون»: «إذا» is annexed to the inchoative and its predicate, and «إذا» is repeated for emphasis, and what it is annexed to has been omitted. The implied form is: 'when that is so, they rejoice,' so 'they rejoice' is the operator in «إذا»; the meaning: when it is so, they rejoiced." The Shaykh said: "This is very far from the truth, if «إذا» is made annexed to the inchoative and predicate." Then he said: "And «إذا» is repeated for emphasis and what it is annexed to is omitted," to the end of his words. [Translator's note: the following comment is al-Samīn's own.] If «إذا» is such that what it is annexed to has been omitted, how can it be annexed to the inchoative and predicate which is «هم يَسْتَبْشِرون»? All this was necessitated by a lack of mastery of the science of grammar and of skill in it. End of quotation. In this wording there is unfairness toward the people of knowledge to whom one refers in it. [Translator's note: the quotation marks in the source are irregular; the attribution of the final comments to al-Samīn is my reading of the passage.]
The Shaykh preferred that the operator in the conditional «إذا» be the verb after it, not its apodosis (jawāb), and that it not be annexed to what follows it, even though that is the view of most scholars. He made the sudden «إذا» governed by what follows it, whether it be of time or of place. But if it is said that it is a particle, then it needs no operator, and it is a linker of the apodosis clause to the condition, like the «فاء».
«الاشمِئْزازُ» is aversion and shrinking. Abū Zayd said: it is terror. One says «اشْمَأَزَّ فلانٌ» when he is terrified. Its pattern is «افْعَلَلَّ», like «اقْشَعَرَّ». The poet said:
3897 - إذا عَضَّ الثِّقافُ بها اشْمَأَزَّتْ ... ووَلَّتْه عَشَوْزَنَةً زَبُوْنا
(When the straightening-tool bit into it, it recoiled, and turned toward him a hard, thorny, repelling [shaft].)

semin-durr:48-48.t: His saying: {سَيِّئَاتُ مَا كَسَبُواْ}: «ما» may be a maṣdar (verbal noun) particle, i.e. "the evil of their earning"; or in the sense of «الذي» (that which): "the evil deeds that they earned."

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {إِنَّمَآ أُوتِيتُهُ}: «ما» may be a preparing, redundant (zāʾida) particle added to «إنَّ», as in «إنما قام زيد» ("Only Zayd stood up"), and it may be a relative noun (mawṣūl), with the pronoun returning to it from «أُوْتِيْتُه», i.e. "that which I was given, [I was given] on the strength of knowledge from me, or on the strength of knowledge from Allah concerning me," that is: I deserve that.
His saying: «بل هي»: The pronoun refers to the favour (niʿma). He made it masculine first in his saying «إنما أوتيتُه» because it is in the sense of «الإنعام» (the bestowing of favour), and made it feminine here in consideration of its wording. It was also said: rather, [it refers to] the condition (al-ḥāla) or the act of giving (al-ītāna).

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {قَدْ قَالَهَا}: that is, he said the aforementioned saying. It was read «قد قاله», i.e. this saying or this speech. This clause, namely {فَإِذَا مَسَّ الإنسان}, was conjoined with «فاء» whereas the one at the beginning of the sūra was with «واو», because this one is caused by (musabbaba ʿan) his saying «وإذا ذُكِر», that is: they recoil from the mention of Allah and rejoice at the mention of their gods, so when harm touches one of them... unlike the first, where there is no causal relation, so the «واو», which is for mere conjunction, was used. On this view, what lies between the cause and the effect are parenthetical clauses (jumal iʿtirāḍiyya). al-Zamakhsharī stated this meaning. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) thought it unlikely, because Abū ʿAlī (al-Fārisī) forbids a parenthesis of two clauses, so how about this many clauses? Then he said: "What appears to me regarding the connection is that when He said {وَلَوْ أَنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ} [al-Zumar: 47] etc., that gave notice of what befalls the wrongdoers of severe punishment and that it will appear to them on the Day of Resurrection; He then followed that with what indicates his wrongdoing and transgression, in that when harm touches him he calls upon Allah, and when He is good to him he does not ascribe that to Him."
His saying: «فما أَغْنى»: «ما» may be negative, or interrogative interpreted as a negation. And if we need to interpret it as a negation, let us make it negative to be spared figurative speech (majāz).

semin-durr:53-53.t: His saying: {قُلْ ياعبادي}: It has been said that this verse contains fine points of meaning and rhetoric (maʿānī and bayān). Among them: His turning to them and addressing them; His annexing them to Himself with an annexation of honour; the shift (iltifāt) from the first person to the third person in His saying {مِن رَّحْمَةِ الله}; the annexation of mercy by reason of His most beautiful names; the repetition of the overt noun in its own wording in His saying «إنَّ اللَّهَ»; and the presentation of the clause {إِنَّهُ هُوَ الغفور الرحيم} as emphasised with «إنَّ», with the separating pronoun (faṣl), and with the repetition of the two attributes which the preceding verse contained.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {أَن تَقُولَ}: It is a mafʿūl min ajlihi (object of purpose). al-Zamakhsharī implied "out of dislike that you should say"; Ibn ʿAṭiyya: "turn in repentance for the sake of your saying"; Abū l-Baqāʾ and al-Ḥawfī: "We warned you for fear that you should say." But there is no need to imply this operator given the presence of «أَنيبوا». He made «نفساً» indefinite only because he meant plurality, as in the saying of al-Aʿshā:
3898 - ورُبَّ بَقيعٍ لو هَتَفْتُ بجَوِّه ... أتاني كريمٌ يَنْفُضُ الرأسَ مُغْضَبا
(Many a level plain, had I called out in its expanse, a noble man would have come to me, shaking his head in anger.)
He means: "many noble men came to me," not one single noble man, because that would contradict the intended meaning. It is also possible that he means: a soul distinguished from among souls by intense obstinacy in disbelief, or by great punishment.
His saying: «يا حَسْرتا»: The majority read it with the alif as a replacement for the yā of the first-person annexation. From Ibn Kathīr: «يا حَسْرَتاهْ» with the pausal hā of silence (hāʾ al-sakt) when pausing; Abū Jaʿfar: «يا حَسْرَتي» in the original form. And from him also: «يا حَسْرتاي» with both alif and yā. There are two views on it. One: it combines the replacement and what is replaced. The other: it is the dual of «حَسْرة» annexed to the yā of the first person. This was objected to: it should then have been said «يا حَسْرتيَّ», with the yā of the accusative assimilated into the yā of annexation. The reply: he may have followed the dialect of al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb and others, as in «رأيتُ الزيدان» ("I saw the two Zayds," with the dual in alif in the accusative). It was also said: the alif is a replacement for the yā and the yā after it is an addition. It was also said: the alif is an addition placed between the two terms of the annexation. Both are weak.
His saying: {على مَا فَرَّطَتُ}: «ما» is a maṣdar particle, i.e. "for my neglect." And there is an omitted muḍāf (first term of the annexation), i.e. "in regard to obedience to Allah." It was also said that {فِي جَنبِ الله} means the command and the direction. One says: "he is in the side (janb) of so-and-so and his flank," i.e. his direction and region. The rajaz poet said:
3899 - الناسُ جَنْبٌ والأميرُ جَنْبُ
(The people are on one side, and the commander is on one side.)
And another said:
3900 - أفي جَنْبِ بَكْرٍ قَطَّعَتْني مَلامةً ... لَعَمْري لقد طالَتْ ملامَتُها بيا
(Is it on account of Bakr that blame has cut me to pieces? By my life, her blame of me has gone on long.)
Then the usage was extended, so it was said: "he neglected in his side," i.e. in his right. He said:
3901 - أَمَا تَتَّقِيْنَ اللَّهَ في جَنْبِ عاشِقٍ ... له كَبِدٌ حَرَّى عليكِ تَقَطَّعُ
(Do you not fear Allah in regard to a lover whose parched liver is breaking apart for you?)

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {فَأَكُونَ}: There are two views on its being accusative. One: it is conjoined to «كرَّة», for that is a maṣdar, so an interpreted maṣdar was conjoined to an explicit maṣdar, as in her saying:
3902 - للُبْسُ عَباءةٍ وتَقَرَّ عَيْني ... أَحَبُّ إليَّ من لُبْسِ الشُّفوفِ
(To wear a woollen cloak and have my eye be content is dearer to me than wearing fine garments.)
and the saying of the other:
3903 - فما لَكَ منها غيرُ ذكرى وحَسْرةٍ ... وتَسْأَلَ عن رُكْبانِها أينَ يَمَّموا
(Nothing is left for you of her but remembrance and regret, and asking about her riders: where did they head?)
The second: it is accusative as the answer to the wish (jawāb al-tamannī) understood from His saying {لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةً}. The difference between the two views: in the first, the being [of the righteous] is itself wished for, and «أَنْ» may be either implied or overt; in the second, the being follows upon the attainment of what is wished for and is not itself wished for, and «أَنْ» must be implied.

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {بلى}: A particle of reply. As to what it is given in reply to, there are two views. One: it is an implied negation. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "The proper place of «بلى» is after a negation that carries affirmation (taqrīr), as if the soul had said: 'My view did not have room, and the matter did not become clear to me.'" The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "Its proper place is not the affirming negation; rather its proper place is the negation, and then affirmation was carried over onto it. For that reason some Arabs answered an affirming negation with «نعم» rather than «بلى», and the same occurs in the wording of Sībawayh himself." The second: the wish mentioned and its answer both imply a negation of guidance, as if he had said, "I was not guided," and Allah answered him that. al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was the reply not joined to what it answers, namely His saying {لَوْ أَنَّ الله هَدَانِي}, without separating between them? I say: because it can only be one of two things: either it is placed before one of the three parallel statements, thereby splitting them, or the middle statement is delayed. The first is not good because of the breaking up of the composition by joining the parallels. As for the second, it is because of the disruption of the order, which is regret over the neglect of obedience, then excuse-making by the lack of guidance, then wishing for return. So the right thing was what occurred: He related the statements of the soul in their order and arrangement, then answered from among them the one that called for an answer."
The majority read «جاءَتْكَ» with fatḥa on the kāf, then «فكذّبْتَ واستكبرتَ، وكنتَ» with fatḥa on the tā', addressing the disbeliever rather than the soul. al-Jaḥdarī, Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Yaʿmar and al-Shāfiʿī on the authority of Ibn Kathīr read it with kasra on the kāf and the tā', addressing the soul. Umm Salama transmitted it from the Prophet ﷺ, and Abū Bakr and his daughter ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with them, read it so. al-Ḥasan, al-Aʿraj and al-Aʿmash read «جَأَتْكَ», on the pattern of «جَفَتْك», with a hamza and no alif. It may be a shortening, like the reading of Qunbul {أَن رَّأهُ استغنى}, or there may be a transposition (qalb) in the word, in that the lām was placed before the ʿayn, whereupon two silent letters met and the alif was dropped because of their meeting, like «رَمَتْ» and «غَزَتْ».

semin-durr:60-60.t: His saying: {وُجُوهُهُم مُّسْوَدَّةٌ}: The majority read both in the nominative; it is a clause of mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). As to its position, there are two views. One: accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative nouns, because the seeing is visual; this is how al-Zamakhsharī parsed it. His school holds that the «واو» may not be dropped from the like of it except as an irregularity, following al-Farrāʾ in that, so this is a retraction by him from that. The second: it is in the position of accusative as a second object, because the seeing is of the heart. This is remote, because the connection of visual seeing to bodies and their colours is clearer than the connection of heart-seeing to them. It was read «وجوهَهم مُسْودَّة» with both in the accusative, with «وجوهَهم» a badal baʿḍ min kull (partial substitute) and «مُسْوَدَّةً» as per the preceding accusative, as ḥāl or second object. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If «وجوهَهم» were read in the accusative, it would be a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion)." I say: it has indeed been read thus, and praise belongs to Allah, but it is not as he said, a substitute of inclusion; rather it is a partial substitute, and it seems to have been a slip of the tongue or an overflow of the pen. Ubayy read «أُجوهُهم», changing the wāw into hamza, which is eloquent, like {أُقِّتَتْ} [al-Mursalāt: 11] and its kind.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {بِمَفَازَتِهِمْ}: The Two Brothers (Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī) and Abū Bakr read «بمفازاتِهم» in the plural, since the types of the maṣdar differ, it was pluralised. The others read it in the singular, which is the original. It was said that there is an omitted muḍāf, i.e. "by the causes of their success" or "by its means." «المَفازَةُ» is the means of salvation. It was also said that there is no need for that, since by «المَفازة» is meant felicity.
His saying: {لاَ يَمَسُّهُمُ السواء}: This clause may be explicative of their success, as if it were said: "And what is their success?" and the answer was: "Evil does not touch them"; so it has no grammatical position. It may also be in the position of accusative as a ḥāl from {الذين اتَّقَوا}. [Translator's note: the source reads «السواء» in the verse quotation and «السوء» in the following explanation; translated as written.]

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {لَّهُ مَقَالِيدُ}: A resumptive clause. «المَقاليد» is the plural of «مِقْلاد» or «مِقْليد», or it has no singular from its own wording, like «أَساطير» and its sisters. One also says «إِقْليد» and «أَقاليد». They are keys, and the word is an Arabicised Persian one. In this statement is a wonderful metaphor, like your saying "in the hand of so-and-so is the key to this matter," when there is no key there; it is only an expression of the intensity of his control over that thing.
His saying: {والذين كَفَرُواْ بِآيَاتِ الله}: There are two views on this clause. One: it is conjoined to His saying {وَيُنَجِّي الله الذين اتقوا} [al-Zumar: 61], i.e. "He saves the God-fearing by their success, and the disbelievers are the losers," with a parenthesis between them that He is the Creator of all things and has charge over them. al-Zamakhsharī said this. Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī objected to him that it is the conjunction of a nominal clause to a verbal clause, which is not permissible. This objection is itself open to objection, since there is nothing preventing that. The second: it is conjoined to His saying {لَّهُ مَقَالِيدُ السماوات}; that is, when the Exalted described Himself as the Creator of everything in the heavens and the earth, with its keys in His hand, He said: "and those who disbelieve that the matter is so, those are the losers." [Translator's note: the last sentence is as printed in the source, which appears elliptical.]

semin-durr:65-65.t: His saying: {لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ}: The apparent view is that this clause is the one standing in the place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil), since it is what was revealed. The principles of the Basrans refuse that, and they imply that what stands in its place is the pronoun of the maṣdar, because for them a clause cannot be an agent; what stands in the place of the agent here is the preposition and its genitive noun, namely «إليك». It was read «لَيُحْبِطَنَّ», i.e. Allah, and «لَنُحْبِطَنَّ» with the nūn of majesty. «عَمَلَكَ» is a direct object in both readings.

semin-durr:66-66.t: His saying: {بَلِ الله فاعبد}: The Majestic Name is accusative by «اعبُدْ». The discussion of a «فاء» of this kind has already preceded in al-Baqara. al-Zamakhsharī made it the apodosis of an implied condition, i.e. "if you are rational, worship Allah," so he omitted the condition and made the fronting of the object a compensation for it. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) objected: it may occur that one says «زيدٌ فعَمْراً اضرِبْ», so if the fronting were a compensation, the compensation and what is compensated for would be combined. ʿĪsā read «بل اللَّهُ» in the nominative as an inchoative, with the returning pronoun omitted, i.e. "so worship Him."

semin-durr:67-67.t:
al-Ḥasan, Abū Ḥaywa and ʿĪsā read «قَدَّروا» with shadda on the dāl, and «حَقَّ قَدَره» with fatḥa on the dāl. al-Aʿmash agreed with them on fatḥa on the dāl of «قَدَره».
His saying: {والأرض جَمِيعاً قَبْضَتُهُ}: mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of accusative as ḥāl, i.e. "They did not magnify Him as He is due to be magnified, when He is described with this overwhelming power," like His saying {كَيْفَ تَكْفُرُونَ بالله وَكُنْتُمْ أَمْوَاتاً} [al-Baqara: 28]. «جميعاً» is a ḥāl, and it shows that by «الأرض» is meant the earths, and because the place is a place of magnification, and because the plural is conjoined to it. The operator in this ḥāl is what «قَبْضَتُه» indicates. «قبضَتُه» cannot operate in it, whether you make it a maṣdar, because a maṣdar's object does not precede it, or you intend by it a quantity.
al-Zamakhsharī said: "With the intention of the plural, meaning in «الأرض», and that the plural is meant by it, and its emphasis with «الجميع», the emphasiser was made to follow the plural before the predicate came, so that it be known at the outset that the predicate which will come does not apply to a single earth but to all the earths." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«جميعاً» is a ḥāl from «الأرض», and the implied form is: when it is gathered, His grasp, that is, what is grasped; so the operator in «إذا» is the maṣdar, because it is in the sense of the passive participle. Abū ʿAlī said in al-Ḥujja: the implied form is «ذاتُ قبضَتِه» (that which has His grasp). This was objected to: the muḍāf ilayhi does not operate on what precedes it. But this is not sound, because it is now not a muḍāf ilayhi, and after the muḍāf is omitted its ruling does not remain." End of quotation. This statement has a difficulty, since there is no need to imply an operator in the «إذا» which is not pronounced.
As for his saying «قَبْضَتُه»: if we imply a muḍāf, as al-Fārisī said, i.e. «ذاتُ قبضَتِه», then there is no occurrence of the maṣdar in the place of a passive participle; if it is not implied, it may be that the maṣdar occurs in its place, and then it is asked: how was the maṣdar that occurs in the place of a passive participle made feminine, which is not permissible? One does not say «حُلَّة نَسْجة اليمن» but «نَسْجُ اليمن», i.e. woven of Yemen. The answer: what is prohibited is the entry of the tā' that indicates singularity (taḥdīd), and this one is merely for feminine. So it was answered, but that is not convincing, for the meaning is based on singularity, since it is more eloquent in expressing power. It may also be that by the maṣdar is meant the quantity of that.
«القَبْضَةُ» with fatḥa is the single act, and with ḍamma is a noun for what is grasped, like «الغَرْفة» and «الغُرْفَة». The majority read «قَبْضَتُه» in the nominative; al-Ḥasan read it accusative. Ibn Khālawayh and a group parsed the accusative as adverbial (ẓarf), i.e. "in His grasp." This was objected to: it is a specific adverbial, so «في» must be present, which is the view of the Basrans. The Kufans permit it; they allow «زيد دارَك» in the accusative, i.e. "Zayd is in your house." al-Zamakhsharī said: "He made it an adverbial by likening the delimited to the undefined," thus agreeing with the Kufans. The majority read «مَطْوياتٌ» in the nominative as predicate. As for «بيمينِه», there are several views. First: it is attached to «مَطْوِيَّات».
Second: it is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «مَطْوِيَّات». Third: it is a second predicate. ʿĪsā and al-Jaḥdarī read it in the accusative as ḥāl. al-Akhfash used it as evidence for the permissibility of the ḥāl's coming before its operator when the operator is a preposition, as in «زيدٌ قائماً في الدار». But there is no proof in this, since it can be parsed in two ways. One, which is the clearer, is that «السماوات» is conjoined to «الأرض», so the report would be about the earths and the heavens, that all of them are in His grasp, and «مَطْوِيَّاتٍ» would be a ḥāl from «السماوات», just as «جميعاً» was a ḥāl from «الأرض», and «بيمينه» is attached to «مطويَّات». The second: «مطويَّات» is accusative by an implied verb, «بيمينه» is the predicate, and «مطويَّات» and its operator are a parenthetical clause; this is weak.

semin-durr:68-68.t:
His saying: {فِي الصور}: The majority read the wāw with sukūn; Zayd ibn ʿAlī and Qatāda read it with fatḥa, plural of «صُوْرة». This refutes the statement of Ibn ʿAṭiyya that «الصُّوْر» here must be the horn, and cannot be the plural of «صُورَة». It was read «فَصُعِقَ» in the passive; it is taken from their saying «صَعَقَتْهم الصاعقةُ» (the thunderbolt struck them). One says: «صَعَقَه اللَّهُ فصَعِقَ».
{إِلاَّ مَن شَآءَ الله}: a connected exception (istithnāʾ muttaṣil), and the excepted is either Jibrīl, Mīkāʾīl and Isrāfīl, or Riḍwān, the houris and the zabāniya, or the Creator Himself, the Exalted, as al-Ḥasan said. There is some question about that, from His saying {مَن فِي السماوات وَمَن فِي الأرض}, since the Exalted does not occupy space. On this view, it must be a disconnected exception (munqaṭiʿ).
His saying: {ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أخرى}: «أخرى» may be what stands in the place of the agent, being originally an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "another blast was blown into it." This is supported by the explicit statement of it in His saying {فَإِذَا نُفِخَ فِي الصور نَفْخَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ} [al-Ḥāqqa: 13], where the maṣdar is explicitly made to stand in. It may also be that what stands in its place is the preposition and genitive, with «أخرى» accusative as stated before.
His saying: {فَإِذَا هُمْ قِيَامٌ}: The majority read «قيام» in the nominative as predicate. Zayd ibn ʿAlī put it in the accusative as ḥāl, and then there are several views. One: the predicate is «يَنْظرون», and it is the operator in this ḥāl, i.e. "then they are looking, standing." Second: the operator in the ḥāl is what operates in the sudden «إذا» when it is an adverbial. If it is of place, as Sībawayh said, the implied form is "then in the presence they are, standing"; if it is of time, as al-Rummānī said, "then at that time they are, standing," i.e. their existence. A muḍāf had to be implied in this view only because one cannot predicate time of bodies. Third: the predicate is omitted and it is the operator in the ḥāl, i.e. "then they are resurrected, or gathered, standing." If we make the sudden «إذا» a particle, as some of them said, then the operator in the ḥāl is either «يَنْظُرون» or the implied predicate, as both were investigated above.

semin-durr:69-69.t: His saying: {وَأَشْرَقَتِ}: The majority read it in the active. Ibn ʿAbbās, Abū l-Jawzāʾ and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read it in the passive, which is a transitive made so by the hamza from «شَرَقَتْ» when it rose, and it is not from «أشرقَتْ» in the sense of shone, because that is intransitive. Ibn ʿAṭiyya made it like «رَجَعَ» and «رَجَعْتُه», «وَقَفَ» and «وقَفْته», meaning «أَشْرَق» is both intransitive and transitive.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {زُمَراً}: ḥāl. «زُمَر» is the plural of «زُمْرَة», which are groups in separation, one following another; «تَزَمَّروا» means they gathered. He said:
3905 - حتى احْزَألَّتْ زُمَرٌ بعد زُمَرْ
(Until groups after groups gathered together.)
This is the statement of Abū ʿUbayda and al-Akhfash. al-Rāghib said: "«الزُّمْرَة» is a small group; from it comes «شاةٌ زَمِرة», i.e. a sheep with little wool, and «رجلٌ زَمِرٌ», i.e. a man of little manliness. «زَمَرَتِ النَّعامةُ تَزْمِرُ زَماراً» (the ostrich hooted), and from it are derived «الزَّمْر» and «الزَّمَّارة», a metaphor for the dissolute woman."
His saying: «حتى إذا»: The discussion of «حتى» entering upon «إذا» has already preceded more than once. The apodosis of «إذا» is His saying «فُتِحت». The difference of the readers on shadda and its absence has preceded in Sūrat al-Anʿām. Ibn Hurmuz read «ألم تَأْتِكم» with the tā' of the feminine plural. «منكم» is an adjective of «رسل» or attached to the coming; «يَتْلون» is another adjective; and «خالدين» in both places is a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated circumstantial).

semin-durr:73-73.t: His saying: {وَفُتِحَتْ}: As to the apodosis of «إذا», there are three views. One: His saying «وفُتحت» and the «واو» is redundant; this is the view of the Kufans and al-Akhfash. The «واو» was brought here and not in the one before it because the doors of the prisons are shut until the criminal comes to them, whereupon they are opened for him and then closed on him, so the absence of the «واو» suited that; unlike the doors of joy and delight, which are opened in anticipation of whoever will enter. Second: the apodosis is His saying {وَقَالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا}, with the «واو» again redundant, i.e. "until when they came to it, its keepers said to them." Third: the apodosis is omitted. al-Zamakhsharī said: it should properly be implied after «خالدين». End of quotation. He means because it comes after the dependents of the condition and what is conjoined to it, and the implied form is "they were at ease." al-Mubarrad implied «سُعِدُوا» (they were made happy). On these two views the clause beginning «وفُتِحَتْ» is in the position of accusative as ḥāl. Some called this «واو» the wāw of eight, saying: because the doors of Paradise are eight; they said the same of His saying {وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ} [al-Kahf: 22]. It was also said that the implied form is "until when they came to it and its doors were opened," meaning the apodosis is in the wording of the condition but with the added restriction by ḥāl, and for that reason it is sound.

semin-durr:74-74.t: His saying: {نَتَبَوَّأُ}: a circumstantial clause (jumla ḥāliyya), and «حيثُ» is a direct object. It may be an adverbial in its usual sense, which is the apparent view.

semin-durr:75-75.t:
His saying: {حَآفِّينَ}: the plural of «حافّ», which is what encircles a thing, from «حَفَفْتُ بالشيءِ» when I surrounded it. He said:
3906 - يَحُفُّه جانبا نِيْقٍ وتُتْبِعُهُ ... مثلَ الزُّجاجةِ لم تُكْحَلْ من الرَّمَدِ
(Two sides of a lofty peak surround it, and it is followed by [an eye] like a glass vial not kohl-darkened from ophthalmia.)
It is taken from «الحِفاف», which is the side. The poet said:
3907 - له لَحَظاتٌ عن حِفافي سَرِيْرِه ... إذا كرَّها فيها عقابٌ ونائل
(He has glances from the two sides of his couch; when he repeats them, they contain punishment and bounty.)
al-Farrāʾ said, and al-Zamakhsharī followed him: "«حافِّين» has no singular," as if the two saw that a single one cannot be «حافّ», since «الحُفُوف» is the encircling and surrounding of a thing, and this is realised only in a plural.
His saying: «مِنْ حَوْلِ»: There are two views on «مِنْ». One, the view of al-Akhfash, is that it is redundant. The second: it is for the beginning of the range. The pronoun in «بينهم» refers either to the angels or to the servants. «يُسَبِّحون» is a ḥāl from the pronoun in «حافِّين».

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {أَفَغَيْرَ الله تأمروني أَعْبُدُ}: There are three views on it. First, and it is the apparent one: «غير» is accusative by «أَعْبُدُ», and «أعبدُ» is governed by «تَأْمرونِّي» with an implied maṣdar «أنْ»; when it was omitted its operation became void, and that is one of the two views. The original is: "Do you command me to worship other than Allah?" Then the object of «أعبدُ» was fronted before «تَأْمُرونِّي», the operator of its operator. Some have weakened this: it would entail the fronting of the object of the ṣila before the relative noun; for «غيرَ» is accusative by «أعبدُ», and «أعبدُ» is the ṣila of «أنْ», which is not permissible. This objection is worth nothing, because when the relative particle was omitted its ruling was not observed in what was mentioned; only its meaning is observed to make the speech sound. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "If we ruled so, it would lead to omitting the relative and retaining its ṣila, which is not permitted except in poetic necessity." What he mentioned is open to question, in that this is specific to «أنْ» among the relatives, in that it is omitted while its ṣila remains, and this is regular according to the Basrans in certain places where it is omitted and its operation remains, whereas elsewhere, when it is omitted, its operation does not remain except in necessity or rarely. It is recited in both ways:
