3904 - ألا أيُّهذا الزاجريْ أحضرُ الوغى ... وأنْ أشهدَ اللذاتِ هل أنتَ مُخْلِدي
(O you who rebuke me for attending battle and for witnessing pleasures, are you going to make me immortal?)
What indicates that «أنْ» was intended in the original is the reading of some who read «أعبدَ» with the verb in the accusative, counting «أَنْ» as present. Second: «غيرَ» is accusative by «تأمرونِّي», and «أعبد» is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) from it, with «أنْ» implied with it as well. The implied form is: "Do you command me to worship other than Allah?" The meaning: "Do you command me with worship of other than Allah?" al-Zamakhsharī implied: "you make me a servant and say to me: worship him." The original is «تَأْمُرونني أن أعبدَ», then he omitted «أنْ» and raised the verb. Do you not see that you say: «أفغيرَ اللَّهِ تقولون لي اعبده» and «أفغيرَ اللَّهِ تقولون لي: اعبد», so likewise «أفغيرَ الله تقولون لي أَن أعبده» and «أفغيرَ الله تأمروني أَنْ أعبدَ». And the proof of the soundness of this view is the reading of whoever read «أعبدَ» in the accusative.
As for «أعبد», there are three views on it. One: together with the implied «أَنْ» it is in the position of accusative as a badal from «غير», as above. Second: it is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. Third: it has no position at all.
His saying: «تَأْمُرُوْنِّي»: Ibn Kathīr read it with the nūn of the nominative (nūn al-rafʿ) assimilated into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) and with fatḥa on the yā'; the others left it free. Nāfiʿ read «تَأْمرونيَ» with a light nūn and fatḥa on the yā'. Ibn ʿĀmir read «تأْمرونني» unassimilated with sukūn on the yā'. It has already preceded in Sūrat al-Anʿām, al-Ḥijr and elsewhere that whenever the nūn of the nominative meets the nūn of protection, three forms are permitted, and the investigation of the disagreement over which of the two is omitted has also preceded.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم (In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)

His saying: {تَنزِيلُ}: There are two views on it. One: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, the implied form being: "This is the revelation of...". The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "I say that it is a khabar, and the mubtadaʾ is «هو», referring to His saying {إِنْ هُوَ إِلاَّ ذِكْرٌ لِّلْعَالَمِينَ} [Ṣād: 87], as if it were said: 'And this Reminder, what is it?' So it was said: 'It is the revelation of the Book.'" The second: that it is a mubtadaʾ, with the preposition phrase after it as its khabar, i.e. "the revelation of the Book is from Allah". Al-Zajjāj and al-Farrāʾ held this.

His saying: «مِنَ اللَّهِ»: Several views are possible. One: that it is in the position of nominative as the khabar of «تنزيل», as its explanation came earlier. Two: that it is a khabar after a khabar, if we make «تنزيلُ» the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, as in your saying "This is Zayd, of the people of Iraq". Three: that it is the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "This is a revelation; this is from Allah." Four: that it is attached to «تَنْزيل» itself, if we make it the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. Five: that it is attached to something omitted as a ḥāl from «تنزيل», in which the implied demonstrative acts, said al-Zamakhsharī. The Shaykh said: "It cannot be a ḥāl in which the sense of pointing acts, because the senses of verbs do not act when that in which they are is omitted; for that reason they rejected Abū al-ʿAbbās's statement about the verse of al-Farazdaq:

3884 - ... ... and when (idh mā) their like among men is not found (mithlahum basharu)

that «مثلهم» is accusative by an omitted khabar, the implied form being: 'and when there is in existence, in a state of resemblance to them, a human'." Six: that it is a ḥāl from «الكتاب», said Abū al-Baqāʾ. A ḥāl from the muḍāf ilayhi is allowed here because it is the object of the muḍāf, as the muḍāf is a maṣdar annexed to its object. The majority read «تَنْزيلُ» nominative, as above. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, ʿĪsā and Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it accusative by an implied verb, the implied form being "Hold to" or "Recite", and the like.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His saying: {بالحق}: It may be attached to the sending down (inzāl), i.e. "by reason of the truth", or attached to something omitted as a ḥāl from the agent or the object, which is the Book, i.e. "accompanied by the truth" (in the plural for the agent, singular for the object). In His saying {إِنَّآ أَنزَلْنَآ إِلَيْكَ الكتاب} there is a repetition of glorification, by bringing it out in another sentence in which the sending down is attributed to the One who magnifies Himself.

His saying: «مُخْلِصاً»: A ḥāl from the agent of «اعبد», and «الدين» is accusative by the active participle. The fāʾ in «فاعبُدِ» is for linking, as in your saying "So-and-so was good to you, so thank him". The majority read «الدينَ» accusative, as above. Ibn Abī ʿAbla read it nominative. There are two views on it. One: that it is nominative as agent, governed by «مُخْلِصاً»; on this a figurative usage and an implied element are required. The figurative usage is the attribution of sincerity to the religion when in reality it belongs to its owner; its parallel is their saying "a poet's poetry" (shiʿr shāʿir). The implied element is a pronoun returning to the owner of the ḥāl, i.e. "sincere for Him in the religion, on your part"; this is the opinion of the Basrans in such cases. As for the Kufans, according to them al- may stand in place of the pronoun, i.e. "making your religion sincere". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It is proper for one who reads it nominative to read «مُخْلَصاً» with fatḥa on the lām, because of His saying, the Exalted, {وَأَخْلَصُواْ دِينَهُمْ للَّهِ} [al-Nisāʾ: 146], so that it corresponds to His saying {أَلاَ لِلَّهِ الدين الخالص}; khāliṣ and mukhlaṣ are the same, unless he describes the religion with the attribute of its owner by figurative attribution, as in their saying: shiʿr shāʿir." The second: that the statement is complete at «مُخْلِصاً», which is a ḥāl from the agent of «فاعبدْ», and «له الدينُ» is a mubtadaʾ and khabar; this is the saying of al-Farrāʾ. Al-Zamakhsharī rejected it and said: "He has brought an analysis by which the speech reverts to your saying 'To Allah belongs the religion': {أَلاَ لِلَّهِ الدين الخالص}." I say: what al-Zamakhsharī mentioned does not show a refutation of this analysis.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His saying: {والذين اتخذوا}: Several views are possible. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ, and its khabar is an implied saying which was omitted while its object remained, namely His saying «ما نَعْبُدهم». The implied form is: "they say: We only worship them...". Two: that the khabar is His saying {إِنَّ الله يَحْكُمُ}, and that implied saying is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl, i.e. "and those who took... saying such-and-such — Allah will judge between them". Three: that the implied saying is a badal from the ṣila, which is «اتَّخذوا»; the implied form is "and those who took... said: We worship them only...", and the khabar is also {إِنَّ الله يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ}. In these views «الذين» denotes the polytheists who took others as patrons. Four: that «الذين» denotes the angels and what is worshipped besides Allah, such as ʿUzayr, al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā, and the agent of «اتَّخَذَ» refers to the polytheists. The first object of the taking is omitted, being the returning pronoun of the relative, and the second object is «أولياءَ». The implied form is "and those whom the polytheists took as patrons". Then for the khabar of this mubtadaʾ there are two views: one, the implied saying, the implied form being "those whom the polytheists took as patrons — the polytheists say of them: We only worship them..."; the second, that the khabar is the sentence {إِنَّ الله يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ}.

«ما نُعْبُدُهم» was also read with ḍamma on the nūn, as assimilation to the bāʾ, the sākin not being counted.

His saying: «زُلْفَى»: A confirmatory maṣdar not of the same root, but meeting its governing verb in meaning; the implied form is: "that they may bring us near (liyuzlifūnā) in nearness", or "that they may draw us close, closeness". Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be a confirmatory ḥāl.

His saying: «كاذِبٌ كفَّارٌ»: Al-Ḥasan and al-Aʿraj — and it is reported from Anas — read «كذَّابٌ كَفَّارٌ», and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «كَذُوبٌ كفورٌ».

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {يُكَوِّرُ اليل}: There are two views on this sentence. The more apparent: that it is resumptive, Allah the Exalted informing of that. The second: that it is a ḥāl, said Abū al-Baqāʾ. There is weakness in it, since the wrapping of one over the other occurred only after the creation of the heavens and the earth, unless it is said to be a ḥāl muqaddara (anticipated), which is contrary to the norm.

Al-Takwīr is winding and twisting. One says kāra al-ʿimāma ʿalā raʾsihi and kawwarahā. The meaning of wrapping the night over the day and the day over the night on this sense is: that night and day are successive, one going away and the other covering its place, and when it covers its place, it is as if it had wound over it and clothed it, as a garment is wound over the wearer; or that each of them hides the other when it comes upon it, so it is likened in its hiding of it to something visible that winds over what hides it from the reach of the eyes; or that this one returns over that one in continuous returning, so that is likened to the succession of the coils of a turban, one upon another. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is the most consistent with derivation among the things mentioned. Al-Rāghib said: "Kawr of a thing is rotating it and drawing part of it to another, like the kawr of a turban. His saying {يُكَوِّرُ الليل عَلَى النهار} is an allusion to the course of the sun in its risings and the shortening and lengthening of night and day, and kawwarahu when he throws it gathered. Iktāra al-faras: when it returns its tail in its running. The kuwwāra of bees (the hive) is well known. And al-kūr: the saddle. It is also said that every city has a kūra, which is the area in which villages and settlements gather."

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا}: There are several views on this «ثم». One: that it is in its normal sense of succession with delay, because it is reported that Allah the Exalted brought us out from the loins of Adam like tiny particles, then created Ḥawwāʾ (Eve) some time after that. Two: that it is also in its normal sense, but for another consideration: that what follows is conjoined by it to what is understood from the adjective in His saying «واحدة», the implied form being: "from a soul that was single, i.e. alone, then He made from it its mate". Three: that it is for succession in reports, not in actual time, as if it were said: "It was among its affairs before that that He made from it its mate". Four: that it is for succession in states and ranks. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: what is the point of His saying {ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا} and the delay it conveys? I say: they are two signs among the signs that He enumerated as pointing to His oneness and power: by branching out this uncountable creation from the single soul of Adam, peace be upon him, and creating Ḥawwāʾ from his short rib; except that one of them Allah made a continuing custom, while the other was not the custom, and no female other than Ḥawwāʾ was created from the short rib of a man, so it was more fully a sign and more apt to cause the hearer's wonder. So He conjoined it by «ثم» to the first sign to indicate its distinction in excellence and merit, and its remove from it in what returns to the increase of its being a sign; so it is a delay in state and rank, not a delay in existence."

His saying: {وَأَنزَلَ لَكُمْ مِّنَ الأنعام}: Conjoined to «خَلَقَكم». The sending down may be literal; it is reported that He created them (the cattle) in Paradise and then sent them down. It may also be figurative, in two ways. One: that they live only by vegetation and water, and vegetation lives only by water, and water descends from the clouds; so "sending down" is applied to them, though in reality it is applied to the cause of the cause, as in his saying:

3885 - The humps of the camels in rain-clouds (rabābah) ...

and his saying:

3886 - The tharīd (bread-and-meat dish) became on the tops of the date-palms ...

and his saying:

3887 - When the sky (rain) descends on the land of a people ... we graze it, even if they are angry

The second: that His decrees and rulings are sent down from the heaven in that they are written in the Preserved Tablet, which is also a cause of bringing them into being.

His saying: «يَخْلُقكم»: This sentence is resumptive; there is no need to make it the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ; rather it was begun anew to report with a verbal sentence. The difference among the readers over kasra or fatḥa of the hamza, and likewise the mīm, has already been given.

His saying: «خَلْقاً»: A maṣdar of «يَخْلُق», and {مِّن بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ} is an adjective of it; it is for specifying the kind, in that when it is described, its meaning exceeds that of its governing verb. {مِّن بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ} may be attached to the preceding verb, in which case «خَلْقاً» is for mere emphasis.

His saying: «ظُلُمات»: Attached to the preceding «خَلْق»; it cannot be attached to the accusative «خَلْقاً», since it is a confirmatory maṣdar, although Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it, then forbade it for the reason I mentioned, for he said: "«في» is attached to it, i.e. to «خَلْقاً», or to the second khalq, because the first is confirmatory and does not act." It cannot be attached to the verb before it, because a like particle is already attached to it; and two particles identical in wording and meaning are not attached to the same thing except by way of badal or conjunction. If you make «في ظلمات» a badal from {فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ}, a badal al-ishtimāl, since the wombs include them, and a badal with repetition of the governing particle, that is permissible — I mean the attachment of both prepositional phrases to «يَخْلُقكم». The separation between the badal and the substituted-for by the maṣdar does no harm, because it is a completion of the governor and so is not foreign.

His saying: {ذَلِكُمُ الله رَبُّكُمْ}: «الله» may be the khabar of «ذلكم», and «ربُّكم» an adjective of Allah or a badal from it. It may also be that «الله» is a badal from «ذلكم» and «ربُّكم» its khabar.

His saying: «له المُلْكُ»: It may be resumptive, or a khabar after a khabar; or «الله» may be a badal from «ذلكم», and «ربُّكم» an adjective of Allah or a badal from it, with the sentence «له الملكُ» as the khabar. The khabar may also be the preposition and its genitive noun alone, with «المُلْكُ» as its agent, so it is a case of predicating with a single word.

His saying: {لا إله إِلاَّ هُوَ}: It may be resumptive, or a khabar after a khabar.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ}: Ibn Kathīr, al-Kisāʾī and Ibn Dhakwān read «يَرْضَهُوْ» with the lengthening (ṣila) — which is the original, without disagreement. It is a clear reading. Nāfiʿ, ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read «يَرْضَهُ» with ḍamma on the hāʾ and no lengthening, without disagreement. Al-Sūsī, from Abū ʿAmr, read «يَرْضَهْ» with sukūn on it in connected speech, without disagreement. Al-Dūrī, from Abū ʿAmr, read both ways — I mean sukūn and lengthening. Hishām, from Ibn ʿĀmir, read both ways — I mean sukūn and vowelling without lengthening. These are five grades among the readers. You already know the explanation of sukūn, shortening and full lengthening from what came earlier at the beginning of this work, and what I cited in support and attributed to its speaker as a dialect. No attention is paid to Abū Ḥātim in his declaring the transmitter of the sukūn mistaken, for it is an established dialect from Banū ʿUqayl and Banū Kilāb.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
His saying: {مُنِيباً}: A ḥāl from the agent of «دَعَا», and «إليه» is attached to «مُنيباً», i.e. "returning to Him".

His saying: «خَوَّله»: One says khawwalahu niʿmatan, i.e. "he gave it to him, as an initial gift without any requirement". It is not used for recompense but for the initiation of a gift. Zuhayr said:

3888 - There, if they are granted wealth (yustakhwalū), they ... (Translator's note: the source line is incomplete.)

And it is reported «يُسْتَخْبَلُوا المالَ يُخْبِلوا». And Abū al-Najm said:

3889 - He gave and was not stingy, nor made stingy ... humped, high-backed (camels), from the gift of the one who gives gifts

The reality of «خَوَّل» is from one of two senses: either from their saying "he is a khāʾil of wealth" when he looks after it, taking good care of it; or from khāla yakhūlu, when he is conceited and boastful, and of it is the saying "the rich man is long of skirt, swaggering". The derivation of this root was fully given in al-Anʿām.

His saying: «منه»: It may be attached to «خَوَّل», or attached to something omitted as an adjective of «نِعْمة».

His saying: {مَا كَانَ يدعوا}: Four views are possible for this «ما». One: that it is a relative noun meaning "that which", with the harm meant by it, i.e. "he forgot the harm for whose removal he used to call". Two: that it is in the sense of "the one who", with the Creator, the Exalted, meant by it, i.e. "he forgot Allah, to whom he used to plead"; this is according to those who allow «ما» for those with knowledge. Three: that «ما» is maṣdarī, i.e. "he forgot his having been a supplicant". Four: that «ما» is negative; on this the statement is complete at His saying «نَسِيَ», then He began anew a report with a negated sentence, the implied form being: "he forgot what he was in; the supplication of this disbeliever was not sincere to Allah the Exalted". And «من قبلُ» means "before the harm" on the last view; on the views before it, the implied form is "before the bestowal of the favour".

His saying: «لِيُضِلَّ»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «لِيَضِلَّ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, i.e. "that he himself go astray". The others read it with ḍamma, i.e. he was not content with his own going astray until he made others do so as well; its object is omitted, and it has parallels already given. The lām may be for cause, or for consequence.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ}: The two Ḥaramī readers, Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr, read it with lightened mīm (amman); the rest read it with doubled mīm (ammann). As for the first, there are two views. One: that it is the interrogative hamza entering upon «مَنْ» in the sense of "the one who", the interrogation being one of affirmation, and its counterpart omitted, the implied form being: "Is he who is devout like one who sets up rivals to Allah the Exalted?", or "Is he who is devout like another?", or the implied form: "Is this devout one better, or the disbeliever addressed in His saying {قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلاً}?" What indicates this is His saying {قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الذين يَعْلَمُونَ والذين لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ}; so he omitted the khabar of the mubtadaʾ or the counterpart of what is asked about. The first two implied forms are preferable because less is omitted. Of omitting the counterpart because of indication is the poet's saying:

3890 - The heart called me to her; I am to her affair ... listening, yet I do not know: is pursuing her right guidance? meaning: "or error".

The second: that the hamza is for calling, «مَنْ» being the one called, the one called being the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who is the one commanded by His saying {قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الذين يَعْلَمُونَ}, as if He said: "O you who are devout, say such-and-such", like the other's saying:

3891 - O Zayd, brother of Warqāʾ, if you are seeking revenge ... ...

There is remoteness in this, and no vocative with other than yā occurs in the Qur'an so that this could be carried on it. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) weakened this view also, because it is extraneous to what precedes and what follows. I say: it was said earlier that it is not extraneous to what follows, since the one called is the one commanded to speak. Al-Fārisī also weakened it with something close to this. Abū Ḥātim and al-Akhfash have been bold against the reader of this reading.

As for the second reading, it is «أم» entering upon the relative «مَنْ» as well, so the mīm is assimilated. There are two views on «أم» then. One: that it is connected, its counterpart omitted, the implied form being: "Is the disbeliever better, or the one who is devout?" This is the meaning of al-Akhfash's saying. The Shaykh said: "Omitting the counterpart when it is first requires attestation from usage." It is also said: the implied form is: "Is he who disobeys (like) he who obeys, so that they are equal?" The khabar is omitted because His saying {قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الذين يَعْلَمُونَ} indicates it. The second: that it is disconnected, so it is implied as "rather" plus the hamza, i.e. "Rather, is he who is devout like another, or like the disbeliever to whom it was said: enjoy your disbelief?" Abū Jaʿfar said: "It is in the sense of 'rather', and «مَنْ» in the sense of 'the one who', the implied form being: 'rather, the one who is devout is better than the one mentioned before him.'" This implied form was criticised in that the one mentioned before has no merit at all so that this one could be better than him. What should be implied is: "rather, the one who is devout is of the companions of Paradise", because what is for its counterpart indicates it, in His saying {إِنَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النار}. And «آناءَ» is accusative as an adverbial; its derivation and the discussion of its singular came earlier.

His saying: «ساجِداً وقائماً»: Two ḥāls. As to their owner there are two views. The apparent: that it is the latent pronoun in «قانِتٌ». The second: that it is the pronoun that is nominative by «يَحْذَرُ», fronted before their governor. The majority read both accusative. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read both nominative, on one of two views: either as adjectives of «قَانِتٌ», or as khabar after khabar.

His saying: «يَحْذَر»: It may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «قانتٌ», or a ḥāl from the pronoun in «ساجداً وقائماً», or resumptive as an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "What is his state that he is devout during the hours of the night and tires and exhausts himself?" So it was said: "He is wary of the Hereafter and hopes for the mercy of his Lord", i.e. the punishment of the Hereafter. And {إِنَّمَا يَذَّكَّرُ أُوْلُو} was read with the tāʾ assimilated into the dhāl.

semin-durr:10-10.t: His saying: {فِي هذه الدنيا}: It may be attached to the preceding verb, with the adjective of «حسنةٌ» omitted, since the meaning is "a great good", because one who does a good deed in this world is not promised an unqualified good but one qualified by greatness; or it may be attached to something omitted as a ḥāl from «حسنة» which was an adjective of it, and when it was fronted it remained a ḥāl. And «بغيرِ حسابٍ» is a ḥāl, either from «أَجْرَهم» or from «الصابرون», i.e. "not reckoned against", or "not being reckoned with".

semin-durr:12-12.t:
His saying: {وَأُمِرْتُ لأَنْ أَكُونَ}: There are two views on this lām. One: that it is for cause, the implied form being: "and I was commanded with what I was commanded in order that I be...". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: how did he conjoin «أُمِرْت» to «أُمِرت» when they are one? I say: they are not one, because their aspects differ: the command to sincerity and its imposition is one thing, and the command to it so that he secure the lead in religion is another. When two aspects and two attributes of a thing differ, it is thereby treated as two different things." The second: that the lām is redundant before «أَنْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "You may make the lām redundant, like it in your saying 'I wished to do' (aradtu li-an afʿala); it is not added except with «أَنْ» in particular and not with an explicit noun, as if it were added as compensation for leaving the original for what stands in its place, as the sīn in «اسطاع» was a compensation for leaving the original, which is aṭwaʿa. The evidence for this view is its coming without a lām in His saying: {وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ المسلمين} [Yūnus: 72], {وَأُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِنَ المؤمنين} [Yūnus: 104], {أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ مَنْ أَسْلَمَ} [al-Anʿām: 14]." End of quotation.

His saying "it is not added except with «أنْ»" is open to doubt, in that it is added regularly when the governed element is fronted or the governor is derivative, and irregularly in other than these two cases; and none of the grammarians mentioned this breakdown. His saying "as the sīn in «اسْطاع» was a compensation" is on one of two views; the other view is that it is istaṭāʿa from which the tāʾ of istifʿāl was dropped. And his saying "the evidence for it is its coming without a lām" may be answered: its original is with the lām, and it was dropped only because the dropping of a preposition is regular with «أنْ» and «أنَّ»; and what was commanded is omitted, the implied form being: "and I was commanded to worship, in order that I be".

semin-durr:14-14.t: His saying: {قُلِ الله أَعْبُدُ}: The majestic name is fronted, according to some, to convey specificity. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "And because of its indication of that, he put the One worshipped before the act of worship here and delayed it in the first; the speech at first concerns the act itself and bringing it about, and second concerns the one for whose sake the act is done; for that reason he built on it His saying {فاعبدوا مَا شِئْتُمْ مِّن دُونِهِ}."

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {لَهُمْ مِّن فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ}: The khabar may be either of the two preceding prepositional phrases, though the apparent course is to make the first the khabar; «مِنْ فوقِهم» is then either a ḥāl from «ظُلَل», attached to something omitted, or attached to what the khabar is attached to; and «مِن النار» is an adjective of «ظُلَل». And His saying {وَمِن تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ} is as above; He called them "canopies" (ẓilāl) in relation to those beneath them.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {أَن يَعْبُدُوهَا}: The pronoun refers to al-ṭāghūt, because it is feminine; the discussion of it was given fully in al-Baqara. And «أَنْ يعبدوها» is in the position of accusative as a badal al-ishtimāl from al-ṭāghūt, as if it were said: "avoid the worship of al-ṭāghūt". The relative is a mubtadaʾ, and the sentence «لهم البشرى» is the khabar. It is also said: «لهم» is itself the khabar, with «البُشْرى» as its agent; this is preferable because it is a case of predicating with single words. And His saying «فبَشِّرْ عبادي» is a placing of the overt noun in the place of the pronoun, i.e. "so give them good tidings", meaning those who avoid; this was done only to state the mentioned attribute explicitly.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {الذين يَسْتَمِعُونَ}: Apparently it is an adjective of «عبادي», or a badal from it, or a bayān of it. It is also said: it may be a mubtadaʾ, with His saying {أولئك الذين} etc. as its khabar. On this the pause is at His saying «عبادي», and the beginning is with what follows.

semin-durr:19-19.t: His saying: {أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ}: There are two views on this «مَنْ». The more apparent: that it is a relative in the position of nominative as a mubtadaʾ, its khabar omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied "like him who was saved". Al-Zamakhsharī implied: "so you rescue him", saying: "It was omitted because «أفأنت تُنْقِذُ» indicates it." Others implied "you grieve over him", and others "he escapes from it", i.e. from the punishment. And al-Zamakhsharī, as is his custom, implied a sentence between the hamza and the fāʾ, its implied form being: "Are you the master of their affair? So whoever the word of punishment has become due against..." As for others, they claim that the original is that the fāʾ is fronted and was delayed only because of what the hamza deserves of first place. The verification of these two views has been given more than once. The second: that «مَنْ» is conditional, and its apodosis is «أفأنت»; the fāʾ is the fāʾ of the apodosis entering upon the sentence of recompense, and the hamza is repeated to emphasise the meaning of denial, and the overt noun {مَن فِي النار} is placed where the pronoun should be, since the original was "Can you rescue him?"; it was put in its place only as testimony against him of that. Al-Ḥawfī and al-Zamakhsharī leaned toward this. Al-Ḥawfī said: "The interrogative alif was brought in, for emphasis, when the speech became long, and were it not for its length it would not be permissible to bring it, for it is not right in Arabic to bring an interrogative alif with the noun and another alif with the recompense. The meaning of the speech is: Can you rescue him?" On the view that it is conditional, a question arises between al-Zamakhsharī's view and that of the majority: on the majority view, a condition and an interrogation have been combined, and there is then a disagreement between Sībawayh and Yūnus: is the last sentence the answer to the interrogation, which is Yūnus's saying, or the answer to the condition, which is Sībawayh's saying? As for al-Zamakhsharī's view, no condition and interrogation have been combined, since the interrogative particle according to him enters upon an omitted sentence, to which the conditional sentence is conjoined, and it did not enter upon the conditional sentence. His saying «أفأنت تُنْقِذُ» is an interrogation of confrontation, and the pronoun is fronted in it to signal that you are not able to rescue him; the only one able to do so is Allah alone.

semin-durr:20-20.t:
His saying: {لكن الذين اتقوا}: An istidrāk (rectification) between two opposites or contraries, namely the believers and the disbelievers.

And His saying: «وَعْدَ اللَّهِ»: A confirmatory maṣdar of the content of the sentence, so it is accusative by an obligatorily implied verb.

semin-durr:21-21.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ}: The majority read the verb nominative, conjoined to what precedes. Abū Bishr read «ثم يَجْعَلَه» accusative. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said: "The author of al-Kāmil said: 'It is weak.'" End of quotation. He means by the author of al-Kāmil "al-Hudhalī". Neither he nor the author of al-Kāmil explained the reason for its weakness or its analysis. As for its weakness, it is clear, since nothing preceded that apparently requires the accusative. As for its analysis, Abū al-Baqāʾ mentioned two views. One: that it is accusative by an implied «أن» and is conjoined to His saying {أَنَّ الله أَنزَلَ مِنَ السمآء مَآءً} at the beginning of the verse, the implied form being: "Have you not seen Allah's sending down, then His making it...". The second: that it is accusative by the implying of «تَرَى», i.e. "then you see its being made chaff". He means that it is accusative by an implied «أنْ», and «أنْ» and what is in its sphere is an object of an implied verb, which is «تَرَى», because «ألم تَرَ» indicates it.

semin-durr:22-22.t: His saying: {أَفَمَن شَرَحَ الله}: And {أَفَمَن يَتَّقِي} [al-Zumar: 24] are as was said at {أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ} [al-Zumar: 19]. The implied form is: "Is he whose breast Allah has opened to Islam like him whose heart is hardened?", or "like the hardened one who turns away", as His saying {فَوَيْلٌ لِّلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ} indicates it. Likewise the implied form in «أفَمَنْ يَتَّقِي» is "like him who is secure from punishment", which is al-Zamakhsharī's implied form, or "like those enjoying bliss in Paradise", which is Ibn ʿAṭiyya's implied form.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {كِتَاباً}: There are two views on it. The more apparent: that it is a badal from «أحسنَ الحديث». The second: that it is a ḥāl from it. The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) said — when he transmitted it from al-Zamakhsharī: "It is as if built on the basis that «أَحْسَن الحديث» is definite because of its annexation to a definite, whereas there is a disagreement about the elative when annexed to a definite: it is said that its annexation is genuine (maḥḍa), and it is said that it is not genuine." I say: even if it is indefinite, it is also good for it to be a ḥāl, because whenever an indefinite is annexed, a ḥāl from it is allowed without disagreement. The correct view is that the annexation of afʿal is genuine. And «مُتَشابِهاً» is an adjective of «كتاب», and it is what justifies the coming of an inert noun as a ḥāl, or it is because it is equivalent in force to "written".

The majority read «مثانيَ» with fatḥa on the yāʾ, as a second adjective, or another ḥāl, or a tamyīz transferred from agency, i.e. "its mathānī being similar"; al-Zamakhsharī held this. Hishām, from Ibn ʿĀmir, and Abū Bishr read it with sukūn on it, and there are two views on this. One: that it is a case of making the weak letter sākin out of reluctance to put a vowel on it, like the reading «تُطْعِمُوْن أهاليْكم» and his saying:

3892 - As if their hands (aydīhinna) ... ... (Translator's note: the verse is incomplete in the source.)

and the like. The second: that it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is mathānī", as the Shaykh mentioned. There is some doubt about this, since it should have been given tanwīn and its yāʾ dropped because of the meeting of two sukūns, so that one says mathānin, as you say hāʾulāʾi jawārin. It may be said: it was stopped upon, and then the connected form was treated as the pause; but it may be objected that pausing on a defective noun with tanwīn is by dropping the yāʾ, as in hādhā qāḍ, and retaining it is a rare dialect. This may be answered: it has been read thus in the mutawātir readings, such as {مِنْ والي}, {باقي} and {هادي} in the reading of Ibn Kathīr.

His saying: «تَقْشَعِرُّ»: This sentence may be an adjective of «كتاب», or a ḥāl from it because of its specification by the adjective, or resumptive. Iqshaʿarra jildhu: when the skin contracts and gathers from fear, and the hair stands. The maṣdar is iqshiʿrār and also qushaʿrīra. The pattern of iqshaʿarra is ifʿalalla; the pattern of qushaʿrīra is faʿallīla.

And «مَثاني» is the plural of mathnā, because in it is the repetition of stories and exhortations; or the plural of mathnā, a maf ʿal pattern from tathniya, in the sense of repetition. «كتاب», though singular, is described by mathānī, a plural, because the Book includes sūras and verses; or it is of the type "a pot in pieces" (burma aʿshār) and "a garment in rags" (thawb akhlāq), as al-Zamakhsharī said. It is also said: there is an omitted noun described, i.e. "repeated sections", omitted because of indication.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {قُرْآناً عَرَبِيّاً}: There are three views on it. One: that it is accusative for praise, because when it is indefinite, following «القرآن» is impossible. Two: that it is accusative by «يتذكَّرون», i.e. "they remember a Qur'an". Three: that it is accusative as a ḥāl from «القرآن», as a confirmatory ḥāl, and it is called a ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa (a preparatory one), because the real ḥāl is «عربياً» and «قرآناً» is a preparation for it, like "Zayd came, a righteous man".

His saying: {غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ}: An adjective of «قرآناً», or another ḥāl. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you ask: why was it not said 'straight' or 'not crooked'? I say: there are two benefits in it. One: the negation of there ever being any crookedness in it, as He said {وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا} [al-Kahf: 1]. The second: that ʿiwaj is specific to meanings, not to concrete things. It is also said that what is meant by ʿiwaj is doubt and confusion." And he cited:

3893 - And certainty has come to you, free of crookedness ... from the Deity, and a word not belied

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ}: This may be a sentence of mubtadaʾ and khabar in the position of accusative as an adjective of «رجل», or the description may be the preposition and its genitive noun alone, with «شركاءُ» its agent, which is preferable because of its closeness to the single word. And «مُتَشاكِسُوْن» is an adjective of «شركاء». Al-Tashākus is disagreement. Its origin is bad character and difficulty, which is the cause of disagreement and quarrelling. One also says al-tashākus and al-tashākhus, with khāʾ in place of the kāf. The discussion of the accusative of al-mathal and what comes after it after «ضَرَب» has already been given. Al-Kisāʾī said: «رجلاً» is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "for a man" or "in a man".

And His saying: «فيه» means "in the owning of him". Abū al-Baqāʾ said something that does not seem to come from the like of him, or even from lesser. He said: "«وفيه شركاءُ»: the sentence is an adjective of «رجل», and «في» is attached to «متشاكسون». In it is evidence for the permissibility of fronting the khabar of the mubtadaʾ before it." End of quotation. As for this, I do not doubt that it is an oversight, because, having made it a sentence, how can he then say that «فيه» is attached to «متشاكسون»? It may be said that he meant in terms of meaning, but that is very remote. Then his saying "in it is evidence" to the end also contradicts it. And the matter is not an unusual one so that he should say "in it is evidence". It seems he meant: in it is evidence for fronting the governed element of the khabar before the mubtadaʾ, on the basis that «فيه» is attached to «متشاكسون»; but this is invalid, and what is invalid is not to be sought to be set right.

His saying: «سَلَماً لرَجُلٍ»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «سالماً» with an alif and kasra on the lām. The others read «سَلَماً» with fatḥa on the sīn and the lām. Ibn Jubayr read it with kasra on the sīn and sukūn on the lām (silman). The first reading is an active participle from salima lahu kadhā, so he is sālim. The other two readings, salaman and silman, are both maṣdars, used as descriptions by way of exaggeration, or by an omitted muḍāf, or by occupying the place of the active participle, so they revert to being like the first reading. «ورجلٌ سالِمٌ» was also read with both nominative. There are two views on it. One: that it is a mubtadaʾ with an omitted khabar, the implied form being "and there is a man wholly devoted to one man", as al-Zamakhsharī implied it. Two: that it is a mubtadaʾ and «سالمٌ» its khabar. Beginning with an indefinite is allowed because it is a place of breakdown, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

3894 - When it (the child) cried behind her, she turned to him ... with half of her, and the other half of her with us was not turned

and their saying: "People are two men: a man I honoured, and a man I insulted".

His saying: «مَثَلاً»: Accusative as a tamyīz transferred from agency, since the original is "Are their likenesses equal?". The tamyīz is singular because it was limited to it at first in His saying {ضَرَبَ الله مَثَلاً}. «مِثْلَيْن» was also read, so it corresponds to the states of the two men. Al-Zamakhsharī said — regarding the reading «مِثْلين» — "The pronoun in «يَسْتَويان» refers to the two likenesses, because the implied form is: the likeness of a man and the likeness of a man. The meaning is: are the two equal in what returns to the quality of description, as you say: «كفى بهما رجلين»."

The Shaykh said: "Apparently the pronoun in «يَسْتَويان» refers to «رَجُلَيْن». But if you make it refer to the two likenesses which he said is the implied form, 'the likeness of a man and the likeness of a man', then the tamyīz would by then have been understood from the specified, which is the pronoun, since the implied form becomes: 'Are the two likenesses equal, as two likenesses?'" I say: this does no harm, since the implied form is: "Are the two likenesses equal, as two likenesses, in the quality of description?" The first two likenesses are the familiar ones, and the second two are two indefinite classes, as you say «كَفَى بهما رجلَيْن»: the pronoun in «بهما» refers to what is meant by the two men, so there is no difference between the two cases. Whatever is the answer for «كفَى بهما رجلين» is the answer for it.

semin-durr:30-30.t: His saying: {إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَّيِّتُونَ}: The majority read «مَيِّت ومَيِّتون». Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and al-Yamānī read «مائِتٌ ومائتون», which is an adjective suggesting occurrence (in time), unlike «مَيِّت». It was mentioned earlier that there is no disagreement among the readers on the doubling of the like of this. «ثم إنكم»: the second person is given precedence, though it is singular in His saying «إنَّك», over the third persons in «وإنَّهم».

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {والذي جَآءَ}: «بالصدق»: its wording is singular, and its meaning is plural, because the class is meant by it. It is also said: because recompense is intended by it, and where that is so, «الذي» frequently occurs in place of «الذين»; for that reason its meaning was respected, so it was made plural in His saying {أولئك هُمُ المتقون}, as the meaning of «مَنْ» was respected in His saying «للكافرين»; for «الكافرين» is an overt noun in place of the pronoun, since the original is "an abode for them". It is also said: rather the original is «والذين جاء بالصدق», with the nūn dropped for lightness, as in His saying {وَخُضْتُمْ كالذي خاضوا} [al-Tawba: 69]. This is an error, since had that been intended, a plural pronoun would have followed, and it would have been said «والذي جاؤوا», as in «كالذي خاضُوا». What indicates this is that when the dual nūn is dropped, the pronoun returns as a dual, as in his saying:

3895 - O sons of Kulayb, my two paternal uncles, the two who (alladhā) ... killed the kings and unfastened the shackles

and it would have come as in his saying:

3896 - And those whose (alladhī) blood was shed at Falj ... they are the people, the whole of the people, O Umm Khālid

ʿAbd Allāh (ibn Masʿūd) read {والذي جَآؤوا بالصدق وَصَدَّقَوا بِهِ}. The verification of a verse like this was given earlier at the beginning of al-Baqara and elsewhere. It is also said: «الذي» is an adjective of an omitted noun with a plural sense, the implied form being "the party" or "the company", and for that reason He said {أولئك هُمُ المتقون}. It is also said: what is meant by «الذي» is one particular person, Muḥammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; but since what is meant is he and his followers, that was taken into account and so it was made plural, and He said «أولئك هم», as in His saying {وَلَقَدْ آتَيْنَا موسى الكتاب لَعَلَّهُمْ يَهْتَدُونَ} [al-Muʾminūn: 49]. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, and his wording is: "He is the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace; He meant him and those who followed him, as He meant by Moses him and his people." The Shaykh (Abū Ḥayyān) took issue with him over placing the detached pronoun where the attached one belongs, saying: "Its correction is to say: 'He meant him by it, as He meant him by Moses and his people.'" I say: there is no basis for the objection, because with the fronting of «به» and «بموسى» for one of the purposes, attachment of the pronoun is impossible. This is like the discussion that came to you at His saying, the Exalted: {وَلَقَدْ وَصَّيْنَا الذين أُوتُواْ الكتاب مِن قَبْلِكُمْ وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 131] and His saying {يُخْرِجُونَ الرسول وَإِيَّاكُمْ} [al-Mumtaḥana: 1]: some people claimed that detachment is allowed even with the ability to attach; the answer given earlier was close to what I mention here, and I explained the wisdom of the fronting there. Al-Zamakhsharī's statement that the pronoun in «لعلهم يَهْتدون» refers to Moses and his people is open to doubt; rather the apparent is that the pronoun is specific to his people and not him, because they are the ones from whom guidance is sought; as for Moses, peace be upon him, he is rightly guided and firm in guidance. Al-Zamakhsharī also said: "It is possible that He means: the party or the group who brought the truth and believed in it, and they are the Messenger who brought the truth and his Companions who believed in it." The Shaykh said: "In it is a distribution of the ṣila, and the party is the relative; so it is like your saying: 'The party that honoured and honoured came'. The more apparent is no distribution; rather, what is conjoined to the ṣila is a ṣila for the one who has the first ṣila."

Abū Ṣāliḥ, ʿIkrima ibn Sulaymān and Muḥammad ibn Juḥāda read it lightened (ṣaddaqa → ṣadaqa), meaning "he was truthful in it" and did not change it. «وصُدِّق به» was also read, doubled and passive.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {لِيُكَفِّرَ}: There are two views on its attachment. One: that it is attached to something omitted, i.e. "He made that easy for them so that He might expiate". The second: that it is attached to «المحسنين» itself, as if it were said: "Those who did good, so that He might expiate", i.e. for the sake of expiation.

His saying: «أسْوَأَ الذي»: Apparently it is an elative, and the majority read it so. It is also said: it is not an elative but in the sense of "the bad of what they did", like their saying «الأَشَجُّ والناقص أعدلُ بني مروان», i.e. "the two just ones among them". What indicates this is the reading of Ibn Kathīr in one transmission, «أَسْواءَ», with an alif between the wāw and the hamza, on the pattern of aḥmāl, a plural of sūʾ; and likewise he read in Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda.

ukberi-tibyan:1-3.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ (١) إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتَابَ بِالْحَقِّ فَاعْبُدِ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينَ (٢) أَلَا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الْخَالِصُ وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِيَاءَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونَا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفَى إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ فِي مَا هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يَهْدِي مَنْ هُوَ كَاذِبٌ كَفَّارٌ (٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتَابِ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «مِنَ اللَّهِ» is the khabar (predicate).
It may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "this is a sending down" (هَذَا تَنْزِيلٌ). And (مِنْ) is then attached (mutaʿalliq) to the maṣdar (verbal noun), or is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الْكِتَاب. And (الدِّينَ) is accusative by مُخْلِص, and مُخْلِصًا is a ḥāl.
Al-Farrāʾ permitted (لَهُ الدِّينُ) in the nominative [Translator's note: the source prints «الدِّينَ»], as a resumptive clause.
(وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا): a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "they say: We do not worship them…" (يَقُولُونَ مَا نَعْبُدُهُمْ).
And (زُلْفَى) is a maṣdar, or an emphatic ḥāl (ḥāl muʾakkida).

ukberi-tibyan:5-6.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهَارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهَارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى أَلَا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ (٥) خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْهَا زَوْجَهَا وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَنْعَامِ ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَاتِكُمْ خَلْقًا مِنْ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ فِي ظُلُمَاتٍ ثَلَاثٍ ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُصْرَفُونَ (٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (يُكَوِّرُ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) or resumptive. And «يَخْلُقُكُمْ» is resumptive, and «خَلْقًا» is a maṣdar (verbal noun) from it; «فِي» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to it, or to the second خَلْق, because the first is emphatic and so does not govern.
And (رَبُّكُمْ) is a naʿt (adjective) or a badal (substitute); as for the khabar (predicate), it is اللَّه. And (لَهُ الْمُلْكُ) is a second khabar, or resumptive. It is also permissible that «اللَّهُ» be a badal from ذَلِكُمْ [Translator's note: the source prints ذَلِكَ], with the khabar being لَهُ الْمُلْكُ. And (لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ) is resumptive, or another khabar.
And (يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ) [Translator's note: from the following verse, 7]: with a ḍamma on the hāʾ, with it pronounced fleetingly (ikhtilās), and with a sukūn on it; the like of this has been dealt with at (يُؤَدِّهِ إِلَيْكَ).

ukberi-tibyan:7-8.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (إِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنْكُمْ وَلَا يَرْضَى لِعِبَادِهِ الْكُفْرَ وَإِنْ تَشْكُرُوا يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ وَلَا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَى ثُمَّ إِلَى رَبِّكُمْ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِمَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذَاتِ الصُّدُورِ (٧) وَإِذَا مَسَّ الْإِنْسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَا رَبَّهُ مُنِيبًا إِلَيْهِ ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلَهُ نِعْمَةً مِنْهُ نَسِيَ مَا كَانَ يَدْعُو إِلَيْهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَنْدَادًا لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ النَّارِ (٨)).
And (مُنِيبًا) is a ḥāl (circumstantial). And «مِنْهُ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to خَوَّلَ, or is an adjective (ṣifa) of نِعْمَة.

ukberi-tibyan:9-10.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَمَّنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ آنَاءَ اللَّيْلِ سَاجِدًا وَقَائِمًا يَحْذَرُ الْآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُو رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ (٩) قُلْ يَاعِبَادِي الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا فِي هَذِهِ الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةٌ وَأَرْضُ اللَّهِ وَاسِعَةٌ إِنَّمَا يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ (١٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ): it is read with the doubled consonant [Translator's note: i.e. أَمَّنْ], the origin being أَمْ مَنْ; so أَمْ is interrogative and disconnected (munqaṭiʿa), i.e. "rather, is he who is devoutly obedient…" (بَلْ أَمْ مَنْ هُوَ قَانِتٌ).
It has been said: it is connected (muttaṣila), its implied form being: "Are he who disobeys and he who is obedient equal?" (أَمْ مَنْ يَعْصِي، أَمْ مَنْ هُوَ مُطِيعٌ مُسْتَوِيَانِ); the khabar (predicate) is omitted because His saying, Exalted is He, «هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ» indicates it.
It is also read with the undoubled consonant [Translator's note: i.e. أَمَنْ], and it contains the interrogative; the counterpart (al-muʿādil) and the khabar are both omitted. It has been said: it is the hamza of the vocative.
And (سَاجِدًا وَقَائِمًا) are two ḥāls (circumstantials) from the pronoun in «قَانِتٍ», or from the pronoun in «يَحْذَرُ».
And (بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ) is a ḥāl from the reward, i.e. "in full" (مُوَفَّرًا), or from the patient, i.e. "not called to account" (غَيْرَ مُحَاسَبِينَ).

ukberi-tibyan:14-14.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلِ اللَّهَ أَعْبُدُ مُخْلِصًا لَهُ دِينِي (١٤)).
(قُلِ اللَّهَ): it is accusative by «أَعْبُدُ».

ukberi-tibyan:16-17.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (لَهُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ مِنَ النَّارِ وَمِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ ذَلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ اللَّهُ بِهِ عِبَادَهُ يَا عِبَادِ فَاتَّقُونِ (١٦) وَالَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوهَا وَأَنَابُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ لَهُمُ الْبُشْرَى فَبَشِّرْ عِبَادِ (١٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ظُلَلٌ): it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «لَهُمُ» is the khabar (predicate).
And (مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ): its governor may be the preposition-phrase; or it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «ظُلَلٌ», the implied form being "canopies being above them" (ظُلَلٌ كَائِنَةٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ).
And (مِنَ النَّارِ) is a naʿt (adjective) of ظُلَل.
And (الطَّاغُوتُ) is feminine, and the pronoun here comes accordingly.

ukberi-tibyan:19-20.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ الْعَذَابِ أَفَأَنْتَ تُنْقِذُ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ (١٩) لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ غُرَفٌ مِنْ فَوْقِهَا غُرَفٌ مَبْنِيَّةٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لَا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ الْمِيعَادَ (٢٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَمَنْ): a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "like one who is saved" (كَمَنْ نَجَا).
And (وَعْدَ) is a maṣdar (verbal noun) whose governor is indicated by His saying «لَهُمْ غُرَفٌ», because it is like your saying "He promised them" (وَعَدَهُمْ).

ukberi-tibyan:21-21.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنَابِيعَ فِي الْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعًا مُخْتَلِفًا أَلْوَانُهُ ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَرَاهُ مُصْفَرًّا ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطَامًا إِنَّ فِي ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرَى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ (٢١)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ): the majority read the nominative [Translator's note: i.e. the indicative].
It has been read, as an irregular (shādhdh) reading, with the accusative; its explanation is that «أَنْ» is implied with it, and what it is conjoined to is «أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ» at the beginning of the verse, the implied form being: "Have you not seen Allah's sending down — or [looked] to His sending down — and then His making it…" (أَلَمْ تَرَ إِنْزَالَ اللَّهِ، أَوْ إِلَى إِنْزَالِهِ ثُمَّ جَعَلَهُ).
It may also be accusative on the implied form "you see His making it chaff" (تَرَى جَعْلَهُ حُطَامًا).

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَامِ فَهُوَ عَلَى نُورٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ فَوَيْلٌ لِلْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ (٢٢)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ) and (أَفَمَنْ يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ): the ruling on both is like the ruling on His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ), which has already been dealt with.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (اللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيثِ كِتَابًا مُتَشَابِهًا مَثَانِيَ تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ ذَلِكَ هُدَى اللَّهِ يَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ هَادٍ (٢٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كِتَابًا): it is a badal (substitute) from «أَحْسَنَ», and «تَقْشَعِرُّ» is a third naʿt (adjective).

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنَا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هَذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ (٢٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُرْآنًا): it is a preparatory ḥāl (ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa) from الْقُرْآن; the ḥāl in meaning is His saying, Exalted is He: (عَرَبِيًّا).
It has been said: it is accusative by «يَتَذَكَّرُونَ».

ukberi-tibyan:29-29.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكَاءُ مُتَشَاكِسُونَ وَرَجُلًا سَلَمًا لِرَجُلٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٢٩)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (مَثَلًا رَجُلًا): «رَجُلًا» is a badal (substitute) from «مَثَلًا»; it has been dealt with at His saying (مَثَلًا قَرْيَةً) in al-Naḥl.
And (فِيهِ شُرَكَاءُ): the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of رَجُل, and «فِيهِ» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «مُتَشَاكِسُونَ»; this is evidence that it is permissible for [what belongs to] the khabar (predicate) of a mubtadaʾ (subject) to precede it. And «مَثَلًا» [Translator's note: the second, in هَلْ يَسْتَوِيَانِ مَثَلًا] is a tamyīz (specification).

ukberi-tibyan:33-33.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَالَّذِي جَاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ (٣٣)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالَّذِي جَاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ): the meaning is plural; the like of it has been dealt with at His saying: (مَثَلُهُمْ كَمَثَلِ الَّذِي).

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلْ أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ مَا تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ إِنْ أَرَادَنِيَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ هَلْ هُنَّ كَاشِفَاتُ ضُرِّهِ أَوْ أَرَادَنِي بِرَحْمَةٍ هَلْ هُنَّ مُمْسِكَاتُ رَحْمَتِهِ قُلْ حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ يَتَوَكَّلُ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ (٣٨)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (كَاشِفَاتُ ضُرِّهِ): it is read with tanwīn and with annexation (iḍāfa); this is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ أَنْتَ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ عِبَادِكَ فِي مَا كَانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ (٤٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ): like (قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ مَالِكَ الْمُلْكِ).

ukberi-tibyan:49-49.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (فَإِذَا مَسَّ الْإِنْسَانَ ضُرٌّ دَعَانَا ثُمَّ إِذَا خَوَّلْنَاهُ نِعْمَةً مِنَّا قَالَ إِنَّمَا أُوتِيتُهُ عَلَى عِلْمٍ بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ وَلَكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ (٤٦)) [Translator's note: so numbered in the source; this is verse 49].
His saying, Exalted is He: (بَلْ هِيَ): «هِيَ» is the pronoun of the trial (al-balwā), or of the state (al-ḥāl).

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يَا حَسْرَتَا عَلَى مَا فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنَ السَّاخِرِينَ (٥٦)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَنْ تَقُولَ): it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "We warned you for fear that [a soul] should say" (أَنْذَرْنَاكُمْ مَخَافَةَ أَنْ تَقُولَ).
(يَاحَسْرَتَا): the alif is substituted for the yāʾ of the first person.
It has been read «حَسْرَتَايَ», and this is far-fetched; it has been explained on the view that the yāʾ was added after the alif that had been converted [from it].
Others said: rather, the alif is augmentative. This is more far-fetched, because of the separation it involves between the muḍāf and the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (بَلَى قَدْ جَاءَتْكَ آيَاتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِهَا وَاسْتَكْبَرْتَ وَكُنْتَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ (٥٩)).
The kāf in «جَاءَتْكَ» is given a fatḥa by construing it on the one addressed, who is a human being [Translator's note: i.e. masculine]; whoever gives it a kasra construes it on the feminine gender of النَّفْس (the soul).

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ تَرَى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةٌ أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوًى لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ (٦٠)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وُجُوهُهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةٌ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا», because «تَرَى» is from seeing with the eye.
It has also been said: it has the sense of knowing, so the clause would be a second mafʿūl bihi (direct object).
Had it been read «وُجُوهَهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةً» with the accusative, it would have been as a badal (substitute) of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl).

ukberi-tibyan:61-61.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَيُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفَازَتِهِمْ لَا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ وَلَا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ (٦١)).
And (مَفَازَتِهِمْ): [it is read] in the singular, because it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and in the plural because of the differing kinds of the maṣdars, like الحُلُوم (minds) and الأَشْغَال (occupations). It has also been said: الْمَفَازَة here means the road, and the meaning is: "in their place of safety (فِي مَفَازَتِهِمْ)".
(لَا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ): a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:64-64.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (قُلْ أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَأْمُرُونِّي أَعْبُدُ أَيُّهَا الْجَاهِلُونَ (٦٤)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ): there are several views on its i'rab:
The first: that «غَيْرَ» is accusative (manṣūb) by «أَعْبُدُ», placed before it. This view has been judged weak on the ground that the implied form is «أَنْ أَعْبُدَ», and in that case it would lead to placing the ṣila (relative clause) before the relative [particle]. But this is nothing, because «أَنْ» is not in the wording, so its governing effect does not remain; and if we were to suppose that its rule remained, it would lead to omitting the relative [particle] while keeping its ṣila, and that is not permitted except under the necessity of poetry. The second view: that it is accusative by «تَأْمُرُونِّي», with «أَعْبُدُ» a badal (substitute) from it, the implied form being: "Say: do you then command me to the worship of other than Allah, Mighty and Majestic (قُلْ أَفَتَأْمُرُونِّي بِعِبَادَةِ غَيْرِ اللَّهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ)?" This is a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl), and of the pattern «أَمَرْتُكَ الْخَيْرَ» ("I commanded you [to] the good").
The third: that «غَيْرَ» is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. «أَفَتُلْزِمُونِي غَيْرَ اللَّهِ» ("do you then bind me to other than Allah?"), and what follows explains it.
It has also been said: «أَعْبُدَ» has no position in the i'rab. And it has been said: it is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the governing [of «غَيْرَ»] is according to the first two views. As for the nūn, it is doubled according to the original form, and it has been lightened by omitting the second one; its parallels have already been mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَمَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ وَالْأَرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ (٦٧)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (وَالْأَرْضُ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «قَبْضَتُهُ» is the khabar (predicate), and جَمِيعًا is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الأرض. The implied form is: "when it is gathered together, [it is] His grasp (إِذَا كَانَتْ مُجْتَمِعَةً قَبْضَتُهُ)", i.e. grasped; so what governs إذا is the maṣdar (verbal noun), because it has the sense of the passive participle. Abū ʿAlī mentioned in al-Ḥujja: the implied form is «ذَاتُ قَبْضَتِهِ» ("the object of His grasp"). This was rejected against him on the ground that the muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct) does not govern what precedes it; but this [rejection] is not sound, because it is now not a muḍāf ilayhi, and after the muḍāf is omitted its rule does not remain.
And قَبْضَتَهُ is read with the accusative, in the sense of «فِي قَبْضَتِهِ» ("in His grasp"); this is weak, because this adverb is delimited, so it is like your saying «زَيْدٌ الدَّارَ».
(وَالسَّماوَاتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ): a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and (بِيَمِينِهِ) is attached to (mutaʿalliq) the khabar. It may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in the khabar, and it may be a second khabar.
And «مَطْوِيَّاتٍ» was read with the kasra, as a ḥāl, with «بِيَمِينِهِ» the khabar. It has also been said: the khabar is omitted, i.e. «وَالسَّمَاوَاتُ قَبْضَتُهُ» ("and the heavens are His grasp").

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ زُمَرًا حَتَّى إِذَا جَاءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلَامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ طِبْتُمْ فَادْخُلُوهَا خَالِدِينَ (٧٣)).
And (زُمَرًا): in both places it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). [Translator's note: the other place is āya 71.] (وَفُتِحَتْ): the wāw is redundant (zāʾida) according to some, because the clause is the answer of حتّى [Translator's note: i.e. of «إِذَا» after حَتَّى]; it is not redundant according to the rigorous scholars, and the answer is omitted, its implied form being "they were at rest (اطْمَأَنُّوا)", or the like. And (نَتَبَوَّأُ): a ḥāl from the fāʿil (agent) or the mafʿūl (object). [Translator's note: نَتَبَوَّأُ occurs in āya 74.]

ukberi-tibyan:74-75.t:
Allah the Exalted says: (وَقَالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَنَا وَعْدَهُ وَأَوْرَثَنَا الْأَرْضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ حَيْثُ نَشَاءُ فَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعَامِلِينَ (٧٤) وَتَرَى الْمَلَائِكَةَ حَافِّينَ مِنْ حَوْلِ الْعَرْشِ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَقِيلَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ (٧٥)).
His saying, Exalted is He: (حَيْثُ): here it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), as we mentioned on His saying (وَكُلَا مِنْهَا رَغَدًا حَيْثُ شِئْتُمَا), according to one of the views. And (حَافِّينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الملائكة.
And (يُسَبِّحُونَ): a ḥāl from the pronoun in (حَافِّينَ). And Allah knows best.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Zumar
Meccan, except for three verses which were revealed in Medina: ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أسْرَفُوا عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 53], up to the completion of three verses. It is called "Sūrat al-Ghuraf (the Chambers)" and it is called "Sūrat al-Zumar (the Groups)". It is narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih that he said: "Whoever would like to know Allah's decree concerning His creation, let him read Sūrat al-Ghuraf."
﷽
His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿تَنْـزِيلُ الكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ العَزِيزِ الحَكِيمِ﴾ ﴿إنّا أنْـزَلْنا إلَيْكَ الكِتابَ بِالحَقِّ﴾ [al-Zumar: 2]: "اَلْكِتابُ" here is the Qur'an. "تَنْزِيلُ الكِتابِ" is nominative in two respects. One of them is as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being "مِنَ اللَّهِ", that is, "it has come down from Allah". It is also possible that its nominative is on [the implied form] "this is the sending down of the Book (هَذا تَنْزِيلُ الكِتابِ)".

zajjaj:2-2.t:
And His saying: ﴿فاعْبُدِ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾: "اَلدِّينَ" is accusative because the action falls upon it, and "مُخْلِصًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), that is: worship Allah affirming His oneness, not associating anything with Him.
One of the grammarians claimed that "مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينُ" is permissible, and said: "اَلدِّينُ" is put in the nominative in your saying "مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينُ", "مُخْلِصًا" being the completion of the sentence, and "لَهُ الدِّينُ" being a nominal clause [lit. a mubtadaʾ]. This is not permissible, for two reasons. One of them is that it has not been read so. The other is that ﴿ألا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الخالِصُ﴾ [al-Zumar: 3] spoils it, since "لَهُ الدِّينُ" would then be repeated in the speech without need; rather, the benefit of ﴿ألا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الخالِصُ﴾ [al-Zumar: 3] becomes fitting by His saying ﴿مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينَ﴾.
The meaning of making the religion pure here is worshipping Allah alone, without partner. This was said to establish the oneness of Allah (tawḥīd) and negate associating partners (shirk). Do you not see His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أوْلِياءَ ما نَعْبُدُهُمْ﴾ [al-Zumar: 3], up to His saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَن هو كاذِبٌ كَفّارٌ﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]? That is: so you make the religion pure, and do not take protectors besides Him. All of this is confirmed by "مُخْلِصًا لَهُ الدِّينَ".
As for the position of ﴿والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أوْلِياءَ ما نَعْبُدُهُمْ﴾ [al-Zumar: 3]: "اَلَّذِينَ" is nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), and its khabar (predicate) is omitted, there being an indication of it in the speech. The meaning is: "and those who take protectors besides Him say: we only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah (والَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِن دُونِهِ أوْلِياءَ يَقُولُونَ ما نَعْبُدُهم إلّا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ زُلْفى)". Further evidence for this is the reading of Ubayy: "ما نَعْبُدُكم إلّا لِتُقَرِّبُونا إلى اللَّهِ" (we only worship you so that you may bring us near to Allah); this confirms that it is reported speech. The meaning is: "they say to their protectors: we only worship you so that you may bring us near to Allah". And on this meaning they say "ما نَعْبُدُهُمْ", that is, they say to whoever says to them "why have you worshipped them?": "We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah (زُلْفى)", that is, in nearness.
Then He, Mighty and Majestic, made known that He does not guide these people, saying: ﴿إنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَن هو كاذِبٌ كَفّارٌ﴾ [al-Zumar: 3].

zajjaj:4-4.t: Then He, Majestic and Mighty, made known that He, Exalted is He, is far above this description, saying: ﴿لَوْ أرادَ اللَّهُ أنْ يَتَّخِذَ ولَدًا لاصْطَفى مِمّا يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ سُبْحانَهُ﴾, that is: "declaring Him free (tanzīh) of that". ﴿هُوَ اللَّهُ الواحِدُ القَهّارُ﴾. In this there is evidence that among those who took protectors besides Him are included those who said "Jesus is the son of Allah" — Allah is far exalted and mighty above that — and those who said "ʿUzayr is the son of Allah".

zajjaj:6-6.t:
Then He, Majestic and Mighty, made clear what indicates His oneness through what He created and what created beings are incapable of, saying: ﴿خَلَقَكم مِن نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنها زَوْجَها﴾. "ثُمَّ" is only for one thing after another. By "اَلنَّفْسُ الواحِدَةُ" (the single soul) He means Adam ﷺ, and "زَوْجُها" (its mate) is Eve. His saying "ثُمَّ" is only for the meaning of "He created you from a single soul", that is, He created it single, then made from it its mate; that is, He created it, then made from it its mate before you.
And His saying: ﴿وَأنْـزَلَ لَكم مِنَ الأنْعامِ ثَمانِيَةَ أزْواجٍ﴾: He means of camels a male and a female, of cattle a male and a female, of sheep likewise, and of goats a male and a female. The male and the female are called "a pair (زَوْجانِ)", and each one of them is called "زَوْجٌ".
﴿يَخْلُقُكم في بُطُونِ أُمَّهاتِكم خَلْقًا مِن بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ في ظُلُماتٍ ثَلاثٍ﴾: as drops of sperm, then clinging clots, then lumps of flesh, then bones; then the bones are clothed with flesh, then it is given form and the spirit is breathed into it. That is the meaning of His saying ﴿خَلْقًا مِن بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ في ظُلُماتٍ ثَلاثٍ﴾: in the belly, the womb and the placenta; and it has also been said: in the loins, the womb and the belly.
﴿ذَلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكم لَهُ المُلْكُ لا إلَهَ إلا هُوَ﴾: the meaning is: the One who has arranged creation in this arrangement, there is nothing like Him. ﴿فَأنّى تُصْرَفُونَ﴾: the meaning is "so from where are you turned away from the path of truth?!", like ﴿فَأنّى تُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ [Ghāfir: 62], that is: so how do you deviate from the truth after this clarification which indicates the soundness of tawḥīd?!

zajjaj:7-7.t:
﴿وَإنْ تَشْكُرُوا يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ﴾: its meaning is: He is pleased with the gratitude, because His saying "وَإنْ تَشْكُرُوا" indicates gratitude [and the pronoun refers to it].
And His saying: ﴿وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى﴾: no one is taken to task for the sin of another.

zajjaj:8-8.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿مُنِيبًا إلَيْهِ﴾, that is: turning to Him in repentance. ﴿ثُمَّ إذا خَوَّلَهُ نِعْمَةً مِنهُ﴾, that is: He removed the harm from him and bestowed favour upon him. ﴿نَسِيَ ما كانَ يَدْعُو إلَيْهِ مِن قَبْلُ﴾: He is saying: he forgot the supplication with which he used to implore Allah, Majestic and Mighty. It is possible that its meaning is: he forgot Allah, whom he used to implore before. Like it is: ﴿وَلا أنا عابِدٌ ما عَبَدْتُمْ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 4] ﴿وَلا أنْتُمْ عابِدُونَ ما أعْبُدُ﴾ [al-Kāfirūn: 5], where "ما" refers to Allah. "مَن" expresses every rational being, while "ما" can be for every kind: you say "what do you have? (ما عِنْدَكَ؟)" and the answer can be "a man", or "a horse", or whatever genus you wish; so the rational being enters into "ما" by way of its applying to genera.
﴿قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلا﴾: the wording of this is the wording of a command, but its meaning is threat and warning. Like it is: ﴿فَتَمَتَّعُوا فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 34], and like it: ﴿فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]; and like it is one's saying to someone he is threatening: "Go back to what I hate, and that will be enough for you (عُدْ لِما أكْرَهُ وحَسْبُكَ)" — you are not in reality commanding him; you are only warning and threatening him.

zajjaj:10-10.t:
﴿لِلَّذِينَ أحْسَنُوا في هَذِهِ الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةٌ وأرْضُ اللَّهِ واسِعَةٌ﴾: He mentioned the vastness of the earth here [with respect to] those who used to worship idols, and He commanded us to emigrate from a land in which one is forced to worship them, as He said: ﴿ألَمْ تَكُنْ أرْضُ اللَّهِ واسِعَةً فَتُهاجِرُوا فِيها﴾ [al-Nisāʾ: 97]. Mention of the idols has already occurred in His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أنْدادًا لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 8].
﴿إنَّما يُوَفّى الصّابِرُونَ أجْرَهم بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ﴾, that is: whoever is patient under affliction in obedience to Allah is given his reward without reckoning. It has come in the exegesis: without a measure and without a scale; it is scooped out for him in scoops. And this, even though measure and weight do not apply to any part of the reward — the delight, joy and ease in which a person takes pleasure — [is said] because what is known by the sense of the heart is represented by what is perceived by sight, so that the extent of scarcity is distinguished from abundance.

zajjaj:11-11.t: And His saying: ﴿قُلْ إنِّي أُمِرْتُ أنْ أعْبُدَ اللَّهَ﴾: He is saying: I have been commanded to affirm the oneness of Allah — and all of creation has been commanded that — and not to take any protector besides Him nor set up rivals to Him.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
And His saying: ﴿فاعْبُدُوا ما شِئْتُمْ مِن دُونِهِ﴾: this is by way of threat, as we said, like His saying: ﴿قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلا﴾ [al-Zumar: 8]. This indicates — and Allah knows best — that it was before the Muslims were commanded to fight; and it is like ﴿فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]. He has made clear the share of the believers in abundant reward and the share of the disbelievers in great punishment.
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿قُلْ إنَّ الخاسِرِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أنْفُسَهم وأهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾: by this He means the disbelievers, for they have lost themselves by being made to abide forever in the Fire, and they have lost their families because they did not enter where the believers enter, who have families in Paradise. Then He made clear their state, saying: ﴿ألا ذَلِكَ هو الخُسْرانُ المُبِينُ﴾.

zajjaj:16-16.t:
﴿لَهم مِن فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ﴾, to the end of the verse: this is like His saying: ﴿يَوْمَ يَغْشاهُمُ العَذابُ مِن فَوْقِهِمْ﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 55]. ﴿ذَلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ اللَّهُ بِهِ عِبادَهُ﴾, that is: that which has been described of the punishment, and what He has prepared for the people of misguidance, is what Allah frightens His servants with.
﴿يا عِبادِ فاتَّقُونِ﴾: the reading is with the yāʾ omitted, and this is the preferred choice among the scholars of Arabic. "يا عِبادِي" and "يا عِبادِيَ" are also permissible, but the omission is better, and the reading follows it.

zajjaj:17-17.t:
And His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطّاغُوتَ أنْ يَعْبُدُوها﴾, that is: those who avoid following the devils. ﴿وَأنابُوا إلى اللَّهِ لَهُمُ البُشْرى فَبَشِّرْ عِبادِ﴾ ﴿الَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ القَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أحْسَنَهُ﴾ [al-Zumar: 18], to the end of the verse.
In this there are — and Allah knows best — two aspects. One of them is that they listen to the Qur'an and other things, and follow the Qur'an. And it is possible that they listen to everything Allah has commanded and follow the best of that, such as retaliation (qiṣāṣ) and pardon: for whoever pardons and forgoes what is due to him has a greater reward than one who exacts retaliation. Like it is: ﴿وَلَمَن صَبَرَ وغَفَرَ إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمِن عَزْمِ الأُمُورِ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 43], ﴿وَلَمَنِ انْتَصَرَ بَعْدَ ظُلْمِهِ فَأُولَئِكَ ما عَلَيْهِمْ مِن سَبِيلٍ﴾ [al-Shūrā: 41].

zajjaj:19-19.t:
And His saying: ﴿أفَمَن حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ العَذابِ أفَأنْتَ تُنْقِذُ مَن في النّارِ﴾: this is one of the subtleties of Arabic. Its meaning is the meaning of condition and requital (al-sharṭ wa-l-jazāʾ). The interrogative alif here has the sense of bringing [the addressee] to acknowledge (tawqīf), and the second alif in "أفَأنْتَ تُنْقِذُ مَن في النّارِ" came as an emphasis, repeated because the speech had become long; for it is not proper in Arabic to bring an interrogative alif on the subject (ism) and another alif on the predicate (khabar). The meaning is: "Is the one against whom the word of punishment has been realised — will you then save him?! (أفَمَن حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ العَذابِ أفَأنْتَ تُنْقِذُهُ؟!)". Like it is: ﴿أيَعِدُكم أنَّكم إذا مِتُّمْ وكُنْتُمْ تُرابًا وعِظامًا أنَّكم مُخْرَجُونَ﴾ [al-Muʾminūn: 35]: He repeated "أنَّكم" a second time, and the meaning is "does he promise you that when you have died and become dust and bones you will be brought forth? (أيَعِدُكم أنَّكم إذا مِتُّمْ وكُنْتُمْ تُرابًا وعِظامًا مُخْرَجُونَ؟!)".
It may also be — and Allah knows best — on another aspect: that something has been omitted, with an indication of the omitted part in the speech, in the sense of: "Is the one against whom the word of punishment has been realised to get free of it, or escape it? Will you then save him?! (أفَمَن حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ العَذابِ يَتَخَلَّصُ مِنهُ، أوْ يِنْجُو مِنهُ، أفَأنْتَ تُنْقِذُهُ؟!)", that is: no one is able to save one whom Allah has sent astray and of whom it has preceded in His knowledge that he is among the people of the Fire.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿أمَّنْ هو قانِتٌ آناءَ اللَّيْلِ﴾: most readings have the mīm doubled, in the sense of "rather, is the one who is devoutly obedient (بَلْ أمْ مَن هو قانِتٌ)…". "اَلْقانِتُ" is the one who persists in obedience; the supplication of qunūt is supplication while standing; so the qānit is the one who stands by what is obligatory upon him of Allah's command.
It is also read "أمَن هو قانِتٌ", with the mīm undoubled, and its interpretation is: "Is the one who is devoutly obedient like this one we mentioned, of those who set up rivals to Allah?" Likewise "أمْ مَن": its meaning is "rather, is the one who is devoutly obedient like another?", that is, "is the one who obeys like the one who disobeys?"
﴿يَحْذَرُ الآخِرَةَ ويَرْجُو رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ﴾: its meaning is: he is wary of the punishment of the Hereafter. ﴿قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾, that is: the one who knows and the ignorant are not equal, and likewise the obedient and the disobedient are not equal. "أُولُو الألْبابِ" are those possessed of intellects; the singular of "الألْبابِ" is "لُبٌّ", and they are the intellects.

zajjaj:21-21.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ أنَّ اللَّهَ أنْـزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنابِيعَ في الأرْضِ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that all [the water] in the earth has its origin from the sky. The meaning of "يَنابِيعَ" is the places from which water springs. The singular of "اَلْيَنابِيعُ" is "يَنْبُوعٌ", and you analyse it as [the pattern] "يَفْعُولٌ", from "نَبَعَ، يَنْبُعُ".
﴿لَكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهم لَهم غُرَفٌ مِن فَوْقِها غُرَفٌ﴾ [al-Zumar: 20]: lofty dwellings in Paradise, and above them dwellings loftier still. ﴿وَعْدَ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 20]: the reading is the accusative, and "وَعْدُ اللَّهِ" [nominative] is permissible. Whoever reads it in the accusative — and that is the reading — does so in the sense of "they have chambers, because what is meant is: Allah has promised them chambers, a promise (لَهم غُرَفٌ لِأنَّ المُرادَ وعَدَهُمُ اللَّهُ غُرَفًا وعْدًا)"; so "وَعْدُ اللَّهِ" is accusative as a maṣdar [i.e. a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)]. Whoever reads it in the nominative, the meaning is "that is Allah's promise (ذَلِكَ وعْدُ اللَّهِ)".
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعًا مُخْتَلِفًا ألْوانُهُ﴾: "ألْوانُهُ" (its colours) are green, yellow, red, white and others. ﴿ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ﴾: al-Aṣmaʿī said: it is said of a plant when its drying is complete: "قَدْ هاجَ، يَهِيجُ، هَيْجًا" (it has withered).
﴿ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطامًا﴾: "اَلْحُطامُ" is what has crumbled and broken of plants and other things; like "اَلْحُطامُ" are "اَلرُّفاتُ" and "اَلدَّرِينُ". ﴿إنَّ في ذَلِكَ لَذِكْرى لأُولِي الألْبابِ﴾, that is: [an occasion for] reflection for those possessed of intellects, so they bring to mind what there is for them in this of evidence for the oneness of Allah, Majestic and Mighty.

zajjaj:22-22.t:
﴿أفَمَن شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلإسْلامِ فَهو عَلى نُورٍ مِن رَبِّهِ﴾: this fāʾ is the fāʾ of requital (al-mujāzāt). The meaning is: "Is the one whose breast Allah has opened, so that he is guided, like the one upon whose heart He has set a seal, so that he is not guided because of its hardness?! (أفَمَن شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ فاهْتَدى، كَمَن طَبَعَ عَلى قَلْبِهِ فَلَمْ يَهْتَدِ لِقَسْوَتِهِ؟!)". The answer is left unexpressed because the speech indicates it, and His saying, Majestic and Mighty, confirms that: ﴿فَوَيْلٌ لِلْقاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهم مِن ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾.
One says: "قَسا قَلْبُهُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ، ومِن ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ" (his heart hardened away from / because of the remembrance of Allah). Whoever says "مِن ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ", the meaning is: "whenever the remembrance of Allah is recited to him, his heart hardens", as He said: ﴿وَأمّا الَّذِينَ في قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ فَزادَتْهم رِجْسًا إلى رِجْسِهِمْ﴾ [al-Tawba: 125]. Whoever says "عَنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ", the meaning is that his heart became coarse and turned away from accepting the remembrance of Allah. ﴿أُولَئِكَ في ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ﴾: He means those whose hearts are hardened, to the end of the verse.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
