And His saying: ﴿اللَّهُ نَـزَّلَ أحْسَنَ الحَدِيثِ كِتابًا مُتَشابِهًا﴾: He means the Qur'an. The meaning of "مُتَشابِهًا" is: its parts resemble one another in excellence and wisdom; there is no contradiction in it. "كِتابًا" is accusative as a badal (substitute) for "أحْسَنَ الحَدِيثِ".
And His saying: ﴿مَثانِيَ﴾ is a qualifier of His saying "كِتابًا", accusative as a naʿt (adjective). "مَثانِيَ" is a diptote, for the reason we have explained: that it is a plural that does not follow the pattern of the singular.
﴿تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنهُ جُلُودُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ﴾: He is saying: when the verses of punishment are mentioned, the skins of those humble before Allah shiver. ﴿ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهم وقُلُوبُهم إلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ﴾: when the verses of mercy are mentioned, their skins and their hearts soften. ﴿ذَلِكَ هُدى اللَّهِ يَهْدِي بِهِ مَن يَشاءُ﴾: He is saying: "what Allah has granted them of reverence for Him, fear of His punishment and hope for His mercy is the guidance of Allah."

zajjaj:24-24.t: ﴿أفَمَن يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوءَ العَذابِ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾: this is one of those whose answer is omitted; the meaning is "[is he] like one who enters Paradise? (كَمَن يَدْخُلُ الجَنَّةَ)". It has come in the exegesis that the disbeliever will be thrown into the Fire shackled, unable to shield himself from the Fire except with his face.

zajjaj:27-27.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنا لِلنّاسِ﴾, up to His saying: ﴿عَرَبِيًّا غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ﴾ [al-Zumar: 28]: "عَرَبِيًّا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is "We have set forth for people in this Qur'an, in the state of its being Arabic and clear". He mentioned "قُرْآنًا" for emphasis (tawkīd), just as you say "جاءَنِي زَيْدٌ رَجُلًا صالِحًا" (Zayd came to me, a righteous man) and "جاءَنِي عَمْرٌو إنْسانًا عاقِلًا" (ʿAmr came to me, an intelligent person), mentioning "رَجُلًا" and "إنْسانًا" for emphasis.

zajjaj:29-29.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty: ﴿ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلا رَجُلا فِيهِ شُرَكاءُ مُتَشاكِسُونَ ورَجُلا سَلَمًا لِرَجُلٍ﴾: it is also read "سالِمًا" and "سِلْمًا". "سالِمًا" is in the sense of the active participle: "سَلِمَ، فَهو سالِمٌ".
"سَلَمٌ" and "سِلْمٌ" are two maṣdars (verbal nouns) used as descriptions, in the sense of "and a man possessed of exclusive belonging (وَرَجُلًا ذا سَلَمٍ)". Like it, among maṣdars that come on the patterns "فِعْلٌ" and "فَعَلٌ", is their saying "رَبِحْتُ رِبْحًا، ورَبَحًا" (I made a profit). The poet said:
؎إذا الحَسْناءُ لَمْ تَرْحَضْ يَدَيْها ∗∗∗ ولَمْ يُقْصَرْ لَها بَصَرٌ بِسِتْرِ
؎قَرَوْا أضْيافَهم رَبَحًا بِبُحٍّ ∗∗∗ يَعِيشُ بِفَضْلِهِنَّ المَشُّ سُمْرِ
(When the fair lady does not wash her hands [for want of food to prepare], and no screen keeps her gaze confined, they hosted their guests with a profit [won] by hoarse-sounding [gaming arrows], brown ones, by whose bounty the needy live.)
That is: they hosted their guests by slaughtering [what they won with] the arrows they cast in maysir (the game of chance) «[Translator's note: the source literally says «بِذَبْحِ القِداحِ», "by slaughtering the arrows"; the bracketed words are added for sense.]».
The interpretation of this parable is that it was set forth for one who affirms the oneness of Allah and for one who ascribes a partner to Him. The one who affirms the oneness of Allah is like the one belonging wholly to one man, whom no one else shares in; and the one who worships other than Allah is like the one owned by quarrelling partners. "اَلشُّرَكاءُ المُتَشاكِسُونَ" are those who are at odds and difficult, who do not agree.
And His saying: ﴿هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ مَثَلا﴾, that is: is the likeness of the one who affirms Allah's oneness equal to the likeness of the one who associates partners?

zajjaj:31-31.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿ثُمَّ إنَّكم يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ عِنْدَ رَبِّكم تَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾: the believer and the disbeliever will dispute, and the wronged will dispute with the wrongdoer.

zajjaj:32-32.t: ﴿فَمَن أظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَذَبَ عَلى اللَّهِ وكَذَّبَ بِالصِّدْقِ إذْ جاءَهُ﴾: the meaning is: "who is more unjust than one who lies against Allah and denies His Prophet ﷺ?"

zajjaj:33-33.t:
﴿والَّذِي جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وصَدَّقَ بِهِ﴾, to the end of the verse: it is narrated from ʿAlī, may Allah have mercy on him, that he said: "The one who brought the truth is Muhammad ﷺ, and the one who affirmed it is Abū Bakr, may Allah have mercy on him." It is narrated that the one who brought the truth is Gabriel and the one who affirmed it is Muhammad, may Allah bless them both. And it is narrated that the one who brought the truth is Muhammad ﷺ, and those who affirmed it are the believers. All of these aspects are sound.
What has come in the reading (ḥarf) of Ibn Masʿūd is "والَّذِينَ جاؤُوا بِالصِّدْقِ وصَدَّقُوا بِهِ" (and those who brought the truth and affirmed it). "اَلَّذِينَ" here and "اَلَّذِي" have one meaning; its being singular — because it is not specific (ghayr muwaqqat) — is permissible, and it is equivalent to your saying "whoever brought the truth and affirmed it (مَن جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وصَدَّقَ بِهِ)", ﴿أُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُتَّقُونَ﴾. "اَلَّذِي" here is for the genus; the meaning is "and the party (al-qabīl) that brought the truth", and His saying "أُولَئِكَ هُمُ المُتَّقُونَ" indicates the meaning of a plurality. Like it in poetry is:
؎إنَّ الَّذِي حانَتْ بِفَلْجٍ دِماؤُهم ∗∗∗ هُمُ القَوْمُ كُلُّ القَوْمِ يا أُمَّ خالِدِ
(Those whose blood was spilt at Falj — they are the people, the people indeed, O Umm Khālid.)

zajjaj:36-36.t:
﴿ألَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ﴾: it is also read "عِبادَهُ" (His servants). Had it been read "كافِي عَبْدِهِ" and "كافِي عِبادِهِ" [in genitive construct], it would be permissible; but reading is an established practice (sunna) that is not to be contravened. The meaning of "بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ" indicates help to victory, and that it is like His saying: ﴿لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ﴾ [al-Tawba: 33]; and it is like ﴿إنّا كَفَيْناكَ المُسْتَهْزِئِينَ﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 95].
﴿وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِالَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِ﴾, that is: they frighten [you] with their gods and their idols. It is narrated «that the Prophet ﷺ sent Khālid ibn al-Walīd to al-ʿUzzā to break it. When Khālid came, its custodian said to him: I warn you against her, O Khālid; she has a ferocity that nothing can withstand. So Khālid went straight to al-ʿUzzā and smashed its nose.» This is the meaning of "وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِالَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِ", because their frightening Khālid is their frightening the Prophet ﷺ, since he was the one who sent him.
Then He made known that, despite their worshipping al-ʿUzzā and the idols, they acknowledge that Allah is their Creator, saying: ﴿وَلَئِنْ سَألْتَهم مَن خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ قُلْ أفَرَأيْتُمْ ما تَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 38], up to His saying: ﴿هَلْ هُنَّ مُمْسِكاتُ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 38]. It is also read "كاشِفاتُ ضُرِّهِ", without tanwīn and with the genitive in "ضُرِّهِ" and "رَحْمَتِهِ". Whoever reads with tanwīn does so because it has not [yet] occurred, in the sense of "can they remove His harm or withhold His mercy?!" «[Translator's note: i.e. the participle with tanwīn refers to what has not yet happened and so operates like the imperfect verb.]» Whoever puts it in genitive construct and in the genitive does so for lightness (istikhfāf), dropping the tanwīn. Both ways are good, and it has been read in both.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
﴿قُلْ يا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ﴾, and "عَلى مَكاناتِكم": this wording is a command in the sense of warning and threat, after they had been informed of what they must act upon; then it was said to them: ﴿فَمَن شاءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن ومَن شاءَ فَلْيَكْفُرْ﴾ [al-Kahf: 29]. This is speech that people use in threatening and warning; you say: "Whenever you wrong so-and-so, I will take revenge on you, and whenever you treat him well, I will treat you well; so do what you like, and choose for yourself." So the servants were addressed according to the measure of their own ways of speaking and their knowledge.
His saying "عَلى مَكاناتِكم" and "مَكانَتِكم" means: according to your side that you have chosen, and your direction in the knowledge of which you consider yourselves firmly established. ﴿إنِّي عامِلٌ﴾: He did not say "according to my direction (عَلى جِهَتِي)", because there is an indication of that in the speech.

zajjaj:41-41.t:
﴿وَما أنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِوَكِيلٍ﴾, that is: "you are not a guardian over them (ما أنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِحَفِيظٍ)". Then He told that He is the Guardian over them, the All-Powerful, saying: ﴿اللَّهُ يَتَوَفّى الأنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِها والَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ في مَنامِها﴾ [al-Zumar: 42], that is: and He takes the souls that have not died in their sleep.
So the dead one, taken in the taking of death, is the one which has been left by the soul (nafs) by which there is life and movement, and the soul by which it discerns; while what is taken in sleep is the soul of discernment (nafs al-tamyīz), not the soul of life, because when the soul of life departs, the breath (nafas) departs with it, whereas the sleeper breathes. This is the difference between the taking of the sleeper's soul in sleep and [the soul of] the living «[Translator's note: the source reads «ونَفْسِ الحَيِّ», "and the soul of the living".]».

zajjaj:45-45.t: ﴿وَإذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وحْدَهُ اشْمَأزَّتْ﴾, to the end of the verse: they — I mean the polytheists — when Allah was mentioned and it was said "there is no god but Allah (لا إلَهَ إلّا اللَّهُ)", recoiled from this, because they used to say: al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā and these idols are gods.

zajjaj:49-49.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿فَإذا مَسَّ الإنْسانَ ضُرٌّ دَعانا﴾, to the end of the verse. "ثُمَّ إذا خَوَّلْناهُ": [when] We give him that as a favour; everyone who gives without requital has "خَوَّلَ" (bestowed). ﴿قالَ إنَّما أُوتِيتُهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ﴾, that is: I was given it on account of an honour and merit for which this that I have been given is due to him; for I knew that I would be given guidance «[Translator's note: so the source, «هُدًى»; the sense of the context suggests «هَذا», "this".]». So Allah made known that He may give as a test and a trial, saying: ﴿بَلْ هي فِتْنَةٌ﴾, that is: that gift is a trial from Allah, an affliction with which the servant is tried, so that he may be grateful or ungrateful.

zajjaj:50-50.t: ﴿قَدْ قالَها الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ فَما أغْنى عَنْهم ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ﴾: He is saying: so their deeds were made void.

zajjaj:51-51.t: ﴿فَأصابَهم سَيِّئاتُ ما كَسَبُوا والَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِن هَؤُلاءِ سَيُصِيبُهم سَيِّئاتُ ما كَسَبُوا وما هم بِمُعْجِزِينَ﴾, that is: their return is to Allah, and He will recompense them for their deeds.

zajjaj:53-53.t: ﴿قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أسْرَفُوا عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ﴾: the meaning of "لا تَقْنَطُوا" is "do not despair". It has come in the exegesis that some people of Mecca said: Muhammad says, "Whoever has worshipped idols, taken another god alongside Allah and killed a soul will not be forgiven." So Allah made known that whoever repents and believes, Allah forgives him every sin, and He said: ﴿لا تَقْنَطُوا مِن رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ إنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعًا﴾.

zajjaj:54-54.t: And He said: ﴿وَأنِيبُوا إلى رَبِّكُمْ﴾, that is: "repent". It has been said that it was revealed about some people who were persecuted for their religion and tortured in Mecca, and who turned back from Islam; it was said: these will not be forgiven after their turning back from Islam. So Allah made known that if they repent and become Muslim, He will forgive them.

zajjaj:55-55.t:
﴿واتَّبِعُوا أحْسَنَ ما أُنْـزِلَ إلَيْكم مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾: He means the Qur'an, and the evidence for it is: ﴿اللَّهُ نَـزَّلَ أحْسَنَ الحَدِيثِ كِتابًا مُتَشابِهًا﴾ [al-Zumar: 23].
And His saying: ﴿مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ العَذابُ بَغْتَةً وأنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ﴾: "بِغْتَةً" means suddenly.

zajjaj:56-56.t:
﴿أنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يا حَسْرَتا عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ في جَنْبِ اللَّهِ﴾, that is: "O remorse!" The particle of the vocative indicates how firmly the matter has taken hold of the one concerned: when someone says "يا حَسْرَتاهُ" (O my regret!) and "يا ويْلاهُ" (O my woe!), its interpretation is "regret and woe have befallen him, and they cling to him without leaving". "يا حَسْرَتِي" is also permissible.
Al-Farrāʾ claimed that it is permissible to say "يا حَسْرَتاهُ عَلى كَذا وكَذا" with fatḥa on the hāʾ, and "يا حَسْرَتاهُ" with kasra and with ḍamma [on the hāʾ, in continuous speech]; whereas all the grammarians agree in not permitting this hāʾ to be kept in continuous speech (waṣl). He claimed that a man of Banū Asad, of Banū Faqʿas, recited to him:
؎يا رَبُّ يا رَبّاهُ إيّاكَ أسَلْ ∗∗∗ عَفْراءَ يا رَبّاهُ مِن قَبْلِ الأجَلْ
(O Lord, O my Lord, of You I ask for ʿAfrāʾ, O my Lord, before the appointed end.)
And he also recited:
؎يا مَرْحَباهِ بِحَمّارِ ناجِيَةٍ
(O welcome to the donkey-driver of Nājiya!)
What I know is that the Kufans recite it:
؎يا مَرْحَباهُ بِجَمّارِ ناجِيَةٍ
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: I do not know why he adduced this as evidence, since it has never been read so, and it is of no use at all in the interpretation of this verse; and it is an error.
The meaning of "أنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ" is "for fear that a soul should say (خَوْفَ أنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ)" and "out of aversion that a soul should say (كَراهَةَ أنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ)"; the meaning is: "follow the best of what has been sent down, for fear that you should come to a state in which this saying is said, which is the state of remorse". The meaning of "عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ في جَنْبِ اللَّهِ" is "in the matter of Allah", that is: "I neglected the path which is the path of Allah to which He called me, which is affirming His oneness and acknowledging the prophethood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ".
﴿وَإنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنَ السّاخِرِينَ﴾, that is: "and I was nothing but one of the mockers (وَما كُنْتُ إلّا مِنَ المُسْتَهْزِئِينَ)".

zajjaj:57-57.t: ﴿أوْ تَقُولَ لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي﴾, up to His saying: ﴿فَأكُونَ مِنَ المُحْسِنِينَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 58], that is: and out of aversion that you should say this saying, which leads to the like of this state in which a person is in this world; because Allah has made clear the paths of guidance, and the living person, in his intention, is in the position of one who has [already] been resurrected «[Translator's note: so the source; the sentence is obscure.]», because Allah created him from a drop of sperm and brought him to the point of discernment, so the proof stands against him.

zajjaj:59-59.t:
And His saying: ﴿بَلى﴾ is the answer to a negation, though there is no negating word in the speech. The meaning of "لَوْ أنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي" and ﴿لَوْ أنَّ لِي كَرَّةً﴾ [al-Zumar: 58] is as though it was said "I was not guided (ما هُدِيتُ)", so it was said: ﴿بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكَ آياتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِها واسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَوْ رُدُّوا لَعادُوا لِما نُهُوا عَنْهُ وإنَّهم لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 28], that is, where they said: ﴿يا لَيْتَنا نُرَدُّ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 27], to the end of the verse.
It has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ with kasra on the kāf: "بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكِ آياتِي" (feminine "you"), as an answer matching the word "نَفْس" (soul, grammatically feminine), as He said: ﴿أنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ﴾ [al-Zumar: 56]. When He says "بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكَ آياتِي" with fatḥa, it is because "nafs" applies to male and female, so the males were addressed. Like "قَدْ جاءَتْكِ آياتِي", in addressing it in the feminine, is: ﴿يا أيَّتُها النَّفْسُ المُطْمَئِنَّةُ﴾ [al-Fajr: 27] ﴿ارْجِعِي إلى رَبِّكِ راضِيَةً مَرْضِيَّةً﴾ [al-Fajr: 28].

zajjaj:60-60.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَيَوْمَ القِيامَةِ تَرى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ﴾: the reading has "وُجُوهُهم مُسْوَدَّةٌ" in the nominative, as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). "وُجُوهَهم مُسْوَدَّةً" [accusative] is also permissible, as a badal (substitute) from "اَلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا" «[Translator's note: so the source; the verse has «الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا».]»; the meaning [then] is: "and on the Day of Resurrection you will see the faces of those who lied against Allah blackened". The nominative is more common, and the readers follow it. Like the accusative is the saying of ʿAdī ibn Zayd:
؎دَعِينِي إنَّ أمْرَكِ لَنْ يُطاعا ∗∗∗ وما ألْفَيْتِنِي حِلْمِي مُضاعا
(Leave me — your command will not be obeyed; and you have not found me, my forbearance squandered.)

zajjaj:61-61.t:
﴿بِمَفازَتِهِمْ﴾ and "بِمَفازاتِهِمْ": both are read.
﴿لَهُ مَقالِيدُ السَّماواتِ والأرْضِ﴾ [al-Zumar: 63], that is: the keys of the heavens. The meaning is: whatever thing there is of the heavens and the earth, Allah is its Creator and the Opener of its door. ﴿والَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الخاسِرُونَ﴾ [al-Zumar: 63], that is: those who say that something is not among what Allah has created or provided from the heavens and the earth, so that Allah is not its Creator — those are the losers.

zajjaj:64-64.t: Then Allah, Majestic and Mighty, made known that only the Creator should be worshipped, alone, without partner, and He said: say to them after this clarification: ﴿قُلْ أفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَأْمُرُونِّي أعْبُدُ أيُّها الجاهِلُونَ﴾. "أفَغَيْرَ" is accusative by "أعْبُدُ", not by His saying "تَأْمُرُونِّي"; the meaning is: "Is it other than Allah that I should worship, O ignorant ones, in what you command me?! (أفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ أعْبُدُ أيُّها الجاهِلُونَ فِيما تَأْمُرُونَنِي؟!)".

zajjaj:66-66.t: ﴿بَلِ اللَّهَ فاعْبُدْ﴾: the word "اَللَّهَ", Majestic and Mighty, is made accusative by His saying "فاعْبُدْ", and this is agreed upon in the view of the Basrans and the Kufans. The fāʾ came in the sense of requital (mujāzāt), as though He said: "it has become clear to you, so worship Allah (قَدْ تَبَيَّنْتَ فاعْبُدِ اللَّهَ)".

zajjaj:67-67.t:
﴿وَما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾: it is also read "قَدَرِهِ", with fatḥa on the dāl. It has come in the exegesis: "they did not magnify Him as His greatness deserves". "اَلْقَدْرُ" and "اَلْقَدَرُ" here have one meaning.
﴿والأرْضُ جَمِيعًا قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ﴾: "جَمِيعًا" is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the meaning is: "and the earth, when it is gathered together, is in His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are folded in His right hand". Most readings have "مَطْوِيّاتٌ" in the nominative, as mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate). It has also been read "والسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيّاتٍ", with kasra on the tāʾ, in the sense of "and the earth altogether and the heavens are His grasp on the Day of Resurrection, folded (والأرْضُ جَمِيعًا، والسَّماواتُ قَبْضَتَهُ يَوْمَ القِيامَةِ ومَطْوِيّاتٍ)", [مَطْوِيّاتٍ being] accusative as a ḥāl.
Some grammarians permitted "قَبْضَتَهُ" with the tāʾ in the accusative. This has not been read, and the Basran grammarians do not permit it: they do not say "زَيْدٌ قَبْضَتَكَ" or "اَلْمالُ قَبْضَتَكَ" in the sense of "in your grasp (في قَبْضَتِكَ)"; if this were permissible, then "زَيْدٌ دارَكَ" would be permissible, meaning "Zayd is in your house (زَيْدٌ في دارِكَ)".

zajjaj:68-68.t:
﴿وَنُفِخَ في الصُّورِ﴾ — we have explained it — ﴿فَصَعِقَ﴾, that is: died, ﴿مَن في السَّماواتِ ومَن في الأرْضِ﴾. It has come in the exegesis that it [al-ṣūr] is the horn into which Isrāfīl blows; some of the people of the language said: it is the plural of "صُورَةٌ" (form).
﴿إلا مَن شاءَ اللَّهُ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that this exception applies to Gabriel, Michael and the Angel of Death; and it has come that the exception applies to the bearers of the Throne.

zajjaj:69-69.t:
﴿وَأشْرَقَتِ الأرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّها﴾: its meaning is: when Allah willed the reckoning and the recompense, the earth shone.
In the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ, it was said to him: «"Shall we see our Lord, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Do you suffer harm (تُضارُونَ) in seeing the sun and the moon when there are no clouds?" They said: "No." He said: "Then you will not suffer harm in seeing Him."»
And it has come in the ḥadīth: «"You will not be wronged (لا تُضامُونَ) in seeing Him."» What has come in the ḥadīth is the undoubled form of "تُضارُّونَ" and "تُضامُّونَ", and it has a good aspect in Arabic. This is a place whose explanation needs to be pursued exhaustively, because it is a fundamental of the Sunna and the Community (al-sunna wa-l-jamāʿa). Its meaning is: "no harm (ḍayr) and no wrong (ḍaym) will befall you in seeing Him", that is: "you will see Him so that you are equal in the seeing, and none of you will wrong another or harm another".
The people of the language gave two other views. They said "لا تُضارُّونَ", with the rāʾ doubled, and "لا تُضامُّونَ", with the mīm doubled, with ḍamma on the tāʾ in "تُضامُّونَ" and "تُضارُّونَ". And some of the people of the language said — with fatḥa on the tāʾ and the rāʾ doubled — "تَضارُّونَ في رُؤْيَتِهِ" and "لا تَضامُّونَ", in the sense of "تَتَضارُّونَ" and "تَتَضامُّونَ". The explanation of this is that you will not crowd against one another, nor disagree with one another in that. One says "ضارَرْتُ الرَّجُلَ، أُضارُّهُ، مُضارَّةً، وضِرارًا" when you have opposed him. Al-Nābigha of Banū Jaʿda said:
؎وَخَصْمَيْ ضِرارٍ ذَوَيْ تُدْرَإٍ ∗∗∗ مَتى يَأْتِ سِلْمُها يَشْغَبِ
(And two opposing adversaries, possessed of force in repelling: whenever their peace comes, they stir up trouble.)
The meaning of "لا تُضامُّونَ في رُؤْيَتِهِ" is: you will not press close to one another, one saying to the other "show Him to me", as you do when looking for the new crescent moon. This is a clear explanation.
And all that has been said about this "وَأشْرَقَتِ الأرْضُ" is: it was clothed with radiance by the light of Allah.

zajjaj:73-73.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءُوها وفُتِحَتْ أبْوابُها﴾, up to His saying: ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾: people have differed about the answer (jawāb) to His saying ﴿حَتّى إذا جاءُوها﴾.
Some people said: the wāw is redundant (musqaṭa); the meaning is "until, when they came to it, its gates were opened (حَتّى إذا جاؤُوها فُتِحَتْ أبْوابُها)".
Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: I heard Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] mention that the answer is omitted, and that the meaning of "حَتّى إذا جاؤُوها… to the end of the verse" is: they attained happiness. He said: so the meaning of the answer is "until, when these things took place, they came to happiness".
Some people said: [it is] "until, when they came to it, they came to it while its gates had been opened (حَتّى إذا جاؤُوها جاؤُوها وفُتِحَتْ أبْوابُها)"; so in their view "جاؤُوها" is omitted. According to the meaning of these people's view, the coming coincided with the entering in one state; the meaning is: "until, when they came to it, their coming coincided with the opening of its gates".
Abū Isḥāq said: what I myself say — and it is the [right] view, if Allah wills — is that the meaning is: "until, when they came to it and its gates were opened, and its keepers said to them: peace be upon you, you have been good, so enter it to abide forever — they entered it (دَخَلُوها)". So the answer is "دَخَلُوها", and it was omitted because there is an indication of it in the speech.
The meaning of "طِبْتُمْ" is: "you were good in this world"; you were not foul, that is, you were not people of foul deeds.

zajjaj:74-74.t: And His saying: ﴿وَأوْرَثَنا الأرْضَ﴾: He means the land of Paradise, from which we take whatever dwellings we wish. The Arabs say of everyone who has taken a dwelling: "تَبَوَّأ فُلانٌ مَنزِلًا" (so-and-so settled in a dwelling).

zajjaj:75-75.t: ﴿وَتَرى المَلائِكَةَ حافِّينَ﴾: the meaning of "حافِّينَ" is "surrounding", and so it has come in the exegesis. ﴿وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهم بِالحَقِّ وقِيلَ الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾: so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, began the creation of things with praise and concluded it with praise. He said: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ وجَعَلَ الظُّلُماتِ والنُّورَ﴾ [al-Anʿām: 1]; and when He had made creation perish, resurrected them and judged between them, and the people of Paradise had settled in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire, He concluded with His saying: ﴿الحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ العالَمِينَ﴾.
